name: Claudia Lawrence
summary: Claudia Lawrence, a 35-year-old chef at the University of York, was last seen on March 18, 2009, walking towards her home in Heworth, York, and failed to arrive for work the next morning. North Yorkshire Police treat the case as a suspected murder. Several men were arrested in 2014 and 2015, but prosecutors found insufficient evidence and no one has been charged. She has never been found.
lastSeen: March 18, 2009, about 3:05 pm, walking towards her home on Heworth Road, York, England

sources.title: BBC News - Mother speaks out 17 years since disappearance of Claudia Lawrence in York
BBC News - What happened to Claudia?
York Press - Claudia Lawrence: Timeline of her disappearance and suspected murder
Yorkshire Post (archived) - Suspects won't be charged over Claudia Lawrence 'murder'
BBC News - Claudia Lawrence: Former gravel pits searched in missing chef case
BBC News - Claudia Lawrence: New investigation leader appointed in search for missing York chef
BBC News - Man bailed in Claudia Lawrence probe
BBC News - Claudia Lawrence: End despair of missing woman's family - police

narrative: Claudia Lawrence was a 35-year-old chef who worked at Goodricke College at the University of York and lived alone in a terraced house on Heworth Road in the Heworth area of the city. According to a BBC News account of the case, her car was in a garage at the time and she had been walking to and from work.

On Wednesday, March 18, 2009, she finished her shift and was recorded on cameras as she walked home. The BBC reports that she was last seen at about 3:05 pm walking towards her home. That evening she spoke by phone to her father, Peter, and then to her mother, Joan, with whom she discussed plans for Mother's Day. She was due to start work at 6:00 am on March 19 but did not arrive. A friend, Suzy Cooper, waited for her that evening at the Nag's Head pub near her home, could not reach her by phone, and raised the alarm the next day. Her father reported her missing on March 20.

In April 2009 North Yorkshire Police said they were treating the disappearance as a suspected murder. The York Press timeline of the case records a reward from Crimestoppers, a televised reconstruction, searches at the university and in Heslington, and the jailing in 2011 of a man who made hoax calls that had prompted one search. The inquiry was scaled down in 2010.

The force's Major Crime Unit began a review in 2013 and re-examined her house. The BBC reported that fingerprints were recovered using techniques not available in 2009. In May 2014 a 59-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder and bailed; according to the York Press he was released from bail that November. A 46-year-old man arrested in July 2014 on suspicion of perverting the course of justice was also released. In March and April 2015 four men in their fifties were arrested on suspicion of murder. On March 8, 2016, the Yorkshire Post reported, the Crown Prosecution Service advised that there was insufficient evidence against the four and that no further action should be taken. The senior detective, Dai Malyn, said the inquiry had been hampered by witnesses who refused to co-operate or were not truthful.

The investigation has been in what police call a reactive phase since 2017. Peter Lawrence, who campaigned for the Guardianship (Missing Persons) Act 2017, known as Claudia's Law, died in February 2021. In August 2021 officers began searching the former gravel pits at Sand Hutton, about eight miles from York; the BBC reported at the time that nine people had been questioned over the years and none charged.

Detective Superintendent Jon Sygrove took over as senior investigating officer in February 2025. On the 17th anniversary in March 2026, the BBC reported that police still believe Claudia Lawrence was murdered, that her body has not been found and that no charges have ever been brought.

timeline.event: Claudia Lawrence is last seen at about 3:05 pm walking towards her home on Heworth Road, York; she speaks to both parents by phone that evening.
She fails to arrive for her 6:00 am shift at the University of York.
Her father reports her missing to North Yorkshire Police.
Police announce they are treating the disappearance as a suspected murder.
Forensic officers from the force's Major Crime Unit begin a new examination of her home as part of a review.
A 59-year-old man is arrested on suspicion of murder; he is bailed and later released without charge.
Three more men are arrested on suspicion of murder, following one arrest in March 2015; all are bailed.
The Crown Prosecution Service finds insufficient evidence to charge four men; no further action is taken.
Her father, Peter Lawrence, dies without learning what happened to her.
Police begin a search of Sand Hutton gravel pits near York.
Det Supt Jon Sygrove is confirmed as the new senior investigating officer.
On the 17th anniversary police renew their appeal; no charges have been brought.

name: Olof Palme
summary: Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme was shot dead on February 28, 1986 while walking home from a cinema in Stockholm without bodyguards. Christer Pettersson was convicted in 1989 but acquitted on appeal the same year. In 2020 prosecutors closed the case naming the late Stig Engström as the suspected killer, but in December 2025 Sweden's director of public prosecutions said the evidence did not support that conclusion; the investigation remains closed and the murder unsolved.
lastSeen: February 28, 1986, Sveavägen, Stockholm, Sweden

sources.title: Assassination of Olof Palme - Wikipedia
Wikipedia - Stig Engström (suspected murderer)

narrative: On the evening of February 28, 1986, Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme and his wife Lisbet attended a screening at the Grand Cinema on Sveavägen in central Stockholm. Having dismissed his security detail earlier in the day—as was his habit, reflecting Sweden's tradition of political openness—the couple walked home alone. At approximately 11:21 p.m., a man approached from behind and shot Palme once in the back at close range with a .357 Magnum revolver. A second shot grazed Lisbet Palme's back. The killer fled up steps into the surrounding streets.

The assassination of Sweden's prime minister sent shockwaves around the world and launched one of the largest murder investigations in Scandinavian history. The initial police response was widely criticized as chaotic and slow, with roadblocks not established for hours. Over the following decades, more than 130 people confessed to or were suspected of the murder, and the case file grew to over 700,000 pages.

The most prominent early suspect was Christer Pettersson, a petty criminal and drug addict who was identified by Lisbet Palme in a controversial lineup. He was convicted in July 1989 but acquitted on appeal in November 1989 due to insufficient evidence. Pettersson died in 2004, maintaining his innocence. Numerous conspiracy theories emerged, involving the South African apartheid regime, Kurdish separatists, the Iranian government, rogue elements of Swedish intelligence, and the arms company Bofors.

In June 2020, after 34 years, chief prosecutor Krister Petersson announced that Stig Engström—a graphic designer who had been an early witness at the scene—was the likely killer. Engström had given inconsistent accounts of his movements that night and matched descriptions given by witnesses. However, Engström had died by suicide in 2000, so the case was formally closed without a conviction. Many observers remain skeptical of this conclusion.

timeline.event: Prime Minister Olof Palme is shot and killed on Sveavägen in Stockholm.
The largest murder investigation in Swedish history is launched.
Christer Pettersson is convicted of the murder.
Pettersson's conviction is overturned on appeal.
Prosecutors name Stig Engström as the killer and close the investigation.
Director of public prosecutions Lennart Guné states it was wrong to name Stig Engström as the killer for lack of evidence; the investigation is not reopened.

name: Monster of Florence Victims
summary: Sixteen people were killed in eight double shootings in the countryside around Florence, Italy, between 1968 and 1985, most of them couples in parked cars. Pietro Pacciani was convicted in 1994, acquitted on appeal in 1996 and died before a retrial. Mario Vanni and Giancarlo Lotti were definitively convicted in 2000 over four of the attacks, but the gun was never found and the case is widely regarded as unresolved.
lastSeen: Eight locations in the countryside around Florence, Italy, 1968-1985

sources.title: Il Post - La storia dei delitti del mostro di Firenze
CBS News - Newly found DNA could shed light on "Monster of Florence" serial killer cold case
L'Unione Sarda - Monster of Florence: DNA rewrites the story of the first crime
Biography.com - The true story behind Netflix's Monster of Florence
Wikipedia - Monster of Florence

narrative: The name Monster of Florence was given by the Italian press to the person or persons responsible for eight double murders committed in the countryside around Florence between 1968 and 1985. According to Il Post and Wikipedia's summary of the case, the sixteen victims were almost all couples who had parked or camped in secluded spots, and the attacks were linked by the use of the same .22 calibre pistol and the same type of Winchester ammunition. In several of the attacks the female victim was also mutilated with a knife.

The first attack took place on the night of August 21, 1968, in Signa, where Antonio Lo Bianco, 29, and Barbara Locci, 32, were shot in a car while Locci's young son Natalino slept in the back seat. Locci's husband, Stefano Mele, was convicted and sentenced to 14 years. The later attacks were: Pasquale Gentilcore and Stefania Pettini near Borgo San Lorenzo in September 1974; Giovanni Foggi and Carmela De Nuccio at Scandicci in June 1981; Stefano Baldi and Susanna Cambi at Calenzano in October 1981; Paolo Mainardi and Antonella Migliorini at Baccaiano in June 1982; German students Horst Meyer and Jens-Uwe Rüsch at Giogoli in September 1983; Claudio Stefanacci and Pia Rontini near Vicchio in July 1984; and French visitors Jean-Michel Kraveichvili and Nadine Mauriot near San Casciano in Val di Pesa in September 1985.

According to Wikipedia's account, the 1968 shooting was connected to the series in 1982, when cartridge cases from that case file were found to match the later crimes. Investigators then pursued several Sardinian acquaintances of Barbara Locci, a line of inquiry that ended in 1989 with all of those suspects formally cleared.

Attention then turned to Pietro Pacciani, a farm labourer. He was convicted at first instance in 1994 of seven of the double murders, but was acquitted on appeal in 1996. Italy's Court of Cassation ordered a new appeal trial, and Pacciani died in February 1998 before it could be held, so no final verdict was ever reached in his case. Two of his acquaintances, Mario Vanni and Giancarlo Lotti, were convicted, and their convictions became final in 2000; sources report that the final judgment covered four of the double murders, with Vanni receiving a life sentence and Lotti 26 years. A third defendant, Giovanni Faggi, was acquitted, and pharmacist Francesco Calamandrei, tried separately, was acquitted in 2008.

The convictions have been widely questioned, and many commentators regard the case as unresolved. The pistol has never been recovered. CBS News reported in August 2024 that a DNA profile recovered from a bullet connected to the 1985 attack did not match the victims or anyone convicted, and that a lawyer for victims' relatives had asked for the exhumation of Stefania Pettini. In July 2025, L'Unione Sarda reported that genetic testing had shown that Natalino Mele's biological father was Giovanni Vinci, a member of the Sardinian family examined in the 1980s, rather than Stefano Mele. No new charges have been reported.

timeline.event: Antonio Lo Bianco and Barbara Locci are shot dead in a car at Signa; Locci's young son, asleep in the back seat, survives.
Pasquale Gentilcore and Stefania Pettini are killed near Borgo San Lorenzo.
Giovanni Foggi and Carmela De Nuccio are killed at Scandicci.
Stefano Baldi and Susanna Cambi are killed at Calenzano.
Paolo Mainardi and Antonella Migliorini are shot at Baccaiano; the 1968 shooting is later linked to the series through ballistic evidence.
German students Horst Meyer and Jens-Uwe Rüsch are shot in their camper van at Giogoli.
Claudio Stefanacci and Pia Rontini are killed near Vicchio.
French visitors Jean-Michel Kraveichvili and Nadine Mauriot are killed near San Casciano in Val di Pesa, the last attack in the series.
Pietro Pacciani is convicted at first instance of seven of the double murders.
Pacciani is acquitted on appeal; the Court of Cassation later orders a new appeal trial.
Pacciani dies before the new appeal trial is held.
The convictions of Mario Vanni and Giancarlo Lotti become final.

name: Ben Needham
summary: 21-month-old British toddler Ben Needham vanished while playing near his grandparents' farmhouse on the Greek island of Kos. Despite decades of searching, he has never been found. Police believe he may have been accidentally killed by a digger operator.
lastSeen: July 24, 1991, Iraklise, Kos, Greece

sources.title: Disappearance of Ben Needham - Wikipedia

narrative: On July 24, 1991, 21-month-old Ben Needham, a British toddler, vanished while playing outside his grandparents' farmhouse in the small village of Iraklise on the Greek island of Kos. His mother Kerry had traveled to Kos with her parents, who were renovating a farmhouse they had purchased on the island. Ben was playing in the area around the property under the supervision of his grandparents when he disappeared.

The search for Ben became one of the longest-running missing child cases in British history. Kerry Needham and her family spent decades campaigning for a thorough investigation, often expressing frustration with both Greek and British authorities. Multiple theories emerged: that Ben had been abducted and sold or adopted by a Greek family, that he had wandered off and fallen into difficulties, or that he had been taken by human traffickers.

In 2012, South Yorkshire Police took over the investigation and conducted extensive inquiries in Kos, including excavating the area around the farmhouse in 2016. During this investigation, a significant line of inquiry emerged: police came to believe that Ben may have been accidentally killed by a digger operator named Konstantinos 'Dino' Barkas, who was working on the adjacent property that day. Barkas, who died of cancer in 2015, may have accidentally buried Ben under rubble without realizing what had happened.

Despite extensive excavation of the area, no remains were found. South Yorkshire Police stated in 2016 that they believed Ben had died as a result of an accident involving the digger, but they could not conclusively prove this. Kerry Needham has expressed skepticism about this theory and continues to believe her son may still be alive. The case remains officially open.

timeline.event: 21-month-old Ben Needham disappears from his grandparents' property on Kos, Greece.
Greek police begin a search of the area; Ben is not found.
South Yorkshire Police take over the investigation.
Police excavate the Kos property; believe Ben may have died in an accident with a digger.
Police announce they believe Ben died accidentally; no remains found.

name: Andrew Gosden
summary: Andrew Gosden, 14, has been missing since September 14, 2007, when he skipped school in Doncaster, withdrew about £200 and travelled alone by train to London on a one-way ticket. CCTV recorded him leaving King's Cross station at 11:25am, the last confirmed sighting. Two men arrested in 2021 were released without charge in 2023 and eliminated from the inquiry.
lastSeen: September 14, 2007, King's Cross Station, London

sources.title: Major Incident Public Portal (South Yorkshire Police) - Missing Person Appeal: Andrew Gosden
BBC News - Andrew Gosden: Two men arrested for trafficking and kidnap
BBC News - Andrew Gosden: Men released without charge in 2007 missing boy case
Missing People - Andrew Gosden
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Andrew Gosden

narrative: Andrew Gosden was 14 when he disappeared on Friday, September 14, 2007. He lived with his family in the Balby area of Doncaster, South Yorkshire. South Yorkshire Police's appeal page describes him as academically gifted with a perfect school attendance record, and notes that he is deaf in his left ear, needs strong glasses and has a distinctive double ridge on his right ear.

According to the BBC, Andrew set off that morning as if going to school, but returned home once his parents had left for work and changed out of his uniform. The police appeal says he left wearing a black Slipknot T-shirt and black jeans and carrying a messenger bag with his bank card and a PlayStation Portable. He withdrew £200 from a cash machine and bought a one-way ticket to London at Doncaster station. The BBC reports that he is believed to have turned down a return ticket even though it cost a similar amount. He left no note.

He travelled on a mid-morning service that reached London King's Cross at about 11:20am. CCTV recorded him leaving the station at 11:25am, which police describe as the last confirmed sighting. According to the police appeal, there have been no confirmed sightings since, and the reason for his journey has never been established.

The family and the charity Missing People have run repeated public appeals, and age-progressed images have been issued to show how Andrew might look as an adult. The BBC reported that the family also commissioned their own searches, including a sonar scan of the River Thames.

On December 8, 2021, South Yorkshire Police, assisted by the Metropolitan Police, arrested two men in London, aged 38 and 45, on suspicion of kidnap and human trafficking; the older man was also arrested on suspicion of possessing indecent images of children. The arrests were made public in January 2022 and were believed to be the first in the case. In September 2023 police announced that both men had been released without charge. Detective Chief Inspector Andy Knowles said the force was confident the men had played no part in the disappearance. Andrew's parents, Kevin and Glenys Gosden, said publicly that the men had no connection to their son and expressed sympathy for the distress caused to them.

Police say the investigation remains open. Wikipedia's account of the case, citing news coverage, records a further anniversary appeal in September 2025. Anyone with information is asked to contact South Yorkshire Police or Missing People.

timeline.event: Andrew leaves home as if going to school, returns after his parents leave, changes clothes and withdraws £200.
He buys a one-way ticket at Doncaster station and boards a morning train to London.
CCTV records him leaving King's Cross station at 11:25am, the last confirmed sighting.
His family report him missing that evening (per Wikipedia).
Two men, aged 38 and 45, are arrested in London on suspicion of kidnap and human trafficking.
South Yorkshire Police make the arrests public; both men have been released under investigation.
Police announce both men have been released without charge and eliminated from the inquiry.
A renewed appeal is issued on the 18th anniversary of the disappearance.

name: Lars Mittank
summary: Lars Mittank, a 28-year-old from Itzehoe, Germany, disappeared on July 8, 2014 after abruptly leaving a doctor's office at Varna Airport in Bulgaria and running from the terminal, leaving his luggage, passport and phone behind. He had stayed on alone after an ear injury kept him from flying home with friends. German police still list him as missing.
lastSeen: July 8, 2014, Varna Airport, Bulgaria

sources.title: Bundeskriminalamt (BKA) - Fahndung nach vermisstem MITTANK, Lars Joachim
Der Spiegel - Verschwunden in Bulgarien: Auf der Suche nach Lars Mittank
Mirror - Chilling mystery of the 'most famous missing person on YouTube'
MEL Magazine - The Mystery of the Most Famous Missing Person on YouTube
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Lars Mittank

narrative: Lars Joachim Mittank, born in Berlin on February 9, 1986, lived in Itzehoe in the German state of Schleswig-Holstein and worked at a power plant. According to the German Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) appeal, which is handled by the criminal police in Itzehoe, he was on holiday with friends in Varna, Bulgaria, from June 30 to July 7, 2014. The group stayed at the Golden Sands resort on the Black Sea coast.

The BKA states that during an altercation on July 5, 2014 Mittank was struck on his left ear and afterwards could barely hear on that side. Der Spiegel and later reports by the Mirror and MEL Magazine described the incident as a dispute with other football fans that left him with a ruptured eardrum. He saw a doctor on July 7, who told him not to fly. His friends returned to Germany that day as planned. According to the BKA, Mittank went to a hospital but was not treated further there. He then took a room at the Hotel Color, near the airport.

His mother, Sandra Mittank, has said in German television interviews quoted by the Mirror and MEL Magazine that he phoned her from the hotel, told her that people were trying to rob or kill him, and asked her to cancel his bank cards. He also sent her a text message asking about the antibiotic he had been prescribed. Those outlets reported that hotel cameras recorded him pacing in the lobby and that he left the building for about an hour during the night.

On the morning of July 8, 2014 Mittank went to see a doctor at Varna Airport. The BKA says that at about 10 a.m. local time he suddenly left the practice and the airport without apparent reason, leaving all his luggage and his mobile phone behind. The airport doctor, Kosta Kostov, told MEL Magazine that Mittank had seemed nervous, distrusted his medication and said he did not want to die there before running out. Security cameras recorded him leaving the terminal. Der Spiegel reported that witnesses saw him cross the car park, climb a fence and disappear into a field, and that border police searched with tracking dogs the next day without result. He did not use the flight booked for that day or an alternative bus booking, and there has been no contact with him since.

The family hired a private investigator, Andreas Gütig, and Der Spiegel reported in August 2014 that Interpol and the German Foreign Office had become involved. No explanation for his behaviour has been established. Possibilities discussed in press coverage include the effects of the head injury, a reaction to medication and an acute psychological crisis; his mother has said he had no history of mental illness, and Kostov said he did not believe Mittank had taken the antibiotic. The airport footage has been viewed millions of times online. Reported sightings have not been confirmed, and the BKA appeal, last updated in June 2024, remains active.

timeline.event: Lars Mittank arrives in Varna, Bulgaria, for a holiday with friends.
He is struck on the left ear during an altercation, according to German police.
A doctor tells him not to fly; his friends return to Germany and he checks into a hotel near the airport.
At about 10 a.m. he leaves a doctor's office at Varna Airport and runs from the terminal without his luggage, passport or phone; he has not been seen since.
Border police search the area with tracking dogs without result, according to Der Spiegel.
Der Spiegel reports that a private investigator hired by the family, Interpol and the German Foreign Office are involved in the search.
The BKA missing-person appeal for Mittank is last updated; he remains missing.

name: Richey Edwards
summary: Manic Street Preachers guitarist and lyricist Richey Edwards disappeared on the day he was due to fly to the US for a promotional tour. His car was found abandoned near the Severn Bridge. He was declared presumed dead in 2008.
lastSeen: February 1, 1995, Embassy Hotel, London, England

sources.title: Richey Edwards - Wikipedia

narrative: On February 1, 1995, Richard James 'Richey' Edwards, the 27-year-old rhythm guitarist, lyricist, and cultural icon of the Welsh rock band Manic Street Preachers, checked out of the Embassy Hotel in London where he had been staying. He was due to fly to the United States that day with bandmate James Dean Bradfield for a promotional tour. Instead of going to the airport, Edwards withdrew £200 from his bank account and drove his silver Vauxhall Cavalier away. He was never seen again.

Over the following two weeks, Edwards' car was spotted by toll booth cameras crossing the Severn Bridge—which connects England and Wales—multiple times. On February 14, his car was found abandoned at the Aust motorway services, near the bridge. The Severn Estuary below the bridge is notorious for its strong currents and has been the site of numerous suicides. However, no body was ever recovered, and Edwards' passport was missing from his flat.

Edwards had a well-documented history of depression, self-harm, anorexia, and alcohol abuse. He had been hospitalized in a psychiatric facility in 1994 and was known to have struggled profoundly with mental health issues. These factors led many to conclude he had likely taken his own life. However, others—including his family—held out hope that he may have simply walked away from fame and started a new life, pointing to the missing passport and reported sightings in locations ranging from Goa to the Canary Islands.

Richey Edwards was officially declared 'presumed dead' by his family in November 2008. The Manic Street Preachers continued as a three-piece, and in 2009 released 'Journal for Plague Lovers,' an album set to lyrics Edwards had left behind. His disappearance remains one of the most poignant mysteries in British music history.

timeline.event: Richey Edwards checks out of his London hotel and disappears.
His car is found abandoned at motorway services near the Severn Bridge.
Police search the Severn Estuary; no body is found.
Edwards is declared 'presumed dead' by his family.

name: Sneha Anne Philip
summary: Dr. Sneha Anne Philip, an internist, was last seen shopping at a store near the World Trade Center on September 10, 2001. She was never seen again. Whether she died in the 9/11 attacks or disappeared separately remains unknown.
lastSeen: September 10, 2001, Century 21 store near WTC, New York City

sources.title: Disappearance of Sneha Anne Philip - Wikipedia
9/11 victims - CNN (archived copy)
Wikipedia - Sneha Anne Philip

narrative: Sneha Anne Philip, a 31-year-old internist at St. Vincent's Hospital in Manhattan, was last confirmed seen on the afternoon of September 10, 2001, shopping at a Century 21 department store near the World Trade Center. She had been placed on leave from the hospital and was dealing with professional and personal difficulties. She did not return to the apartment she shared with her husband Ron Lieberman in Battery Park City, just blocks from the World Trade Center, that night.

The next morning, September 11, 2001, two hijacked planes struck the Twin Towers. Sneha's apartment building was within the evacuation zone, and the area was engulfed in chaos and destruction. Her husband, who was working an overnight shift, tried to reach her but could not. In the aftermath, her family reported her missing and sought to have her declared a victim of the attacks.

The question of whether Sneha Philip died in the September 11 attacks or had disappeared separately became the subject of intense legal and investigative debate. Her family argued she had likely rushed to help victims as a doctor, as St. Vincent's Hospital was a primary triage center. However, the medical examiner's office initially declined to list her as a 9/11 victim, noting she had been missing before the attacks.

A Surrogate's Court judge ruled in 2006 that her death on September 11 could not be established, but on January 31, 2008 an appeals court reversed that decision and she was officially listed as a victim of the September 11 attacks. However, no remains were ever identified as hers, and the circumstances of her disappearance the night before have never been fully explained. Some investigators believe she met with foul play on the evening of September 10, while others accept the official finding that she died on September 11.

timeline.event: Sneha Philip is last seen shopping near the World Trade Center.
The September 11 attacks destroy the World Trade Center near her home.
Her husband reports her missing after the attacks.
A judge rules she should be listed as a victim of the 9/11 attacks.
A New York appeals court reverses a 2006 ruling and declares Philip a victim of the September 11 attacks.

name: Branson Perry
summary: Twenty-year-old Branson Perry vanished from Skidmore, Missouri—the same small town where Ken McElroy was murdered in 1981—after telling a friend he was going to put jumper cables away. He was never seen again.
lastSeen: April 11, 2001, Skidmore, Missouri

sources.title: Disappearance of Branson Perry - Wikipedia
Branson Perry - Charley Project
Branson Perry disappearance - NBC News

narrative: On April 11, 2001, Branson Kayne Perry, a 20-year-old man, vanished from the tiny town of Skidmore, Missouri—population roughly 300 and already infamous as the town where bully Ken McElroy had been shot to death in broad daylight in 1981. Branson had been doing chores at his father's house when he told a friend he was going to put a pair of jumper cables away. He walked out the back door and was never seen again.

Branson's disappearance was particularly alarming because it occurred in a town where everyone knew everyone, and yet no one reported seeing anything unusual. His father Bob Perry had recently been hospitalized and was due to return home, and Branson had been helping clean the house. Investigators considered whether the disappearance was connected to people Branson knew locally, but no motive has been established.

Investigators examined Jack Wayne Rogers, a Presbyterian minister arrested in 2003 on unrelated charges, after online posts attributed to him described killing a hitchhiker resembling Branson. Rogers denied any involvement and has never been charged in connection with Branson's disappearance. No body or physical evidence linking anyone to the disappearance has been found. In 2004 Rogers was sentenced to prison for assault, performing illegal surgery and child pornography offenses unrelated to Branson's case; he remains incarcerated.

Despite searches of numerous properties in the region, including a May 2024 search of a well near Quitman, Missouri, Branson Perry's remains have never been found. The case highlighted the dark undercurrents beneath the quiet surface of small-town America and drew parallels to the McElroy murder that had taken place in the same community two decades earlier.

timeline.event: Branson Perry tells a friend he's going to put jumper cables away and disappears.
Perry is reported missing; search of the area begins.
Jack Wayne Rogers tells people he killed Perry; charged with kidnapping.
Charges against Rogers are dropped due to insufficient evidence.
Rogers dies in prison serving unrelated sentence.
The Nodaway County sheriff says a suspect has been identified but more evidence is needed before an arrest; no one has been charged.
Investigators with FBI assistance search a well near Quitman, Missouri on a tip; nothing is found.

name: Ben McDaniel
summary: Ben McDaniel, 30, of Tennessee was last seen on the evening of August 18, 2010, descending toward the underwater cave at Vortex Spring near Ponce de Leon, Florida. He was not certified for cave diving. Weeks of searches by expert cave divers found two of his tanks but no trace of him, and the Holmes County Sheriff's Office found no evidence that he resurfaced.
lastSeen: August 18, 2010, Vortex Spring, near Ponce de Leon, Holmes County, Florida

sources.title: Tampa Bay Times (archived) - When a diver goes missing, a deep cave is scene of a deeper mystery
The Commercial Appeal (archived) - Parents pull reward for missing diver
Action News 5 - Family ponders fate of Collierville man who disappeared near cave
Casefile True Crime Podcast - Casefile Archives 10: Ben McDaniel
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Ben McDaniel

narrative: Ben McDaniel, a 30-year-old from the Memphis suburb of Collierville, Tennessee, had been living at his parents' property in Santa Rosa Beach, Florida, for several months in 2010. According to the Tampa Bay Times, his parents had suggested the stay after a difficult period in which his construction business failed, his marriage ended and his younger brother Paul died in 2008. A diver since the age of 15, he became a regular at Vortex Spring, a commercial dive park north of Ponce de Leon in Holmes County.

The spring contains a cave whose deeper section lies behind a locked gate; the dive shop released the key only to divers with cave certification, which McDaniel did not hold. The Tampa Bay Times reported that on Wednesday, August 18, 2010, he made a daytime dive, spent the afternoon testing equipment and writing in his dive log, and entered the water again around dusk. Two employees, Eduardo Taran and Chuck Cronin, saw him descending toward the cave mouth with his lights on. Nobody is known to have seen him afterwards.

His pickup truck remained in the parking lot, and on Friday, August 20, Taran called the Holmes County Sheriff's Office. Deputies found McDaniel's wallet, containing about $1,100, along with a detailed dive log and a map he had drawn of the cave. Recovery divers found two decompression tanks belonging to him near the cave. Cave recovery specialist Edd Sorenson told reporters he went about 1,700 feet into the system, beyond the mapped section, and saw no scrape marks, disturbed sediment or other indication that a diver of McDaniel's size had passed through. Steve Keene, who had mapped the cave in 2003, made seven dives for the family with the same result.

According to the Tampa Bay Times, cadaver dogs reacted to the water, but about 30 water samples taken over several months showed no bacterial change consistent with decomposition, and searches of the surrounding woods and downstream waterways found nothing. Taran and Cronin both passed polygraph examinations. Capt. Harry Hamilton of the sheriff's office said monitoring of McDaniel's bank, phone and online accounts showed no activity, and that investigators had no indication he had resurfaced.

McDaniel's parents, Shelby and Patty McDaniel, offered a reward that grew from $10,000 to $30,000. The Commercial Appeal reported that they withdrew it in 2012 after diver Larry Higginbotham of Biloxi, Mississippi, drowned in the cave; his family said he had not been looking for McDaniel, though some cave divers doubted that. A search by cadaver dogs on land that year also found nothing.

Divers, investigators and the family have discussed several possibilities: that his remains lie in an unreached part of the cave, that he left voluntarily, or that he met with foul play. None has been supported by evidence, and no one has been charged with any offence. His parents have rejected the idea that he chose to disappear. Wikipedia states that Florida issued the family a death certificate in 2013. He has never been found.

timeline.event: Ben McDaniel is born in Memphis, Tennessee.
His younger brother Paul dies at age 22.
McDaniel moves to his parents' property in Santa Rosa Beach, Florida, and begins diving regularly at Vortex Spring.
Two dive shop employees see McDaniel descending toward the cave at Vortex Spring around dusk; he is not seen again.
An employee reports the unattended truck to the Holmes County Sheriff's Office; recovery divers find two of McDaniel's tanks.
Cave recovery specialist Edd Sorenson searches beyond the mapped part of the cave and finds no sign of McDaniel.
Volunteer dive searches, attended by the family, continue into the autumn without result.
Family and friends hold a benefit on what would have been his 31st birthday to fund a $10,000 reward.
Diver Larry Higginbotham drowns in the Vortex Spring cave; cadaver dogs search land near the spring without result.
McDaniel's parents withdraw the reward, by then $30,000.
Florida issues a death certificate to the family, according to Wikipedia.

name: Kara Kopetsky
summary: Kara Kopetsky, 17, disappeared after leaving Belton High School in Missouri on May 4, 2007. Her remains were found in woods in Cass County in April 2017, beside those of Jessica Runions, and were identified that August. In April 2021 a jury convicted her former boyfriend Kylr Yust of voluntary manslaughter in her death and second-degree murder in Runions' death. He is serving life plus 15 years.
lastSeen: May 4, 2007, Belton High School, Belton, Missouri (last recorded on school surveillance video that morning)

sources.title: KSHB - In-depth: Details of the case against Yust
KSHB - Cass County human remains ID'd as Kara Kopetsky
KCUR - Kylr Yust Sentenced To 45 Years In Prison For Killings Of Two Kansas City-Area Women
KY3 - Missouri Court of Appeals upholds Kylr Yust's convictions
KSHB - Kylr Yust loses appeal in attempt to overturn convictions
KCTV5 - Convicted killer asks appeals court to vacate convictions in Kopetsky, Runions murders
Bing results - KRCG "Yust gets life, plus 15 years for two murders"; FOX 2 "Kylr Yust sentenced to life and 15 years"

narrative: Kara Kopetsky was a 17-year-old junior at Belton High School in Belton, Missouri, a suburb south of Kansas City. According to a case chronology published by KSHB, she told Belton police on April 28, 2007, that her former boyfriend, Kylr Yust, had kidnapped her. A Cass County court issued an order of protection against him on April 30, and it was served on May 1.

On May 4, 2007, she left the school during the morning and was not seen again. KSHB reports that school surveillance video recorded her that morning and that she was reported missing to Belton police later the same day. Her debit card was found in her school locker on June 1, and her account showed no activity after she vanished. No charges were filed at the time and the case remained open for almost ten years.

On September 8, 2016, Jessica Runions, 21, was last seen leaving a gathering in Grandview with Yust, according to KSHB. She was reported missing the next day, and her vehicle was found burning in Kansas City early on September 10. Yust was arrested on September 11 in connection with the burning of the vehicle.

In early April 2017 a mushroom hunter found human remains in a wooded area of rural Cass County, south of Belton, and investigators located a second skull nearby the following day, KSHB reported. One set of remains was identified as Runions within days. On August 16, 2017, Belton police announced that the FBI laboratory had identified the other set as Kopetsky. Murder charges were filed against Yust on October 5, 2017.

The trial was held in Cass County in April 2021 after several delays. KCUR reported that the defence pointed to the absence of DNA evidence tying Yust to either death and that Yust testified his half-brother, who died in jail in 2018, was responsible. Prosecutors argued Yust acted out of jealousy. On April 15, 2021, the jury found him guilty of voluntary manslaughter in Kopetsky's death and second-degree murder in Runions' death. In June 2021 Judge William Collins imposed the sentences the jury recommended: 15 years and life, to run consecutively.

The Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, affirmed the convictions in August 2023, rejecting all six points raised, KY3 reported. Yust then sought post-conviction relief. According to KCTV5, his lawyers argued before a state appeals panel on September 1, 2026, that his trial counsel was ineffective and that trying the two deaths together prejudiced the jury. No ruling had been reported at the time of writing, and the convictions remain in place.

timeline.event: Kopetsky reports to Belton police that Kylr Yust kidnapped her.
A Cass County court issues an order of protection against Yust; it is served on May 1.
Kopetsky leaves Belton High School and is reported missing later that day.
Jessica Runions, 21, is last seen leaving a gathering in Grandview with Yust.
Runions' vehicle is found burning in Kansas City; Yust is arrested the next day over the burning.
A mushroom hunter finds human remains in woods in rural Cass County; a second skull is found nearby.
Belton police announce that the FBI has identified the second set of remains as Kara Kopetsky.
Murder charges are filed against Yust in both deaths.
A jury convicts Yust of voluntary manslaughter (Kopetsky) and second-degree murder (Runions).
Yust is sentenced to 15 years and life, to run consecutively.
The Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, affirms the convictions.
A state appeals panel hears argument on Yust's post-conviction claim of ineffective counsel; no ruling reported yet.

name: Kyle Fleischmann
summary: Kyle Fleischmann, 24, disappeared in the early hours of November 9, 2007, after leaving the Buckhead Saloon in uptown Charlotte, North Carolina. Surveillance video recorded him leaving the bar alone at about 2:20 a.m., and his phone was last used a little over an hour later. No trace of him has been found, and the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department lists the case as an open missing person investigation.
lastSeen: November 9, 2007, about 2:20 a.m., leaving the Buckhead Saloon, 201 E. 5th St., uptown Charlotte, North Carolina

sources.title: Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department - Missing Person: Kyle Fleischmann (flyer)
WRAL - NC Wanted: Charlotte family continues search for Kyle Fleischmann
WBTV - 10-year anniversary of Kyle Fleischmann disappearance
Creative Loafing Charlotte - MIA
NC Missing Persons (CUE Center) - Kyle Fleischmann
The Vanished Podcast - Episode 276: Kyle Fleischmann

narrative: Kyle Fleischmann was 24 when he disappeared from uptown Charlotte, North Carolina, in the early hours of November 9, 2007. According to the North Carolina missing persons listing maintained by the CUE Center for Missing Persons, he had spent the evening of November 8 at a Dane Cook comedy show at the city's arena, where members of his family were also in the audience, and afterwards went with friends to the Buckhead Saloon on East 5th Street.

The Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department's missing person flyer states that he was last seen leaving the Buckhead Saloon at 201 E. 5th St. at around 2:20 a.m., wearing a dark short-sleeved shirt and jeans. WRAL, in a 2016 report for the program NC Wanted, said the departure was recorded by surveillance video, and that video from a nearby Fuel Pizza showed him buying food at about 2:25 a.m. Creative Loafing Charlotte reported in November 2007 that he left his black peacoat and his credit cards behind at the bar; WBTV later described the item left behind as his wallet. He still had his phone.

Creative Loafing reported that he tried to call friends at 3:28 and 3:29 a.m. and that cell tower data placed at least one call near Seigle Avenue and Tenth Street, east of the city centre. The CUE Center listing says no voicemails were left, that phone activity was concentrated in the uptown and First Ward areas, and that it stopped at about 4 a.m. The Vanished podcast's case summary adds that a cab driver reported watching him walk down a street and out of view.

The search began within days. According to Creative Loafing, search dogs followed a scent on November 14 to the area of the Alpha Mills apartments on Twelfth Street, volunteers distributed fliers across the city, a Facebook group drew more than 33,000 members, and the family hired private investigators and offered a reward of up to $10,000. By 2016 WRAL reported the reward at $50,000. WRAL also quoted his father, Dick Fleischmann, as saying about four weeks after the disappearance that he had come to believe a crime had occurred. Police have not publicly named a suspect or announced evidence of what happened.

On the tenth anniversary in November 2017, WBTV reported that the case had been reviewed by private investigators, missing-person organisations and police, and that it was assigned to the department's Cold Case Unit. A police spokesperson told the station there were no new developments despite the resources devoted to the case over the decade. The station reported that the family had since moved out of state.

Local coverage of the eighteenth anniversary in November 2025 described the disappearance as still unresolved. The police flyer remains published on the City of Charlotte website, and anyone with information is asked to contact Charlotte Crime Stoppers at 704-334-1600.

timeline.event: Kyle Fleischmann is born, according to the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department flyer.
The family hires private investigators and offers a reward of up to $10,000; volunteers distribute fliers.
He attends a comedy show at the Charlotte arena, then goes to the Buckhead Saloon on East 5th Street with friends.
Surveillance video records him leaving the Buckhead Saloon alone at about 2:20 a.m.; he is recorded at a nearby Fuel Pizza at about 2:25 a.m.
He attempts phone calls to friends at about 3:28 and 3:29 a.m.; phone activity ends at about 4 a.m.
Search dogs follow a scent to the area of the Alpha Mills apartments on Twelfth Street, according to Creative Loafing.
WRAL reports the case remains unsolved with a $50,000 reward on offer.
On the tenth anniversary, police say there are no new developments; the case is with the Cold Case Unit.
Local media mark the eighteenth anniversary; he is still missing.

name: Glen & Bessie Hyde
summary: Newlyweds Glen and Bessie Hyde disappeared while attempting to run the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon on a homemade scow. Their boat was found intact but the couple was never seen again.
lastSeen: November 18, 1928, Colorado River, Grand Canyon, Arizona

sources.title: Glen and Bessie Hyde - Wikipedia

narrative: In October 1928, Glen Rollin Hyde (29) and his bride Bessie Louise Hyde (22) set out to run the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon on a homemade wooden scow—a flat-bottomed boat. If successful, Bessie would have been the first woman known to complete the journey. The couple had already navigated portions of the Snake and Salmon Rivers in Idaho and were experienced, if unconventional, river runners.

The Hydes launched from Green River, Utah on October 20 and made good progress through Glen Canyon and Marble Canyon. On November 15, they encountered Emery Kolb, the famous Grand Canyon photographer and river runner, at the South Rim. Kolb offered them life jackets, which Glen declined. He photographed the couple, and these are the last known images of them. They were last seen heading downstream on November 18.

When the Hydes failed to arrive at Needles, California as scheduled, Glen's father Rollin Hyde organized a search. On December 19, their scow was found drifting intact in calm water near Mile 237 of the Colorado River. The boat was upright, their belongings were aboard, and there was no sign of damage or capsize. Bessie's diary, containing entries up to November 30, was found, along with a camera with exposed film. But Glen and Bessie were gone.

The mystery of what happened to the Hydes has never been solved. Theories include drowning in rapids (though the boat showed no signs of capsizing), murder (possibly a domestic dispute), or an encounter with unknown persons. In 1971, a woman named Georgie White, a well-known river guide, was rumored to be Bessie Hyde living under a false identity, but this was never confirmed. No remains of either Glen or Bessie have ever been found.

timeline.event: Glen and Bessie Hyde launch their scow from Green River, Utah.
The couple is photographed by Emery Kolb at the Grand Canyon South Rim.
The Hydes are last seen heading downriver; they disappear.
Their intact, undamaged boat is found drifting with their belongings aboard.

name: Michael Rockefeller
summary: Michael Rockefeller, son of New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller, disappeared off the coast of southwestern New Guinea while on an art-collecting expedition. He likely drowned or was killed by Asmat tribesmen after swimming to shore from a capsized catamaran.
lastSeen: November 19, 1961, Arafura Sea, near Asmat region, New Guinea

sources.title: Michael Rockefeller - Wikipedia
Savage Harvest - Carl Hoffman

narrative: On November 19, 1961, Michael Clark Rockefeller, the 23-year-old son of New York Governor (and future Vice President) Nelson Rockefeller, disappeared off the coast of southwestern New Guinea (then Netherlands New Guinea) during an art-collecting expedition among the Asmat people. He had been traveling by catamaran with Dutch anthropologist René Wassing when their vessel capsized in rough seas at the mouth of the Eilanden River, approximately three miles offshore.

Wassing clung to the overturned hull and was eventually rescued by local villagers. Michael, an athletic young man who had been collecting Asmat tribal art for Harvard's Peabody Museum, decided to swim for shore. He strapped two empty gasoline cans to his body as flotation devices and set off toward the distant coast. He was never seen again.

The disappearance triggered a massive search involving the Dutch Navy, private aircraft, and local boats. Nelson Rockefeller flew to New Guinea to oversee the search personally. Despite weeks of intensive effort, no trace of Michael was found. The official conclusion was that he drowned, but persistent reports suggested a darker fate.

In his 2014 book 'Savage Harvest,' journalist Carl Hoffman presented evidence—including Dutch government documents and accounts from Asmat elders—that Michael reached shore alive but was killed and likely consumed in a ritualistic act by Asmat warriors from the village of Otsjanep. The Asmat had motive: in 1958, Dutch colonial authorities had killed several Otsjanep warriors, and the tribe's culture demanded retributive killing. The Dutch government reportedly investigated this possibility but suppressed the findings to protect diplomatic relations. No remains were ever recovered.

The catamaran capsizes; Michael swims for shore and disappears.

name: Percy Fawcett Expedition
summary: British explorer Colonel Percy Fawcett, his son Jack, and friend Raleigh Rimmell disappeared in the Brazilian Amazon while searching for a lost city Fawcett called 'Z.' Despite over 100 rescue and investigative expeditions, their fate was never determined.
lastSeen: May 29, 1925, Upper Xingu region, Mato Grosso, Brazil

sources.title: Percy Fawcett - Wikipedia
The Lost City of Z - David Grann

narrative: In April 1925, Colonel Percy Harrison Fawcett, a 57-year-old British explorer and veteran of numerous South American expeditions, set out from Cuiabá, Brazil with his 21-year-old son Jack and Jack's friend Raleigh Rimmell to search for what he called the 'Lost City of Z'—an ancient civilization he believed existed in the unexplored jungles of the Mato Grosso. The expedition was financed by a London-based group of investors and backed by the Royal Geographical Society.

Fawcett's last communication was a letter to his wife Nina, dispatched on May 29, 1925, from a point he called 'Dead Horse Camp' on the edge of unexplored territory. In it, he wrote that they were about to enter territory inhabited by indigenous groups and that their animals were failing. He instructed that no rescue expedition be sent if they did not return, as it would be too dangerous. After this letter, the three men were never heard from again.

Despite Fawcett's wishes, over 100 expeditions have ventured into the area over the following decades to search for the party or determine their fate. At least 13 people died in these rescue attempts. Various theories have been proposed: that the party was killed by hostile indigenous groups, that they succumbed to disease or starvation, or that Fawcett chose to live among the indigenous people. Several indigenous groups in the area have offered conflicting accounts, some claiming to have seen or killed the explorers.

In 1951, the Kalapalo people told Orlando Villas-Bôas that they had killed the Fawcett party, producing bones they claimed were Fawcett's, but forensic analysis determined the bones were not his. David Grann's 2009 book 'The Lost City of Z' and the 2016 film of the same name brought renewed attention to the case. Archaeologists have since confirmed that significant pre-Columbian settlements did exist in the area, suggesting Fawcett's theory about an advanced civilization was not entirely unfounded. The fate of the Fawcett expedition remains one of exploration's greatest mysteries.

timeline.event: Fawcett, his son Jack, and Raleigh Rimmell depart Cuiabá, Brazil.
Fawcett sends his last letter from 'Dead Horse Camp.'

name: Dag Hammarskjöld
summary: UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld, 56, and 15 others died when their DC-6 crashed near Ndola, Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia), shortly after midnight on September 18, 1961, as he travelled to ceasefire talks in the Congo crisis. Early inquiries pointed to pilot error or left the cause open. A UN-mandated inquiry reported in 2024 that an external attack or threat remains plausible; the cause is undetermined.
lastSeen: September 17, 1961, departing Léopoldville (now Kinshasa) on a flight to Ndola, Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia)

sources.title: UN News - Mystery still surrounds death of revered UN chief Hammarskjöld, 63 years on
United Nations - 63 years later, mystery still surrounds death of Dag Hammarskjöld
Macau Business (AFP) - UN extends investigation of leader's mysterious 1961 death
Dag Hammarskjöld Foundation - Hammarskjöld Plane Crash, Ndola 1961
Wikipedia - 1961 Ndola United Nations DC-6 crash

narrative: Dag Hammarskjöld, a Swedish diplomat, had served as Secretary-General of the United Nations since April 1953. In September 1961 he was travelling to Ndola, in what was then Northern Rhodesia, to negotiate a ceasefire between UN peacekeepers and separatist forces in the Congolese province of Katanga, according to UN News. He was flying in a chartered Douglas DC-6 registered SE-BDY, which Wikipedia's article on the crash identifies as operated by Transair Sweden.

The aircraft crashed shortly after midnight on the night of September 17-18, 1961, near Ndola. Sixteen people were on board. UN News reports that all but one died at the scene and that the single survivor died of his injuries some days later. Wikipedia names the survivor as Sergeant Harold Julien, a UN security officer, and says he died in hospital five days after the crash; it places the wreckage about 15 kilometres from Ndola airport.

According to Wikipedia, a Rhodesian Board of Investigation worked from September to November 1961 and found no evidence of a bomb or missile, concluding that the aircraft had been flown too low and struck trees. A Rhodesian Commission of Inquiry followed in January 1962, and a UN Commission of Investigation reported later in 1962 without being able to determine the cause. UN News notes that the initial Rhodesian finding of pilot error was disputed. It also summarises eyewitness accounts suggesting that more than one aircraft was in the air, that SE-BDY was on fire before it came down, or that it was fired upon.

Interest revived in the 2010s. Wikipedia reports that an unofficial commission of jurists chaired by Stephen Sedley recommended in September 2013 that the UN reopen its inquiry, and that Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon appointed an independent panel in March 2015, headed by Mohamed Chande Othman, a former Chief Justice of Tanzania. Othman has since led successive UN inquiries as 'Eminent Person'. An AFP report from December 2019 states that his report that year criticised the United States and Britain for withholding information, and that the General Assembly extended the investigation by consensus.

The most recent mandate was given in December 2022, according to UN News. When Othman's report was transmitted to the General Assembly in October 2024, a UN spokesperson said Othman considered it still plausible that an external attack or threat was a cause of the crash, with sabotage or unintentional human error as the remaining alternative explanations. New information cited included probable intercepts of communications, the capacity of Katangan or other forces to attack the aircraft, and the presence of foreign paramilitary or intelligence personnel in the area.

Othman also assessed it as almost certain that relevant undisclosed material remains in the archives of some member states. No person or state has been found responsible, and the cause of the crash remains officially undetermined.

name: Georgi Markov
summary: Bulgarian dissident writer Georgi Markov was assassinated on Waterloo Bridge in London when a ricin-filled pellet was injected into his leg using a modified umbrella. The Bulgarian secret service, aided by the KGB, was responsible, but the individual assassin was never definitively identified.
lastSeen: September 7, 1978, Waterloo Bridge, London

sources.title: Georgi Markov assassination - Wikipedia
Georgi Markov: The Umbrella Assassination - Smithsonian Magazine

narrative: On September 7, 1978, Georgi Markov, a 49-year-old Bulgarian dissident writer working as a journalist and broadcaster for the BBC World Service and Radio Free Europe, was walking across Waterloo Bridge in London on his way to work. He felt a sharp sting in the back of his right thigh and turned to see a man picking up an umbrella. The man apologized in a foreign accent and quickly hailed a taxi. Markov thought little of it at the time.

That evening, Markov developed a high fever. He told his wife about the incident on the bridge, noting that a small red pimple had appeared at the site of the sting. His condition deteriorated rapidly over the next three days. On September 11, Georgi Markov died at St. James's Hospital. An autopsy revealed a tiny metal pellet—only 1.7 millimeters in diameter—embedded in his thigh. The pellet had been engineered with two tiny holes that had contained ricin, an extremely potent biological toxin derived from castor beans.

The investigation determined that the assassination was carried out by the Bulgarian secret service (Darzhavna Sigurnost) with technical assistance from the Soviet KGB, which had developed the modified umbrella weapon. The murder occurred on the birthday of Bulgarian Communist leader Todor Zhivkov, leading some to speculate it was intended as a 'gift.' Just ten days before Markov's murder, another Bulgarian defector, Vladimir Kostov, survived a similar attack in Paris when the pellet fired into his back failed to release its full payload of ricin.

Despite being one of the most notorious assassinations of the Cold War, no individual was ever formally charged. After the fall of communism, Bulgarian authorities investigated and identified a Danish-born Bulgarian agent named Francesco Gullino (codenamed 'Agent Piccadilly') as the likely assassin, but Gullino denied involvement and was never charged. The case was officially closed by Bulgarian prosecutors in 2013 due to the expiration of the statute of limitations.

timeline.event: Georgi Markov is jabbed with a ricin-tipped umbrella on Waterloo Bridge, London.
Markov dies at St. James's Hospital; autopsy finds a poisoned pellet.

name: Christine Sharrock & Marianne Schmidt
summary: Fifteen-year-old friends Christine Sharrock and Marianne Schmidt of West Ryde were killed at Wanda Beach, near Cronulla in Sydney, on January 11, 1965. Their bodies were found partly buried in the sandhills the next day. More than 7,000 people were interviewed and the case was later reviewed by cold case detectives, but nobody has been charged and NSW Police say it remains open.
lastSeen: January 11, 1965, Wanda Beach sandhills, Cronulla, Sydney

sources.title: ABC News - Loved ones of the two girls murdered at Sydney's Wanda Beach reflect (2025)
ABC News - Fresh DNA clue in Wanda Beach cold case (2012)
ABC News - DNA advances may solve brutal murders (2012)
Neighbourhood Media - Cronulla True Crime: The Wanda Beach Murders Mystery
Wikipedia - Wanda Beach murders

narrative: Marianne Schmidt and Christine Sharrock were 15-year-old neighbours and close friends from West Ryde in Sydney. According to ABC News, Marianne lived with her mother and siblings, her father having died, and her mother was in hospital in January 1965. Christine had lost her father as a small child and lived with her grandmother and aunts. Marianne's family had migrated from West Germany, according to a local history feature published by Neighbourhood Media.

ABC News reports that the girls had planned a beach trip for January 10, 1965, which was put off because of rain. On the morning of January 11 they set out for Cronulla with four of Marianne's younger siblings. The younger children came home without them that evening, and Marianne's older brother Hans raised the alarm. The girls had walked on toward the quieter sandhills at Wanda Beach, north of Cronulla.

Their bodies were found the following day, partly buried in sand in the dunes. Both had been stabbed repeatedly, and ABC News reported that the injuries were so severe that relatives had difficulty identifying them. The murder weapons were never recovered, according to Wikipedia's account of the case.

The investigation that followed was one of the largest Sydney had seen, and ABC News reports that more than 7,000 people were interviewed. The detective who led the 1965 inquiry said at the time that he believed the killer was compulsive, and a senior NSW Police forensic officer told the ABC in 2012 that the girls were known to have last been seen with a teenage boy. A reward of 10,000 pounds, equivalent to 20,000 dollars after decimal currency was introduced, was offered and has never been increased, something Marianne's brother criticised publicly on the 60th anniversary in January 2025.

The case was reviewed again from 2007 by cold case detectives. In February 2012 the ABC reported that a bloodstain found on clothing worn by one of the girls had produced a weak male DNA profile, which police said was not strong enough to identify anyone with the technology then available. ABC News later reported that other stored samples were too degraded to test and that a semen sample listed in the records could not be located despite extensive searching.

Over the years several men convicted of other crimes have been discussed publicly as possible suspects, including Christopher Wilder, who died in the United States in 1984, and Derek Percy, who died in prison in Victoria in 2013. None of them was ever charged over the Wanda Beach deaths and no link has been proven. NSW Police told the ABC in January 2025 that the case is still open.

name: Circleville Letter Writer
summary: From 1977 residents of Circleville, Ohio, received hundreds of anonymous threatening letters, many aimed at school bus driver Mary Gillispie. Her husband Ron died in an August 1977 crash that the coroner ruled an accident. Paul Freshour was convicted in October 1983 of attempting to murder her with a booby trap. He denied it, and no one was ever charged with writing the letters, which continued until 1994.
lastSeen: 1977-1994, Circleville, Pickaway County, Ohio

sources.title: CBS News - Has the anonymous author of the infamous Circleville letters been unmasked?
CBS News - The Circleville letters: You've got hate mail
Unsolved Mysteries - Poison Pen Murder
All That's Interesting - Inside the mystery of the Circleville letters

narrative: In March 1977, according to CBS News, anonymous letters began arriving in Circleville, Ohio. Many were addressed to Mary Gillispie, a school bus driver, and accused her of having an affair with the school superintendent, Gordon Massie. Letters were also sent to her husband, Ron Gillispie, to Massie, and to other residents and businesses. Unsolved Mysteries' account of the case places the first letter in 1976. CBS reports that Mary Gillispie denied an affair at the time and said the relationship began only after her husband's death.

On August 19, 1977, Ron Gillispie, 35, left home after receiving a telephone call and died when his pickup truck struck a tree. The coroner ruled the death an accident. His blood alcohol level was 0.16 percent, about one and a half times the legal limit in Ohio at that time, according to Unsolved Mysteries, and a handgun that had been fired once was found with him. His brother-in-law Paul Freshour believed the death was not accidental, CBS News reports. No one was charged in connection with it.

The letters went on, and signs about Mary Gillispie and her daughter appeared along her bus route. On February 7, 1983 she stopped to take one down and found a box holding a .22 calibre handgun rigged to fire. Investigators traced the gun to Freshour, her brother-in-law. He denied any part in the trap or the letters.

Freshour stood trial in October 1983 and was convicted of attempted murder; Unsolved Mysteries gives the date as October 24, 1983. He was sentenced to seven to 25 years. CBS News reports that a state handwriting analyst and an examiner first retained by the defence both found similarities between his writing and the letters. He was never charged with writing them.

Letters postmarked from Columbus kept arriving while Freshour was in prison, and he received some himself. He was paroled in May 1994 after about ten years, and the letters stopped that year. He maintained his innocence until his death on June 28, 2012.

In a later review for CBS's 48 Hours, document examiner Beverley East said she was certain Freshour wrote the letters, while former FBI profiler Mary Ellen O'Toole said she could not account for the letters sent during his imprisonment. CBS reports that the Pickaway County Sheriff's Office regards the case as closed.

name: Mr. Cruel Victims
summary: An unidentified offender known as 'Mr Cruel' attacked three girls in Melbourne between 1987 and 1990, abducting two of them from their homes and later releasing them. He is the prime suspect in the April 1991 abduction and murder of Karmein Chan, 13, though police have not confirmed that link. No one has been charged, and a A$1 million reward remains on offer.
lastSeen: Attacks in the Melbourne suburbs of Lower Plenty, Ringwood, Canterbury and Templestowe, 1987-1991

sources.title: Wikipedia - Mr Cruel
SBS News - Vic schoolgirl murder takes toll on family
Yahoo News Australia (7News) - Police increase Karmein Chan reward to $1million in hunt for child killer
vicpolicenews.com.au - Karmein Chan: Victoria's most enduring cold case and the standing reward

narrative: 'Mr Cruel' is the name given by the media to an unidentified man who broke into family homes in Melbourne's northern and eastern suburbs in the late 1980s and early 1990s and attacked young girls. According to Wikipedia's summary of the case, which draws mainly on Herald Sun reporting, three attacks between 1987 and 1990 are attributed to the same offender on the basis of his methods and the victims' accounts. He is also the prime suspect in a fourth crime, the 1991 abduction and murder of Karmein Chan.

The first attributed attack took place at about 4 a.m. on August 22, 1987, in Lower Plenty, where an armed intruder assaulted an 11-year-old girl in her home. On December 27, 1988, a 10-year-old girl was taken from her home in Ringwood at about 5:20 a.m.; she was held for around 18 hours and released in the grounds of Bayswater High School. On July 3, 1990, a 13-year-old girl was taken from a house in Canterbury late at night, held for about 50 hours and left at a power substation in Kew. Both abducted girls survived.

On the evening of April 13, 1991, an intruder armed with a knife entered a home in Templestowe where Karmein Chan, 13, was looking after her two younger sisters. The sisters were left behind and Karmein was taken. Her remains were found in April 1992 at a site in Thomastown. According to Wikipedia, she had been shot three times in the head.

Victoria Police set up the Spectrum task force in May 1991. By the time it was wound down in January 1994 it had, according to the figures cited by Wikipedia and Australian news outlets, interviewed about 27,000 people, checked some 30,000 houses and cost about A$3.8 million. A later task force, Apollo, ran from about 2010 to 2013 without result. No one has been charged over any of the attacks.

In April 2016, on the 25th anniversary of Karmein Chan's abduction, police raised the reward for information leading to a conviction in her case to A$1 million. SBS News reported that Assistant Commissioner Stephen Fontana said someone close to the offender would know who he was. Investigators have been careful about the link between the cases: Wikipedia quotes retired detective Chris O'Connor as saying there is not enough evidence to be sure that the man responsible for the earlier attacks also killed Karmein Chan. A February 2026 article on the case said a cold case re-examination was confirmed in 2021 and that the investigation remains open.

Karmein Chan's remains are found in Thomastown.
The Spectrum task force is disbanded without an arrest.
The Apollo task force, set up around 2010 to re-examine the case, closes.

name: Angie Dodge
summary: Angie Dodge, 18, was raped and killed in her Idaho Falls apartment on June 13, 1996. Christopher Tapp was convicted in 1998 on the basis of a confession he later said was coerced; he served about 20 years and was exonerated in July 2019. Genetic genealogy led police to Brian Leigh Dripps Sr., who confessed, pleaded guilty and was sentenced on June 8, 2021, to life in prison.
lastSeen: June 13, 1996, her apartment in Idaho Falls, Idaho

sources.title: KTLA / Associated Press - Man gets life in prison for 1996 cold-case murder, rape of 18-year-old Angie Dodge in Idaho Falls
ABC News - 'A new beginning': Man convicted of murder in the '90s exonerated thanks to genetic genealogy
NBC News (Dateline) - Police arrest Idaho man in 23-year-old cold-case murder of Angie Dodge
CBS News (48 Hours) - Angie Dodge case: How a discarded cigarette led to an arrest
CBS News - Former congressional candidate and pro wrestler arrested in Vegas murder of man who was wrongly imprisoned
Wikipedia - Murder of Angie Dodge

narrative: Angie Dodge was 18 and had moved into her own apartment in Idaho Falls, Idaho, about three weeks before she was killed. According to CBS News, she did not arrive for work on the morning of June 13, 1996, and a co-worker who went to check on her found her body in the apartment. She had been raped and had suffered multiple stab and cutting wounds. ABC News, citing Idaho Falls police, reported that semen and hair collected at the scene came from a single unknown man.

In January 1997 police questioned Christopher Tapp, then 20, over a series of interrogations. Tapp confessed to taking part in the crime, although his DNA did not match the evidence; police at the time worked on the theory that more than one person had been involved. A jury convicted him of murder and rape in May 1998. Tapp later said the confession had been coerced, and the Associated Press reported that officers had supplied him with details of the case and warned him that he could face the death penalty.

The Idaho Innocence Project took up his case, and Angie's mother, Carol Dodge, came to believe the wrong man was in prison and campaigned on his behalf. According to ABC News, swabs from Angie's hands were not tested until 2016 and showed DNA only from her and the unknown man. In 2017 Tapp reached an agreement under which his rape conviction was vacated and his murder sentence reduced to time served, and he was released after roughly 20 years.

An earlier attempt to use a genealogy database led police in 2014 to New Orleans filmmaker Michael Usry Jr., whose DNA did not match; CBS News reported that he was cleared and later supported the search for the killer. In 2019 genetic genealogy work by CeCe Moore of Parabon NanoLabs pointed to Brian Leigh Dripps Sr., who had lived across the street from Dodge in 1996 and was by then living in Caldwell, Idaho. Officers collected a cigarette butt he discarded, and its DNA matched the crime scene sample. Police announced his arrest on May 16, 2019, and said he had confessed.

Tapp was formally exonerated on July 17, 2019. Dripps pleaded guilty, and on June 8, 2021, Judge Joel Tingey sentenced him to life in prison with a minimum of 20 years before parole eligibility, the Associated Press reported.

Tapp died in 2023 after being found injured at a Las Vegas hotel on October 29. CBS News reported that the Clark County coroner ruled the death a homicide and that Daniel Rodimer was charged in March 2024; his lawyers said he would contest the allegations.

name: Morgan Harrington
summary: Virginia Tech student Morgan Harrington, 20, disappeared on October 17, 2009, after leaving a Metallica concert at John Paul Jones Arena in Charlottesville. Her remains were found on an Albemarle County farm in January 2010. Jesse Matthew Jr. pleaded guilty on March 2, 2016, to her murder and abduction and to the 2014 murder of Hannah Graham, receiving four life sentences.
lastSeen: October 17, 2009, John Paul Jones Arena, Charlottesville, Virginia

sources.title: NBC Washington - Jesse Matthew Pleads Guilty in Deaths of Hannah Graham, Morgan Harrington
C-Ville Weekly - Jesse Matthew pleads guilty, receives four additional life sentences
ABC News - Parents of Two Murdered Virginia Students Speak Out After Jesse Matthew Pleads Guilty
Wikipedia - Murder of Morgan Dana Harrington
Wikipedia - Murder of Hannah Graham

narrative: Morgan Dana Harrington, a 20-year-old Virginia Tech student, went to a Metallica concert at the John Paul Jones Arena at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville on October 17, 2009. She left the arena during the event and did not get back inside. According to the statement of facts described by NBC Washington, she texted a friend shortly before 8:50 p.m. to say she would find a ride. Wikipedia's summary of the case, drawing on contemporary reports, says she was last seen at about 9:30 p.m. trying to get a lift on a nearby bridge, and that her purse, with her identification and phone, was found in a parking area at a university athletic field.

Her remains were found on January 26, 2010, at Anchorage Farm in southern Albemarle County, roughly ten miles from the arena. The death was treated as a homicide. According to NBC Washington, a Pantera T-shirt she had been wearing was recovered about three weeks after she vanished, and DNA on it matched the profile from an unsolved sexual assault committed in Fairfax, Virginia, in September 2005. That link tied the two crimes to one unknown offender but did not produce a name.

The case changed after University of Virginia student Hannah Graham disappeared in Charlottesville on September 13, 2014. Jesse Leroy Matthew Jr. was arrested in Galveston County, Texas, on September 24, 2014. According to Wikipedia's account of the Graham case, authorities said on September 29, 2014, that forensic evidence from the Harrington investigation matched evidence taken from Matthew. Graham's remains were found in Albemarle County the following month; C-Ville Weekly reported that the two sites were about five miles apart.

Matthew entered an Alford plea in the 2005 Fairfax case in June 2015 and received three life sentences. On September 15, 2015, he was formally charged with first-degree murder and abduction with intent to defile in Harrington's death. NBC Washington reported that prosecutors were prepared to present witnesses who had ridden to the arena that night in a taxi matching the one Matthew drove, and phone records showing a gap in his phone activity around 9:30 p.m.

On March 2, 2016, in Albemarle County Circuit Court, Matthew pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and abduction with intent to defile in both the Harrington and Graham cases. He received four consecutive life sentences with no possibility of parole. According to C-Ville Weekly, a capital murder charge in the Graham case was dropped as part of the agreement. Harrington's mother told reporters after the hearing that the one mistake nobody had made over the years was giving up, ABC News reported.

summary: University of Virginia student Hannah Graham, 18, disappeared from downtown Charlottesville early on September 13, 2014; her remains were found five weeks later in Albemarle County. Jesse Matthew Jr. pleaded guilty on March 2, 2016, to her murder and abduction and to the 2009 murder of Morgan Harrington, and received four consecutive life sentences.
