name: Peter Falconio
summary: British backpacker Peter Falconio, 28, was shot on the Stuart Highway near Barrow Creek in Australia's Northern Territory on July 14, 2001; his girlfriend Joanne Lees escaped. Bradley John Murdoch was convicted of the murder in December 2005 and sentenced to life. Murdoch died in July 2025 without revealing where the body is, and Falconio's remains have never been found.
lastSeen: July 14, 2001, Stuart Highway near Barrow Creek, Northern Territory, Australia

sources.title: BBC News - Man who murdered British backpacker Peter Falconio dies
BBC News - Outback killer trapped by DNA link (December 13, 2005)
ABC News (Australia) - Peter Falconio murder 25 years on
ABC News (Australia) - NT Police release new footage of Bradley John Murdoch ahead of 25th anniversary of Falconio mystery
Wikipedia - Murder of Peter Falconio

narrative: Peter Falconio, 28, and his girlfriend Joanne Lees, both from Yorkshire in England, were travelling around Australia in a Volkswagen Kombi camper van in July 2001. On the evening of Saturday, July 14, they were driving on the Stuart Highway near Barrow Creek, about 300 kilometres north of Alice Springs, when another driver pulled alongside and signalled for them to stop, saying he had seen sparks coming from their vehicle, according to the BBC.

As set out at trial and reported by the BBC and the ABC, Falconio went to the rear of the van with the man and was shot. The gunman then bound Lees' wrists with cable ties and put her in his own vehicle. She got away, hid in the scrub for several hours and eventually flagged down a passing road train. Falconio's body was not at the scene and has never been located.

The investigation was one of the largest in the Northern Territory's history; the BBC reports that at one stage there were about 600 persons of interest. According to the ABC, police came to focus on Bradley John Murdoch, then 43, who was known to authorities for drug trafficking. His vehicle matched the description Lees gave, and security camera footage placed him at an Alice Springs truck stop in the early hours of July 15. Murdoch was arrested in South Australia in November 2003 and charged with murder.

His trial in the Supreme Court of the Northern Territory in Darwin lasted about eight weeks. Lees gave evidence over four days. DNA was central: the ABC reports that a blood smear on her shirt was found to be vastly more likely to have come from Murdoch than from anyone else, and the BBC reported that DNA on the homemade restraints also pointed to him. On December 13, 2005, the jury found him guilty of murdering Falconio and of assaulting and attempting to kidnap Lees. Chief Justice Brian Martin imposed life imprisonment with a non-parole period of 28 years.

Murdoch always denied the crimes. The BBC reports that he tried twice to have the convictions overturned and failed both times. In 2016 the Northern Territory introduced "no body, no parole" legislation, which would have prevented his release unless he disclosed the location of the remains.

In June 2025 Northern Territory Police announced a reward of up to A$500,000 for information leading to the discovery of Falconio's remains. Murdoch, who had throat cancer, died in the palliative care unit of Alice Springs Hospital on July 15, 2025, aged 67. Police said it was deeply regrettable that he had died without disclosing the location. In July 2026, ahead of the 25th anniversary, police released body-worn camera footage of officers questioning Murdoch in his final weeks, in which he said he knew nothing. The reward remains on offer.

name: Brandy Hall
summary: Firefighter Brandy Hall vanished on August 17, 2006 after leaving the Malabar fire station in Brevard County, Florida, where she volunteered. Her pickup truck was found the next day partially submerged in a Palm Bay pond with blood inside. She has never been found and no one has been charged; Palm Bay police searched again in March 2026 after a new tip.
lastSeen: August 17, 2006, leaving the Malabar Volunteer Fire Department station, Malabar (Brevard County), Florida

sources.title: Yahoo News/Florida Today - New tip sparks search in Space Coast's 20-year Brandy Hall mystery

narrative: On August 17, 2006, Brandy Nichole Hall, a Palm Bay firefighter who also volunteered with the Malabar Fire Department in Brevard County, Florida, vanished after leaving the Malabar fire station at about 10:45 p.m. She was last seen at approximately 1:00 a.m. when she told a colleague she was going outside. When the crew awoke the next morning, Brandy was gone.

Her pickup truck was found the following day partially submerged in a pond in Palm Bay, with blood inside. Her firefighting gear and uniform were found neatly arranged. There were no signs of a struggle at the fire station. Surveillance cameras at the station were not functioning at the time of her disappearance.

The investigation revealed that Brandy had been having a relationship with a married man, and her personal life had been turbulent in the period before her disappearance. The Palm Bay Police Department has investigated the case but has not developed enough evidence for charges.

In 2009, a grand jury was convened to investigate the case but did not return any indictments. Brandy's family has continued to press for answers, and her case has been featured on television crime programs. Despite periodic review of evidence and new leads, Brandy Hall has never been found and no arrests have been made.

Grand jury convened; no indictments returned.
Palm Bay police conduct a two-day search after receiving a new tip; nothing conclusive is announced.

name: Emanuela Orlandi
summary: Fifteen-year-old Emanuela Orlandi, daughter of a Vatican employee, disappeared in Rome. Her case has been linked to theories involving the Vatican, organized crime, and international espionage.
lastSeen: June 22, 1983, near Sant'Apollinare, Rome, Italy

sources.title: Disappearance of Emanuela Orlandi - Wikipedia
Il Messaggero - Emanuela Orlandi latest news

narrative: On June 22, 1983, fifteen-year-old Emanuela Orlandi, the daughter of a lay employee of the Vatican, left her family's apartment within Vatican City to attend a music lesson at a school near the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Rome. She never returned. A friend who had been with her at the lesson reported that Emanuela had mentioned a cosmetics job offer from a man representing Avon.

Emanuela's disappearance quickly became entangled in a web of conspiracy theories. Within days, the Vatican received phone calls from individuals claiming to be holding Emanuela and demanding the release of Mehmet Ali Agca, the Turkish gunman who had attempted to assassinate Pope John Paul II in 1981. The calls were never authenticated.

Over the decades, the case has generated numerous theories. Some link her disappearance to the Banda della Magliana, a Rome-based organized crime group with alleged Vatican financial connections. Others suggest she was kidnapped to pressure the Vatican regarding financial scandals. Some theories involve the KGB, the Bulgarian secret service, or Turkish intelligence.

In January 2023, the Vatican announced it would open its own investigation into Emanuela's disappearance, the first time the city-state had formally investigated the case. The Orlandi family has long accused the Vatican of covering up information about what happened to Emanuela. Her brother Pietro has been a prominent campaigner for answers. Despite being one of Italy's most discussed cold cases, the truth about Emanuela's fate remains unknown.

timeline.event: Emanuela Orlandi disappears after leaving a music lesson in Rome.
Callers demand the release of Pope John Paul II's would-be assassin.
Tomb in Sant'Apollinare basilica excavated; no remains found.
Vatican announces its own investigation into the disappearance.

name: Jayme Closs
summary: Thirteen-year-old Jayme Closs was kidnapped after her parents were murdered in Barron, Wisconsin. She escaped 88 days later. Jake Patterson was sentenced to life in prison.
lastSeen: October 15, 2018, her family home, Barron, Wisconsin

sources.title: Kidnapping of Jayme Closs - Wikipedia
Jayme Closs escape - NBC News

narrative: On October 15, 2018, at approximately 12:53 a.m., a 911 call was made from the home of James and Denise Closs in Barron, Wisconsin. When deputies arrived, they found both parents shot dead. Their thirteen-year-old daughter, Jayme, was missing. The crime scene and dispatch call indicated someone had forced entry into the home.

A massive search was launched involving the FBI, the Wisconsin Department of Justice, and hundreds of volunteers. Despite extensive efforts and thousands of tips, Jayme remained missing. The case attracted national attention, and a $50,000 reward was offered for information.

On January 10, 2019, after 88 days in captivity, Jayme escaped from a cabin in the town of Gordon, Wisconsin, where she had been held by 21-year-old Jake Thomas Patterson. She approached a woman walking her dog and told her she had been kidnapped. Patterson was arrested minutes later.

Patterson confessed to the crimes, explaining that he had targeted Jayme after randomly seeing her boarding a school bus. He had meticulously planned the abduction, shaving his head and wearing gloves to avoid leaving evidence. He held Jayme under his bed, forcing her to hide for hours at a time whenever he had visitors. Patterson pleaded guilty to two counts of first-degree intentional homicide and one count of kidnapping, and was sentenced to two consecutive life sentences without the possibility of parole plus 40 years.

timeline.event: James and Denise Closs murdered; Jayme kidnapped from her home.
Jayme escapes captivity after 88 days; Jake Patterson arrested.
Patterson pleads guilty to all charges.
Patterson sentenced to two consecutive life sentences.

name: Trevaline Evans
summary: Antiques dealer Trevaline Evans vanished from her shop in Llangollen, Wales, leaving a 'Back in 2 minutes' sign on the door. She was never seen again.
lastSeen: June 16, 1990, her antiques shop on Castle Street, Llangollen, Wales

sources.title: Disappearance of Trevaline Evans - Wikipedia

narrative: On June 16, 1990, Trevaline Evans, a 52-year-old antiques dealer, was working at her shop on Castle Street in Llangollen, a town in Denbighshire, north-east Wales. At some point during the afternoon, she placed a handwritten sign on the shop door reading 'Back in 2 minutes' and left. She was never seen again.

When Trevaline failed to return, her husband Richard reported her missing. Her car was found parked near the shop, and she had left her handbag and personal belongings inside. The shop's accounts and paperwork were in order, and there was no indication she had planned to leave.

The investigation revealed that Trevaline had received a phone call at the shop shortly before her disappearance, which may have prompted her to leave. She had also recently placed an advertisement seeking to buy Victorian jewelry, which investigators speculated may have led her to meet someone. Some theories suggested she encountered someone in connection with her antiques business.

Despite extensive investigation by North Wales Police, including searches of local waterways and countryside, Trevaline Evans has never been found. The case has been periodically reviewed, and in 2020 police issued renewed appeals for information on the 30th anniversary of her disappearance. The 'Back in 2 minutes' sign has become one of the most haunting details of any missing person case.

timeline.event: Trevaline Evans leaves her shop with a 'Back in 2 minutes' sign and vanishes.
Her car, handbag, and belongings found at the shop.
Police issue renewed appeal on the 30th anniversary.

name: Phoenix Coldon
summary: Phoenix Coldon, a 23-year-old college student, was last seen on December 18, 2011, driving away from her family's home in Spanish Lake, Missouri. Her black 1998 Chevrolet Blazer was found abandoned in East St. Louis, Illinois, about three hours later and was towed; her family did not learn where it was until January 1, 2012. She has not been found.
lastSeen: December 18, 2011, leaving the driveway of her family's home in Spanish Lake, Missouri

sources.title: Missouri State Highway Patrol Missing Persons Clearinghouse - Phoenix Coldon bulletin (PDF)
UMSL Daily - Missing Phoenix: Coldon family asks UMSL community for help
Oxygen - What Happened The Day 23-Year-Old Phoenix Coldon Vanished?
HuffPost - Phoenix Coldon Missing: Missouri College Student Remembered On Birthday
NBC News - Missing in America: Phoenix Coldon
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Phoenix Coldon

narrative: Phoenix Coldon was 23 and a student at the University of Missouri-St. Louis when she disappeared on Sunday, December 18, 2011. According to the Missouri State Highway Patrol's missing-person bulletin, she was last seen leaving the driveway of her family's home in Spanish Lake, in north St. Louis County, driving a black four-door 1998 Chevrolet Blazer. The bulletin lists her date of birth as May 23, 1988, and classes her as an endangered missing person.

Her parents, Lawrence and Goldia Coldon, told the university's news site, UMSL Daily, that they last saw her at about 3 p.m. as she backed out of the driveway. Oxygen, which produced a documentary on the case, reported that she had attended church with her mother that morning, and that a witness account put her departure later, between 4:30 and 4:45 p.m. Her parents reported her missing to the St. Louis County Police Department the next day, according to UMSL Daily.

The Blazer was found the same evening in East St. Louis, Illinois, roughly a 25 to 30 minute drive away. Oxygen reported that a caller told police about an abandoned vehicle at 5:27 p.m., that an officer arrived at 5:42 p.m., and that the vehicle was standing in a traffic lane on St. Clair Avenue. HuffPost reported that it was at Ninth Street and St. Clair Avenue with the keys in the ignition, the engine running and the driver's door open. East St. Louis police had it towed as an abandoned vehicle after establishing that it had not been reported stolen.

The family was not told. According to UMSL Daily and HuffPost, they learned on January 1, 2012, that the vehicle had been in an impound lot since the day she vanished; Oxygen reported that a family friend located it. Wikipedia's summary of the case says her glasses, purse, shoes and identification were found in the vehicle when the family examined it. Oxygen reported that testing found no DNA in the vehicle other than that of family members.

UMSL Daily reported that the Major Case Squad was brought in about five days after the missing-person report. The Coldons also searched on their own and raised money for a private investigator. HuffPost reported in May 2012 that the family had used up their savings and that their home had gone into foreclosure, and quoted her mother saying that police were not actively looking for her daughter.

NBC News profiled the case in December 2014, quoting her father on the unexplained hours between her departure and the discovery of the vehicle. Oxygen broadcast a two-part documentary, The Disappearance of Phoenix Coldon, in November 2018. No arrest has been made, no one has been publicly named as a suspect, and no source found in this review reports any trace of her since 2011. The St. Louis County Police Department remains the investigating agency.

timeline.event: Phoenix Coldon is born, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol bulletin.
She is last seen at about 3 p.m. driving a black 1998 Chevrolet Blazer out of her family's driveway in Spanish Lake, Missouri.
At 5:27 p.m. a caller reports the vehicle abandoned on St. Clair Avenue in East St. Louis, Illinois; police have it towed.
Her parents report her missing to the St. Louis County Police Department.
The family learns that the vehicle has been in an East St. Louis impound lot since December 18.
Her parents appeal to students and staff at the University of Missouri-St. Louis for help.
HuffPost reports on her 24th birthday that the family has exhausted its savings searching for her.
NBC News profiles the case in its Missing in America series.
Oxygen premieres the two-part documentary The Disappearance of Phoenix Coldon.

name: Dorothy Kilgallen
summary: Journalist Dorothy Kilgallen, who was investigating the JFK assassination, was found dead in her New York townhouse. Her death was ruled an overdose but many believe she was murdered.
lastSeen: November 8, 1965, her townhouse on East 68th Street, Manhattan

sources.title: Dorothy Kilgallen - Wikipedia
The Reporter Who Knew Too Much - Amazon

narrative: Dorothy Mae Kilgallen was one of America's most prominent journalists, a syndicated columnist, and a panelist on the CBS game show What's My Line? In the months before her death, she had been actively investigating the assassination of President John F. Kennedy and had obtained the full transcript of Jack Ruby's testimony.

On the morning of November 8, 1965, Kilgallen was found dead in her New York City townhouse at 45 East 68th Street. She was found fully dressed and sitting upright in bed in a room she rarely used. The medical examiner ruled her death was caused by a combination of alcohol and barbiturates.

Many aspects of her death raised questions. She was found in a room not her own, wearing clothes she would not typically sleep in, and with a book she had already finished reading placed beside her. Her investigation files on the JFK assassination disappeared and have never been found.

Kilgallen had told friends she was about to break the Kennedy assassination case wide open. Some researchers believe she was murdered to silence her investigation, while others accept the accidental overdose ruling. Her death has remained a subject of debate among JFK assassination researchers for decades.

timeline.event: Dorothy Kilgallen found dead in her New York townhouse.
Death ruled accidental overdose of alcohol and barbiturates.
Her JFK investigation files discovered missing.

name: Dagmar Hagelin
summary: Swedish-Argentine teenager Dagmar Hagelin, 17, was shot and abducted by an Argentine Navy task group in El Palomar, Buenos Aires Province, on January 27, 1977, and was last seen by fellow detainees at the ESMA detention centre. Navy officer Alfredo Astiz was sentenced to life imprisonment on November 29, 2017, in a trial that covered her disappearance. Her remains have never been found.
lastSeen: Abducted January 27, 1977, in El Palomar, Buenos Aires Province; reported seen by other detainees at the ESMA in Buenos Aires until about February-March 1977

sources.title: La Nación - Condenaron a Alfredo Astiz a prisión perpetua por crímenes de lesa humanidad en la ESMA
Infobae - Astiz y el "Tigre" Acosta fueron condenados a prisión perpetua por los crímenes cometidos en la ESMA
Infobae - Secuestro, balazos y desaparición: Dagmar Hagelin
Maracó Digital - A 50 años del golpe: El secuestro de Dagmar Hagelin
Wikipedia - Dagmar Hagelin
Wikipedia - Alfredo Astiz

narrative: Dagmar Ingrid Hagelin was born in Buenos Aires on September 29, 1959, and held Swedish citizenship through her father, Ragnar Hagelin, according to Wikipedia. On the morning of January 27, 1977, at about 8:30, she went to a house in El Palomar, in Buenos Aires Province, to see her friend Norma Susana Burgos. Argentine press accounts, including Infobae and Maracó Digital, report that a Navy task group from the Escuela de Mecánica de la Armada (ESMA) had detained Burgos the previous day and was waiting at the house for another person, a Montoneros activist.

According to those accounts, Hagelin ran when she was confronted and was shot and wounded in the street. The accounts attribute the shot to Navy lieutenant Alfredo Astiz; Infobae reports that Burgos later testified that Astiz himself said he had fired. Sources differ on whether she was hit in the head or the back. Neighbours saw the wounded girl placed in the boot of a car. It is widely reported that she was mistaken for the person the task group was seeking.

Hagelin was taken to the ESMA, which operated as a clandestine detention centre. Burgos, who survived, stated that she saw Hagelin there with a bandaged head wound, and Maracó Digital reports that other detainees placed her in the building until late February or early March 1977, after which there is no trace of her. Her body has never been located.

Ragnar Hagelin reported the abduction to the Swedish embassy, and the Swedish government pressed the Argentine junta for information. Infobae describes strongly worded protests from Stockholm and wide coverage in Sweden. Maracó Digital reports that an Argentine military proceeding in 1980 cleared Astiz and two other officers. Spanish-language Wikipedia states that the case was closed as time-barred in 1986 and reopened by an appeals court in August 2006 as a crime against humanity.

On November 29, 2017, Federal Oral Court No. 5 in Buenos Aires delivered its verdict in the trial known as ESMA III, which examined 789 crimes and 54 defendants. Infobae reported that Astiz and Jorge Acosta were among those given life sentences and that six defendants were acquitted. La Nación noted that the charges against Astiz in that trial included the disappearance of Dagmar Hagelin. Astiz had already received a life sentence in a separate ESMA trial in October 2011, and a French court had sentenced him in absentia in 1990 for the abduction of two French nuns, according to Wikipedia.

Ragnar Hagelin, who spent decades pursuing the case, died in Stockholm in October 2016, the year before the verdict, according to Wikipedia. What happened to his daughter after she was last seen at the ESMA has not been established.

timeline.event: Dagmar Hagelin is born in Buenos Aires.
Her friend Norma Burgos is detained by an ESMA task group, which then waits at the Burgos family home in El Palomar.
Hagelin is shot, wounded and taken away by the task group in El Palomar.
Detainees report seeing her at the ESMA until about late February or early March; no trace afterwards.
An Argentine military proceeding clears Astiz and two other officers.
An appeals court reopens the case as a crime against humanity, according to Spanish-language Wikipedia.
Astiz receives a life sentence in a separate ESMA trial.
Her father, Ragnar Hagelin, dies in Stockholm.
Federal Oral Court No. 5 sentences Astiz to life imprisonment in the ESMA III trial, which covered Hagelin's disappearance.

name: Helen Brach
summary: Candy heiress Helen Brach vanished after a visit to the Mayo Clinic. Her disappearance was linked to a horse-related fraud ring. She was declared legally dead in 1984.
lastSeen: February 17, 1977, Rochester, Minnesota

sources.title: Disappearance of Helen Brach - Wikipedia
Hot Blood: The Millionairess, the Money, and the Horse Murders

narrative: Helen Vorhees Brach, the 65-year-old widow of Frank Brach, heir to the E.J. Brach & Sons candy company fortune, disappeared in February 1977. She had been visiting the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, for a routine checkup. Her houseman, Jack Matlick, claimed he drove her to O'Hare Airport on February 21, but no record of her boarding a flight was ever found.

Helen's disappearance went unreported for two weeks, raising immediate suspicion about Matlick. The investigation eventually uncovered a massive horse-related fraud ring centered on the Chicago equestrian community, where wealthy buyers were sold over-valued horses that were then killed for insurance money.

Richard Bailey, who had been romancing Helen and selling her overpriced horses, was charged with conspiring to have her killed but was not convicted of her murder; in 1995 he was sentenced to 30 years for defrauding her, with the judge stating that the sentence reflected evidence of his involvement in a conspiracy to murder her. However, Helen's body was never found, and the exact circumstances of her death remain unknown.
The case exposed a dark underworld in the Chicago horse industry involving insurance fraud, corruption, and multiple murders. Helen Brach was declared legally dead in 1984.

timeline.event: Helen Brach last confirmed alive at the Mayo Clinic.
Her disappearance reported two weeks later.
Helen declared legally dead.
Richard Bailey sentenced to 30 years for defrauding Brach; not convicted of her murder.

name: Barbara Bolick
summary: Barbara Bolick, 55, of Corvallis, Montana, disappeared on July 18, 2007 while hiking near Bear Creek Overlook in the Bitterroot Mountains outside Victor. Her hiking companion told investigators she was 20 to 30 feet away when he looked at the view and that she was gone about a minute later. Ground, dog and air searches found no trace of her, and the case remains open.
lastSeen: July 18, 2007, Bear Creek Overlook trail near Victor, Ravalli County, Montana

sources.title: The Charley Project - Barbara Assunta Bolick (archived copy)
Solve the Case - Barbara Bolick Missing Person Case, Corvallis, Montana
NBC Montana - Missing Bitterroot woman still a mystery
Montana Outdoor - Missing in Montana: The Mysterious Disappearance of Barbara Bolick

narrative: Barbara Assunta Bolick was 55 years old when she disappeared during a day hike in the Bitterroot Mountains of western Montana on July 18, 2007. According to the case summary published by Solve the Case, she and her husband had moved to Corvallis, in the Bitterroot Valley, in 2001. The Charley Project describes her as an experienced hiker who knew the area well.

That morning she set out for Bear Creek Overlook, a viewpoint above the valley outside Victor in Ravalli County, with a friend of the family who was visiting from California. Solve the Case says they left her home at about 9 a.m. According to the Charley Project, the companion told investigators that some time between 11:30 a.m. and 1 p.m. he stopped to take in a view while Bolick was 20 to 30 feet from him, and that when he turned around roughly a minute later she was no longer there. She was reported missing that afternoon.

She was wearing a pastel-colored shirt and tan shorts and carrying a black day pack, which the Charley Project says contained a .357 Magnum handgun. Search and rescue teams, dogs and aircraft fitted with infrared and thermal imaging equipment covered the area, according to Solve the Case. Neither Bolick nor the pack was found, and NBC Montana reported in 2023 that nothing connected to her had turned up in the sixteen years since.

Investigators asked for help locating two young men with a black mixed-breed dog who were seen hiking nearby around the time of the disappearance and who may have been driving a light-colored, older Chevrolet S-10 with Missoula County plates. The Charley Project stresses that the two are regarded as possible witnesses, not suspects. It also reports that the hiking companion cooperated with the investigation and has not been named a suspect.

The Charley Project lists the case as 'Lost/Injured Missing' and notes that Bolick left behind her pets, wallet, identification and passport, which investigators took as a sign that she did not leave voluntarily. Her husband said she was afraid of heights and would not have approached a cliff edge or left the trail.

The Ravalli County Sheriff's Office is listed as the investigating agency by the Charley Project, while Solve the Case lists the Missoula County Sheriff's Office cold case unit; a 2023 NBC Montana report said law enforcement had issued a fresh appeal for information. No arrest has been made, no remains have been found, and officials quoted by NBC Montana said all possibilities remain open.

timeline.event: Barbara Bolick is born, according to the Charley Project.
Bolick and her husband move to Corvallis, Montana.
Ground teams, search dogs and aircraft with thermal imaging search the area without result; investigators seek two hikers as possible witnesses.
Bolick leaves home at about 9 a.m. to hike to Bear Creek Overlook with a visiting friend.
Between 11:30 a.m. and 1 p.m. her companion loses sight of her near the overlook; she is reported missing that afternoon.
NBC Montana reports a renewed law-enforcement appeal for information; the case is still unsolved.

name: Nicole Morin
summary: Eight-year-old Nicole Morin disappeared from the hallway of her Toronto apartment building while on her way to the swimming pool. She has never been found.
lastSeen: July 30, 1985, West Mall, Etobicoke, Toronto, Ontario

sources.title: Disappearance of Nicole Morin - Wikipedia

narrative: On July 30, 1985, eight-year-old Nicole Louise Morin left her family's 20th-floor penthouse apartment at 627 The West Mall in Etobicoke, Toronto, at about 11 a.m. She was heading down to the lobby to meet a friend and walk to the building's outdoor swimming pool. She never arrived.

Nicole was last seen by her mother as she left the apartment at approximately 10:15 a.m. She was wearing her bathing suit under her clothes and carrying a white towel. Surveillance in the building was minimal, and no witnesses saw Nicole after she left the apartment.

The Toronto Police Service launched an extensive investigation, canvassing the building's residents and searching the building and surrounding area. The case generated thousands of tips over the years, but none led to Nicole's recovery.

The case remains one of Toronto's most baffling missing child cases. How Nicole vanished from a busy apartment building in broad daylight has never been explained. Her case has been periodically reviewed by Toronto Police with modern investigative techniques, and age-progressed images have been released to keep the public aware.

timeline.event: Nicole Morin leaves her apartment to go swimming and vanishes.
Extensive search of the apartment building and area finds no trace.

name: Cecilia Zhang
summary: Nine-year-old Cecilia Zhang was kidnapped from her bedroom in Toronto. Her body was found five months later. Min Chen pleaded guilty to second-degree murder.
lastSeen: October 20, 2003, her family home in North York, Toronto

sources.title: Murder of Cecilia Zhang - Wikipedia
Cecilia Zhang case - CBC News

narrative: On October 19, 2003, nine-year-old Cecilia Zhang was kidnapped from her bedroom in her family's home in North York, a district of Toronto. Her parents discovered her missing in the morning when they found her bedroom window open and a cut screen. Cecilia's shoes and jacket were still in the house.

A massive search was launched, and the case received extensive media coverage. The Zhang family offered a reward and made emotional public appeals for their daughter's return. Police investigated hundreds of tips but initially made no arrests.

On March 27, 2004, five months after her abduction, Cecilia's body was found in a wooded area near the Credit River in Mississauga. She had died from asphyxiation. DNA evidence and forensic analysis led investigators to Min Chen, a family acquaintance who had known the Zhangs through the Chinese-Canadian community.

Chen was arrested in 2004 and pleaded guilty to second-degree murder in 2006. He was sentenced to life in prison with no possibility of parole for 15 years. The case led to increased discussion about child safety and home security in Toronto.

timeline.event: Cecilia Zhang kidnapped from her bedroom in North York, Toronto.
Cecilia's body found in a wooded area near the Credit River in Mississauga.
Min Chen pleads guilty to second-degree murder; sentenced to life with no parole for 15 years.

name: Daniel Morgan
summary: Private investigator Daniel Morgan, 37, was killed with an axe in the car park of the Golden Lion pub in Sydenham, south London, on March 10, 1987. Several police inquiries and a prosecution that collapsed in 2011 produced no conviction. An independent panel reported in 2021 that the Metropolitan Police had shown a form of institutional corruption, and the force settled with his family in 2023.
lastSeen: March 10, 1987, Golden Lion pub, Sydenham, London

sources.title: The Guardian - Daniel Morgan axe murder case: timeline
The Guardian - Daniel Morgan murder: inquiry brands Met police 'institutionally corrupt'
The Guardian - Daniel Morgan murder: Met admits failings and pays damages in settlement with family
Independent Office for Police Conduct - IOPC assessment of matters linked to Daniel Morgan Independent Panel report
CBS News - London police apologize to family for unsolved 1987 ax murder of private investigator Daniel Morgan
Wikipedia - Murder of Daniel Morgan

narrative: Daniel Morgan, a 37-year-old private investigator, was found dead on March 10, 1987, beside his car in the car park of the Golden Lion pub in Sydenham, south London. He had been struck in the head with an axe. Morgan ran an agency called Southern Investigations with a business partner, Jonathan Rees. Nobody has been convicted of the killing.

According to a timeline published by The Guardian, six people were arrested in April 1987, among them Rees, Detective Sergeant Sid Fillery, brothers Glenn and Garry Vian and two other Metropolitan Police officers. All were released without charge. Fillery had been assigned to the first inquiry and, the newspaper reported, had not told his superiors that he had done work for Southern Investigations. An inquest in 1988 returned a verdict of unlawful killing. Hampshire Police then took over the inquiry on behalf of the Police Complaints Authority; Rees and another man were charged with murder in February 1989, and the charges were dropped in May 1989 for lack of evidence.

Further Metropolitan Police inquiries followed from the late 1990s, including covert recording operations. In 2002 the Crown Prosecution Service decided not to prosecute after reviewing the evidence submitted. In 2005 the then commissioner, Sir Ian Blair, acknowledged that the first inquiry had been compromised, and a fifth investigation began. In April 2008 Rees, the Vian brothers and James Cook were arrested on suspicion of murder, and Fillery on suspicion of attempting to pervert the course of justice.

Pre-trial legal argument opened at the Old Bailey in October 2009. The Guardian reported that the judge excluded three key prosecution witnesses in turn, that the case against Fillery was stayed in February 2010 and that Cook was cleared in November 2010. In March 2011 the prosecution offered no further evidence after disclosure failures, and the three remaining defendants were formally acquitted. All five men denied involvement throughout, and none of them has been convicted of any offence connected with Morgan's death.

The Home Secretary announced an independent panel in 2013. Its report, published on June 15, 2021 under the chairmanship of Baroness Nuala O'Loan, concluded that the Metropolitan Police had displayed a form of institutional corruption by putting the protection of its reputation ahead of candour about its failings. The force rejected that central finding at the time. In August 2022 the Independent Office for Police Conduct said its assessment of the report had identified no new avenues of investigation that could lead to criminal or disciplinary proceedings.

In May 2023 the Metropolitan Police disclosed that documents relevant to the case had been found in a locked cabinet at New Scotland Yard. On July 19, 2023, Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley apologised to the Morgan family, admitted liability for errors and corruption, and announced a settlement of the family's civil claim. The amount was confidential; The Guardian reported it understood the figure to be 2.25 million pounds including costs. CBS News reported at the time that a reward of 50,000 pounds remained on offer for information leading to a prosecution.

timeline.event: Daniel Morgan is found dead with axe wounds to the head in the car park of the Golden Lion pub, Sydenham.
Six people, including Morgan's business partner and three police officers, are arrested and released without charge.
An inquest at Southwark Coroner's Court returns a verdict of unlawful killing.
During the Hampshire Police inquiry two men are charged with murder; the charges are dropped in May 1989 for lack of evidence.
After a fourth inquiry the Crown Prosecution Service decides not to prosecute.
Four men are arrested on suspicion of murder and a former detective on suspicion of attempting to pervert the course of justice.
The prosecution at the Old Bailey collapses and the remaining three defendants are formally acquitted.
The Home Secretary announces the Daniel Morgan Independent Panel.
The panel's report finds a form of institutional corruption in the Metropolitan Police.
The Independent Office for Police Conduct says it has found no new avenues for investigation.
The Metropolitan Police discloses that case-related documents were found in a locked cabinet at New Scotland Yard.
The Metropolitan Police admits liability, apologises and settles the family's civil claim.

name: Marion Barter
summary: Australian schoolteacher Marion Barter secretly changed her name before vanishing during an overseas trip. She legally became 'Florabella Natalia Marion Remakel' before disappearing.
lastSeen: June 22, 1997, departing from Australia for overseas travel

sources.title: Disappearance of Marion Barter - Wikipedia
The Lady Vanishes podcast - ABC

narrative: In June 1997, fifty-one-year-old Marion Barter, a respected schoolteacher from the Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia, departed for an overseas trip to England and Europe. Before leaving, she had secretly changed her legal name to 'Florabella Natalia Marion Remakel' and sold her belongings, including her house.

Marion sent a few postcards and made brief phone calls to her daughter Sally in the initial weeks of her trip, but communication ceased in August 1997. Her bank account was accessed in Luxembourg, and there were indications someone may have been controlling her finances.

When her daughter could not reach her, she reported Marion missing. The investigation revealed the puzzling name change and asset liquidation, suggesting Marion may have been under the influence of another person. A mysterious man was identified as having been in Marion's company before her departure.

The case was examined in the ABC podcast 'The Lady Vanishes' in 2019, which uncovered new leads including connections to other missing women who had similarly changed their names and liquidated their assets. A coronial inquest opened in June 2021 and on February 29, 2024 the New South Wales coroner found that Marion is deceased, having died sometime after October 15, 1997, but could not determine the cause, place or manner of her death.

timeline.event: Marion Barter departs Australia for overseas travel.
Last known communication from Marion to her daughter.
'The Lady Vanishes' podcast launches, uncovering new leads.
Coronial inquest opens into Marion's disappearance.
Coroner finds Marion Barter is deceased; cause, place and manner of death undetermined.

name: Patricia Adkins
summary: Patricia "Patti" Adkins, 29, has not been seen since she finished a late shift at the Honda plant in Marysville, Ohio, on June 29, 2001. She had told her sister she was leaving on a trip to Canada with a married coworker, to whom she had given about $90,000. A court has declared her legally dead. No one has been charged and she has never been found.
lastSeen: June 29, 2001, Honda of America plant, Marysville, Ohio

sources.title: NBC News - Ohio mother Patricia Adkins remains missing 17 years after her disappearance
Yahoo News (NBC/Dateline) - No arrests in 17-year-old cold case of missing Ohio mother
NewsNation (WCMH) - Boyfriend of woman missing for 23 years remains primary suspect, deputies say
WJLA - New investigator now tasked to investigate Union County mom's 2001 disappearance

narrative: Patricia "Patti" Adkins was a 29-year-old single mother who worked at the Honda of America manufacturing plant in Marysville, Ohio. According to NBC News, she clocked out shortly after midnight on June 29, 2001, at the end of the second shift, just as the plant began its annual shutdown week. She has not been seen or heard from since.

NBC News reported that Adkins had told her sister, Marcia Pitts, that she was going on a week-long trip to Canada with her boyfriend, a coworker at the plant who was married to someone else. She arranged for her sister to look after her seven-year-old daughter and was expected back on July 8. When she did not return to collect the child, her sister reported her missing. The case passed to the Union County Sheriff's Office on July 10, 2001, where Lieutenant Jeff Stiers was assigned to it.

According to the same reporting, Adkins had given the man about $90,000 in the months before she disappeared. A banker told investigators she had been withdrawing the money so that he could buy out part of a side business ahead of a divorce. Family members said she had planned to hide in the bed of his pickup truck when they left the plant. Investigators found no DNA from Adkins in the truck bed. They did recover a phone and a T-shirt that her sister said Adkins had given him, as well as a letter she had written about the relationship.

Police have never publicly named the coworker. NBC News reported that he was interviewed and denied any involvement in her disappearance. The sheriff's office has described him as the primary suspect, while acknowledging, in Lieutenant Stiers's words, that an arrest would require evidence proving the case beyond a reasonable doubt. No one has been charged.

Central Ohio Crime Stoppers has said that none of Adkins's financial or personal records show any activity since June 2001, and that a court has declared her legally dead. According to a 2024 report by WCMH carried on NewsNation, Crime Stoppers offered a reward of $25,000 in 2022 for information leading to her discovery.

In 2025, Sinclair stations including WJLA reported that an investigator from the Union County Prosecutor's Office had been assigned to work on the case full time, reviewing the file for gaps. In that report the county sheriff said the matter was being treated strictly as a missing person case and that he would not commit to describing it as foul play. Adkins's daughter, who was seven when her mother vanished, has said publicly that knowing what happened would make closure easier. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Union County Sheriff's Office tip line at 937-642-7653.

name: Angie Housman
summary: Nine-year-old Angie Housman was abducted after leaving her school bus in St. Ann, Missouri, on November 18, 1993. A hunter found her body nine days later in the Busch Wildlife Area in St. Charles County. In 2019 DNA from her clothing was matched to Earl Webster Cox, who pleaded guilty in August 2020 and was sentenced to life without parole. He died in prison in December 2024.
lastSeen: November 18, 1993, after leaving her school bus in St. Ann, Missouri

sources.title: Major Case Squad of Greater St. Louis - Report #233, Victim: Angie Marie Housman
ABC News - Man charged in 1993 murder, abduction, sexual assault of 9-year-old Angie Housman
KRCG / Associated Press - Man sentenced in 1993 cold case of Missouri girl abused, left to die in wildlife area

narrative: Angie Housman was a nine-year-old from St. Ann, a suburb of St. Louis, Missouri. On the afternoon of November 18, 1993, she got off her school bus and did not arrive home. According to the Major Case Squad of Greater St. Louis, police were told at about 7:10 that evening that she was missing. When searches failed to find her, the squad was activated on November 22 to assist the St. Ann Police Department.

On November 27, 1993, at about 10:30 in the morning, a hunter found Angie's body in the Busch Wildlife Area in St. Charles County. The Major Case Squad's summary states that she had been tied to a tree, had been sexually assaulted, and had duct tape over her eyes and mouth. St. Charles County Prosecuting Attorney Tim Lohmar later said the cause of death was determined to be hypothermia. The Associated Press reported that investigators believe she was alive until only hours before she was found.

The case remained unsolved for more than 25 years. In 2019, according to ABC News, a forensic analyst found an unknown male's DNA on torn pieces of the child's underwear recovered at the scene. The profile matched Earl Webster Cox, whose DNA was already in the national CODIS database. Lohmar announced charges of murder, kidnapping and sodomy on June 5, 2019. He said at the time that it was possible another person had been involved; no one else has been charged in the sources reviewed.

Cox had a long record of offences against children. ABC News and the Associated Press reported that he joined the U.S. Air Force in 1974 and was dishonorably discharged in 1982 after being convicted of molesting four girls while stationed in Germany. He was paroled in 1985, later returned to prison, and was released again about 11 months before Angie disappeared. In 2003 he was convicted in a federal case involving an international online child pornography network, and he was subsequently held in North Carolina as a sexually dangerous person. He was in federal custody there when he was charged.

On August 20, 2020, Cox pleaded guilty in St. Charles County to first-degree murder and first-degree sexual abuse and was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Fox 2 reported that the plea removed the possibility of a death sentence and that several of Angie's relatives gave statements in court. Her mother had died before the case was solved.
Cox died in custody on December 2, 2024. A Missouri Department of Corrections spokesperson told First Alert 4 that he died of apparent natural causes.

name: Mark Kilroy
summary: University of Texas student Mark Kilroy was kidnapped during spring break in Matamoros, Mexico and ritually murdered by a drug-trafficking cult. His remains were found at a ranch with other victims.
lastSeen: March 14, 1989, Matamoros, Tamaulipas, Mexico

sources.title: Murder of Mark Kilroy - Wikipedia
Wikipedia - Adolfo Constanzo

narrative: On March 14, 1989, twenty-one-year-old Mark James Kilroy, a pre-med student at the University of Texas at Austin, was on spring break with friends in South Padre Island, Texas. That evening, the group crossed the border into Matamoros, Mexico, to visit bars. While walking back toward the international bridge, Mark was grabbed by members of a drug-trafficking cult.

Mark was taken to Rancho Santa Elena, a ranch outside Matamoros operated by cult leader Adolfo de Jesús Constanzo, a Cuban-American drug trafficker who practiced a dark form of Palo Mayombe. Constanzo believed human sacrifice would protect him and his followers from law enforcement. Mark was tortured and killed in a ritual sacrifice.

The break in the case came weeks later when a cult member ran a police roadblock. The ensuing investigation led authorities to the ranch, where they discovered the remains of Mark Kilroy and at least 14 other victims. The discovery of the cult's activities shocked the world.

Constanzo and his followers fled but were tracked to a Mexico City apartment in May 1989. During a police standoff, Constanzo ordered a follower to shoot him. Several other cult members were arrested and convicted. Sara Aldrete, Constanzo's second-in-command, was sentenced to 67 years in prison.

timeline.event: Mark Kilroy kidnapped in Matamoros, Mexico during spring break.
Police discover the ranch and the remains of 15 victims including Kilroy.

name: Meredith Kercher
summary: British exchange student Meredith Kercher, 21, was killed in her bedroom in Perugia, Italy, on November 1, 2007. Rudy Guede was convicted of murder and sexual assault in 2008 and released in 2021 after serving 13 years of a 16-year sentence. Her housemate Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito were convicted in 2009 but definitively acquitted by Italy's Court of Cassation in 2015.
lastSeen: November 1, 2007, her apartment in Perugia, Italy

Al Jazeera - Italy's top court clears Amanda Knox of murder

WRAL (CNN) - Man convicted of Meredith Kercher's murder facing trial for sexual assault

narrative: Meredith Susanna Cara Kercher, 21, from Coulsdon in Surrey, was a University of Leeds student spending an exchange year in Perugia, Italy. She shared an upstairs flat at Via della Pergola 7 with American student Amanda Knox and two Italian women. According to Channel 4 News and other reports, she was sexually assaulted and stabbed in her bedroom on the night of November 1, 2007. Her body was found the following day; the fatal injury was a wound to the neck.

On November 6, 2007, Italian police arrested Knox, her then boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito, and Patrick Lumumba, the owner of a bar where Knox worked. Knox had named Lumumba during police questioning. He was released on November 20 and was never charged with the killing. Fingerprints in Kercher's bedroom were matched on November 19 to Rudy Guede, a man born in Ivory Coast who lived in Perugia. He was arrested in Germany the next day and returned to Italy.

Guede chose a fast-track trial and was convicted of murder and sexual assault on October 28, 2008, receiving a 30-year sentence that was later reduced to 16 years on appeal. NBC News reported that his DNA was found at the scene. He has denied killing Kercher. He was released in November 2021 after serving about 13 years, according to NBC News and Voice of America.

Knox and Sollecito were tried separately in Perugia from January 2009 and convicted in December 2009, with sentences of 26 and 25 years. An appeal court acquitted them on October 3, 2011, after an independent review questioned the DNA evidence. The Court of Cassation set that acquittal aside on March 26, 2013, and a Florence appeal court convicted them again on January 30, 2014. On March 27, 2015, the Court of Cassation annulled those convictions without ordering a further trial, which ended the murder case against both. They are legally not guilty of the killing.

Knox's separate conviction for falsely accusing Lumumba has followed a different course. In January 2019 the European Court of Human Rights found that her rights had been violated during questioning, because she lacked a lawyer and adequate interpretation. Italian courts reheard the matter; a Florence court convicted her again on June 5, 2024, and the Court of Cassation upheld that conviction on January 23, 2025. The three-year sentence was covered by time she had already spent in custody.

Since his release, Guede has faced unrelated proceedings. In July 2025 a judge in Viterbo ordered him to stand trial on charges of sexual violence, mistreatment and causing injury, based on a complaint by a former partner. His lawyer has said he is innocent. According to Sky TG24, the trial was still hearing witnesses in mid-2026 and no verdict had been given.

name: Deborah Waring
summary: Twenty-year-old Deborah Waring was found murdered in Goddard Memorial State Park in Warwick, Rhode Island. Her case is one of Rhode Island's oldest unsolved homicides.
lastSeen: April 25, 1971, Goddard Memorial State Park, Warwick, Rhode Island
narrative: On April 25, 1971, the body of twenty-year-old Deborah Waring was discovered in Goddard Memorial State Park in Warwick, Rhode Island. She had been strangled. Deborah was a University of Rhode Island student and had been socializing in the area the night before.

The investigation by Warwick police examined multiple persons of interest but failed to identify a suspect. The park, a large wooded area along Narragansett Bay, offered limited forensic evidence in the era before DNA technology.

The case has been periodically reviewed as forensic technology has advanced. Rhode Island State Police and the Warwick Police Department have maintained the case file and continue to accept tips from the public.
Deborah's murder remains one of Rhode Island's oldest unsolved homicides. Her family has advocated for continued investigation, and the case is included in the state's cold case database.

timeline.event: Deborah Waring found murdered in Goddard Memorial State Park.
Investigation launched by Warwick Police Department.

name: Scott Johnson
summary: American mathematician Scott Johnson was found dead at the base of cliffs in Manly, Sydney. Initially ruled a suicide, his death was reclassified as a gay hate crime. Scott White pleaded guilty to manslaughter in 2023.
lastSeen: December 8, 1988, North Head cliffs, Manly, Sydney

sources.title: Death of Scott Johnson - Wikipedia

narrative: On December 10, 1988, the body of twenty-seven-year-old Scott Johnson, an American doctoral student in mathematics at the Australian National University, was found at the base of the North Head cliffs near Manly in Sydney's northern beaches. His clothes were neatly folded at the top of the cliff.

Police initially ruled Scott's death a suicide, but his brother Steve Johnson, a technology entrepreneur in the United States, refused to accept this finding. Steve spent decades and millions of dollars investigating his brother's death, eventually proving it was one of many gay hate crimes committed at Sydney's cliff areas in the 1980s and 1990s.

The cliffs at North Head and other sites around Sydney were known gathering places for gay men, and during the late 1980s, gangs of youths targeted gay men at these locations, bashing and sometimes pushing victims off cliffs. A 2017 inquest found that Scott was a victim of a gay hate crime.

In 2020, Scott Phillip White, who had been a teenager at the time of the killing, was arrested and charged with murder after a $1 million reward offered by Steve Johnson led to new information. White pleaded guilty to murder in January 2022 and was sentenced to 12 years and 7 months, but that conviction was overturned on appeal; in February 2023 he pleaded guilty to manslaughter and in June 2023 was sentenced to nine years in prison.

timeline.event: Scott Johnson found dead at the base of North Head cliffs.
Inquest finds Scott's death was a gay hate crime.
Scott Phillip White arrested and charged.
White, having pleaded guilty to manslaughter in February 2023, is sentenced to nine years.

name: Suzanne Sevakis
summary: Suzanne Sevakis, 20, died in April 1990 five days after an apparent hit-and-run in Oklahoma City, where she was known as Tonya Hughes. The FBI says she had been taken as a child in the mid-1970s by Franklin Delano Floyd, who raised her under false names and later married her. Her identity was confirmed by DNA in 2014. Floyd was never charged in her death, which the FBI describes as suspicious and unsolved.
lastSeen: April 1990, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma

sources.title: FBI - Cold Case Investigation
FBI - Cold Case Investigation (Internet Archive copy)
The Oklahoman - After 20 years of lies, kidnapper admits killing Oklahoma boy (Internet Archive copy)
Newsweek - 'Girl in the Picture': What Happened To Michael Anthony Hughes?
Tampa Bay Times - Franklin Floyd, subject of Netflix's 'Girl in the Picture', dies on Florida death row
Wikipedia - Franklin Delano Floyd

narrative: In the spring of 1990 a young woman known as Tonya Hughes was struck in an apparent hit-and-run in Oklahoma City. According to the FBI, she died five days later, a few months before her 21st birthday. The Oklahoman places her death in April 1990. The FBI describes the death as suspicious, and it has never been solved. It took 24 years to establish that she was Suzanne Marie Sevakis, born on September 6, 1969 in Michigan.

The man who presented himself as her husband, Clarence Hughes, handed her two-year-old son Michael to Oklahoma welfare officials shortly after her death and left. The FBI says the hit-and-run inquiry revealed that he was in fact Franklin Delano Floyd, a federal fugitive wanted since 1973. He was arrested in Georgia two months later and returned to prison. A blood test showed that he was not the boy's biological father.

According to the FBI, Floyd had married Suzanne's mother in North Carolina in 1974 under the name Brandon C. Williams, and the family moved to Texas. Floyd later told agents that, after the mother was jailed in Dallas on minor charges, he took Suzanne away with him and left her sisters at a children's home. He introduced her to others as his daughter. She lived under several names, among them Sharon Marshall, and was later married to him as Tonya Hughes.

On September 12, 1994, Floyd abducted six-year-old Michael Hughes at gunpoint from his elementary school in Choctaw, Oklahoma. Floyd was caught in Kentucky two months later without the boy, was convicted of federal kidnapping and, according to The Oklahoman, was sentenced in 1995 to 52 years. In 2002 he was convicted in Florida of the 1989 murder of Cheryl Ann Commesso and sentenced to death.

The FBI and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children reopened the case in 2013. In 2014, FBI agents Scott Lobb and Nate Furr interviewed Floyd in prison over several days. He admitted shooting Michael on the day of the kidnapping, and he named the woman known as Tonya Hughes as Suzanne Sevakis. The FBI confirmed the identification with court records and DNA and traced her birth parents. Michael's remains have not been found despite a search near the Oklahoma-Texas border in 2015.

Floyd was never charged in connection with Suzanne Sevakis's death. Newsweek reported in 2022 that he remained a person of interest, and the FBI agent who interviewed him said her death was the one subject Floyd would not discuss. Floyd died in January 2023 while on Florida's death row, according to the Tampa Bay Times.

Franklin Delano Floyd, using the name Brandon C. Williams, marries Suzanne's mother in North Carolina, according to the FBI.

name: Katrice Lee
summary: Katrice Lee, the daughter of a British soldier, disappeared on her second birthday, November 28, 1981, from a NAAFI shopping complex at Schloss Neuhaus near Paderborn, West Germany. Searches in 1981 and a 2018 excavation beside the River Alme found nothing, and a man arrested in 2019 was released without charge. She has never been found.
lastSeen: November 28, 1981, NAAFI shopping complex, Schloss Neuhaus, Paderborn, West Germany

sources.title: Forces News - The disappearance of Katrice Lee: How the investigation has unfolded
Forces News - Man arrested over Katrice Lee disappearance released without charge
Ministry of Defence - Defence in the Media: 30 April 2018
Missing People - Katrice Lee

narrative: Katrice Lee was born on November 28, 1979, in Rinteln, West Germany, where her father, Richard Lee, was serving with the British Army's 15th/19th The King's Royal Hussars. On her second birthday, November 28, 1981, she went with her mother, Sharon, and her aunt Wendy to the NAAFI shopping complex at Schloss Neuhaus, near Paderborn, to buy food for her birthday party.

According to Forces News and the Ministry of Defence's media summary, the shop was crowded because it was the last payday before Christmas. At the checkout Sharon Lee realised she had forgotten to pick up crisps, put Katrice down and asked her sister to watch the child while she went back for them. When she returned, in what she has estimated was less than a minute, Katrice was gone. Wikipedia records that she was wearing red Wellington boots and a turquoise duffel coat over a tartan dress, and that she had a squint in her left eye.

German police and the Royal Military Police searched the area and dragged the nearby River Lippe, working on the theory that she had wandered off and drowned. No trace of her was found. Richard Lee has always maintained that his daughter was abducted and has repeatedly criticised the way the first inquiry was run.

The case was re-examined in 2000, when an age-progressed image was produced and the BBC's Crimewatch broadcast an appeal. Forces News reports that a person was questioned at that stage and released without charge. In 2012 the Royal Military Police reopened the investigation and, together with a defence minister, apologised to the family for failings in the original inquiry. In February 2017 police released an e-fit of a man reportedly seen carrying a small child to a green saloon car near the shopping complex.

In April and May 2018 a Royal Military Police team excavated a stretch of the bank of the River Alme near Paderborn over about five weeks after a review of the evidence. Nothing relevant was found. On September 23, 2019, a former serviceman was arrested and an address in Swindon was searched. He was released without charge two days later.

Richard Lee, who lives in Hartlepool, has continued to campaign. Forces News reported that the prime minister agreed in November 2021 to meet him and that in 2023 he announced he would hand back his military medals in protest. A photographic exhibition about the case was held at the former NAAFI site in November 2024. In June 2026 he asked police to act against a woman who has claimed for several years to be Katrice although a 2020 test showed she is not, according to Rayo. Katrice Lee remains missing.

name: Jill Meagher
summary: Jill Meagher, a 29-year-old Irish-born ABC Radio Melbourne employee, was raped and murdered while walking home along Sydney Road in Brunswick, Melbourne, in the early hours of September 22, 2012. Adrian Bayley, who was on parole at the time, pleaded guilty in April 2013 and was sentenced to life imprisonment. The case led to a review of Victoria's parole system.
lastSeen: September 22, 2012, at about 1:40 a.m., Sydney Road, Brunswick, Melbourne

ABC News - Accused killer of Jill Meagher appears in court

narrative: Jill Meagher, 29, was born in Drogheda, Ireland, and lived in Melbourne with her husband, Tom Meagher. She worked for 774 ABC Melbourne; the Irish Times described her role as unit manager at the radio station, and ABC News reports refer to her as an ABC employee. She was not a reporter, although earlier versions of this record described her as a journalist.

According to the Irish Times and ABC News, Meagher spent the evening of Friday, September 21, 2012, with work colleagues at bars on Sydney Road in Brunswick, an inner suburb of Melbourne. She left on foot at about 1:30 a.m. on Saturday, September 22, for the short walk home. CCTV from a bridal shop on Sydney Road recorded her at about 1:40 a.m. speaking with a man in a blue hooded top. Her husband searched for her when she did not return and reported her missing in the early hours of that morning.

The Irish Times reported that her handbag was found the following Monday in a laneway near Sydney Road and that the homicide squad took over the investigation. Police released the CCTV footage on Wednesday, September 26, and ABC News reported that police said the footage played a major part in the arrest. Adrian Ernest Bayley, 41, of Coburg, was arrested on the afternoon of Thursday, September 27. Meagher's body was found in the early hours of September 28 in a shallow grave beside a road at Gisborne South, roughly 50 kilometres north-west of Melbourne. Bayley was charged with rape and murder and appeared in Melbourne Magistrates' Court that day.

Bayley pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria on April 5, 2013. On June 19, 2013, Justice Geoffrey Nettle sentenced him to life imprisonment for murder and 15 years for rape, with a non-parole period of 35 years, according to ABC News. The court heard that Bayley was on parole when he attacked Meagher. ABC News and SBS reported that he had previously been jailed for a series of rapes and had been released on parole in 2010, and that his parole was not cancelled after he was convicted of assaulting a man in Geelong.

In 2014 and 2015 Bayley was tried for three further rapes committed in 2000 and 2012 and was found guilty; ABC News reported that his non-parole period was then extended to 43 years. On July 13, 2016, the Victorian Court of Appeal quashed the convictions relating to one of those complainants on the ground that the identification evidence should not have been admitted, and reduced the non-parole period to 40 years. ABC News reported that he becomes eligible for parole in 2055.

The case drew a large public response. According to Wikipedia's summary of contemporary reports, about 30,000 people took part in a march along Sydney Road on September 30, 2012. The circumstances of Bayley's release led the Victorian government to tighten parole laws in 2013 and to commission a review of the parole system by former High Court judge Ian Callinan.

name: Lynette Dawson
summary: Lynette Dawson vanished from her Sydney home. Her husband Chris Dawson, a former rugby league player and teacher, was convicted of her murder in 2022 after the podcast 'The Teacher's Pet' revived interest.
lastSeen: January 8, 1982, 2 Gilwinga Drive, Bayview, Sydney

sources.title: Disappearance of Lynette Dawson - Wikipedia
The Teacher's Pet podcast - The Australian (archived copy)

narrative: On January 8, 1982, thirty-three-year-old Lynette Joy Dawson vanished from her home in Bayview, a suburb on Sydney's northern beaches. Her husband, Chris Dawson, a well-known rugby league player and high school teacher, claimed she had left to 'find herself' and moved in with his teenage babysitter and lover, Joanne Curtis, almost immediately.

Lynette's family was suspicious from the start—she had left behind her children, her belongings, and her bank account. No evidence of Lynette being alive after January 8, 1982, was ever found. Despite this, police initially accepted Chris Dawson's explanation.

In 2018, journalist Hedley Thomas launched 'The Teacher's Pet,' a podcast investigating Lynette's disappearance. It became one of the most downloaded podcasts in the world, generating renewed public interest and new witnesses. The podcast detailed Chris Dawson's relationship with his teenage student and the inadequacies of the original investigation.

Chris Dawson was arrested in December 2018 and charged with murder. His trial, held before a judge alone to avoid jury bias from the podcast's influence, concluded in August 2022 with a guilty verdict. Dawson was sentenced to 24 years with a non-parole period of 18 years. Lynette's body has never been found.

timeline.event: Lynette Dawson vanishes from her Bayview home.

name: Nell Cropsey
summary: Nineteen-year-old Nell Cropsey vanished from her family home in Elizabeth City, North Carolina. Her body was found in the Pasquotank River 37 days later. Her beau Jim Wilcox was convicted but later pardoned.
lastSeen: November 20, 1901, her family home, Elizabeth City, North Carolina

sources.title: NC Dept. of Natural and Cultural Resources - The Mystery of Beautiful Nell Cropsey

narrative: On the evening of November 20, 1901, nineteen-year-old Ella Maud 'Nell' Cropsey stepped outside her family's home on the banks of the Pasquotank River in Elizabeth City, North Carolina, to speak with her beau, Jim Wilcox, on the porch. She was never seen alive again.

Nell's family raised the alarm that night when she did not return. A massive search of the area ensued, but Nell could not be found. Thirty-seven days later, her body surfaced in the Pasquotank River near the family home. The cause of death was inconclusive—some experts suggested a blow to the temple, others drowning.

Jim Wilcox was arrested and charged with murder. He was convicted in his first trial and sentenced to death, but the verdict was overturned. In a second trial, he was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 30 years. He served 15 years before being pardoned by the governor.

Many in the community believed Wilcox was innocent, while others thought he had killed Nell in a quarrel about their relationship. Wilcox maintained his innocence for the rest of his life. In 1934, he died by suicide. The true circumstances of Nell Cropsey's death remain debated by historians.

timeline.event: Nell Cropsey vanishes from her family home in Elizabeth City.
Her body recovered from the Pasquotank River.

name: Christopher Kerze
summary: Christopher Kerze, 17, has been missing since April 20, 1990, when he left his family's home in Eagan, Minnesota, in the family van. A farewell letter postmarked Duluth reached his parents the next day, and the van was found two days after he left on Highway 38 north of Grand Rapids. Searches found no trace of him, and Eagan police still list the case as open.
lastSeen: April 20, 1990, his family's home in Eagan, Minnesota

sources.title: KSTP - Family of missing Eagan teenager profiled in popular music video remain hopeful for answers
Bemidji Pioneer - Twenty six years later, Minnesota parents believe missing son may still be alive
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Christopher Kerze

narrative: Christopher Kerze was a 17-year-old junior at Henry Sibley High School when he disappeared from Eagan, Minnesota, on April 20, 1990. According to a 2016 Forum News Service report published by the Bemidji Pioneer, he told his parents, Jim and Loni Kerze, that he felt unwell and stayed home from school that day. When his mother returned, he and the family's blue Dodge Caravan were gone.

A note had been left on the kitchen table. As quoted by KSTP, it said that something important had come up, that he was feeling somewhat better, and that he would be back by six unless he got lost. He did not come home that evening. The Bemidji Pioneer report states that a handwritten letter postmarked Duluth arrived the following day, which the family described as a farewell. Wikipedia's summary of the case says the letter admitted he had not really been ill and indicated that he intended to take his own life.

Two days after he left, the van was found abandoned along Minnesota Highway 38, roughly 20 miles north of Grand Rapids and about 200 miles from Eagan, near the George Washington and Chippewa forests. According to the same report, his father's Mossberg 20-gauge bolt-action shotgun was missing from the home, and $200 had been withdrawn from Christopher's savings account. Ground and air searches of the area did not locate him. Search dogs followed a scent about a mile into the woods from the highway before the trail stopped.

The case received national exposure in 1993, when his photograph was included in the American version of Soul Asylum's music video for "Runaway Train", which featured missing young people. In 2004, an anonymous letter postmarked Seattle told the family to stop looking for him; investigators concluded it was not credible, according to the Bemidji Pioneer report.

Interest in the case was renewed in 2016, after the Jacob Wetterling case in Minnesota was resolved. That year the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children released an age-progressed image showing how Christopher might look at 43, and his parents said publicly that they believed he could still be alive.

No remains have been found and no evidence of what happened to him has been made public. In a KSTP report marking 35 years since the disappearance, Eagan Police Detective Angela Casey, who is assigned to the case, said many searches had been carried out and that the department remained committed to it. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Eagan Police Department.

name: Claudia Kirschhoch
summary: Claudia Kirschhoch, a 29-year-old New York travel writer and editor with Frommer's Travel Guides, disappeared in Negril, Jamaica, in late May 2000 after a press trip to Cuba was cancelled. She was last reported seen on May 27 walking along a beach; her passport, credit cards and cash were left at her resort. No one has been charged and she has never been found.
lastSeen: May 27, 2000, walking along a beach away from her resort in Negril, Jamaica

sources.title: Unsolved Mysteries - Claudia Kirschhoch

CBS News - Natalee-Like Case, 5 Years Later

narrative: Claudia Kirschhoch was a 29-year-old travel writer from New York who had recently started work with Frommer's Travel Guides. According to the Jamaica Observer, she was one of a group of American travel writers who flew from New York to Jamaica on May 24, 2000, on their way to Cuba. The Cuban leg of the trip fell through, and the Sandals hotel chain offered the group accommodation in Jamaica instead. Kirschhoch and another writer, Tania Grossinger, chose to stay at the chain's Beaches Negril resort.

Grossinger later booked a flight home and left as scheduled. Kirschhoch stayed on. According to the Unsolved Mysteries case file, a lifeguard reported seeing her walking along a local beach, away from the resort, and she is listed as last seen on May 27, 2000. The Jamaica Observer reported that she missed her June 1 check-out date. Her parents, Fred and Mary Ann Kirschhoch, learned on June 2 that she had not returned to her office in New York.

The Unsolved Mysteries account says her passport, credit cards, cell phone and $180 in cash were found in the hotel safe, and that her clothes, apart from one bathing suit, were packed in her suitcase. It also reports that the resort's vehicle logbook for that month could not be found, that footage from a camera near her room had been recorded over, and that her room was cleared by staff before it could be examined. A Jamaican detective quoted in that account considered a drowning highly unlikely because the water in the area was shallow and the current weak.

Her parents brought in an American search dog team, and the FBI assisted. According to Unsolved Mysteries, the dog indicated her scent at the home and in the car of a resort bartender who had befriended her. Items were sent to the FBI laboratory and no blood was found. The man was questioned and given a polygraph, which was inconclusive, and the detective said police did not regard him as a suspect. CBS News reported in 2005 that he was never charged with anything.

A US$50,000 reward was offered. In February 2002 her parents met Jamaica's police commissioner in Kingston for an update, and in March 2003 the Jamaica Observer reported that police were still following up leads. CBS News reported that the family had her declared legally dead in May 2002 so that they could pursue a lawsuit against Sandals. The New York Post reported that the wrongful-death suit alleged the company failed to warn her of known risks and mishandled evidence; Sandals said it had supported the authorities throughout.

By 2005 the New York Post reported that the FBI had placed the matter in its cold case files. No one has been charged in connection with her disappearance, and no trace of Claudia Kirschhoch has been found.

name: Barbara Blatnik
summary: Barbara Blatnik, 17, of Garfield Heights, Ohio, was found strangled beside O'Neil Road in Cuyahoga Falls on December 20, 1987. In May 2020, after DNA and genetic genealogy work funded by the Porchlight Project, police arrested James Zastawnik of Cleveland, who pleaded not guilty. He was indicted for aggravated murder and murder but died in August 2021 before trial, so the charges were never tested in court.
lastSeen: December 19, 1987, around midnight, corner of Warner Road and Grand Division, Garfield Heights, Ohio

sources.title: Cleveland 19 News - Cleveland man pleads not guilty to 1987 murder in Cuyahoga Falls
Cleveland 19 News - Cleveland man indicted for 1987 murder in Cuyahoga Falls
Cleveland 19 News - Cleveland man waiting to stand trial for 1987 murder dies while out on bond
The Cinemaholic - Barbara Blatnik Murder: How Did She Die? Who Killed Her?

narrative: Barbara Blatnik, known to friends as Barbie, was a 17-year-old from Garfield Heights, a suburb of Cleveland, Ohio. According to a Cuyahoga Falls Police Department statement quoted by Cleveland 19 News, she was last seen alive around midnight on December 19, 1987, when a friend dropped her off at the corner of Warner Road and Grand Division in Garfield Heights.

At about 10 a.m. on December 20, 1987, her unclothed body was found beside O'Neil Road, a narrow access road leading to Blossom Music Center in Cuyahoga Falls, Summit County. Police said her injuries were consistent with strangulation. The location is roughly 25 miles from her home, according to a summary of the case by The Cinemaholic, which also reports that a ring engraved with her name helped identify her.

The investigation produced no charge for more than three decades. The Cinemaholic's account says male DNA recovered from under her fingernails could not be matched to anyone in law-enforcement databases. In August 2019 the journalist James Renner launched the Porchlight Project, a nonprofit that pays for DNA testing in Ohio cold cases, and chose the Blatnik case as its first. According to Wikipedia's article on Renner, the group funded new testing of the fingernail samples and forensic genealogy research carried out by Identifinders International.

On May 6, 2020, Cuyahoga Falls police arrested James Zastawnik, 67, of Cleveland. Police said he had been linked to the crime through new evidence made possible by advances in DNA technology, and the police chief credited cooperation between detectives, the Porchlight Project and the Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation. Zastawnik pleaded not guilty at a video arraignment in Stow Municipal Court and bond was set at $1 million. In June 2020 a Summit County grand jury indicted him on charges of aggravated murder and murder.

The case never reached a jury. The Cinemaholic reports that his bond was later reduced, that the trial was postponed several times, and that he maintained he did not kill her. Cleveland 19 News reported in September 2021 that Zastawnik had died while free on bond awaiting trial; other outlets reported that he died of cancer in late August 2021, about two months before the scheduled trial date.
Because the defendant died before trial, no court ever ruled on the evidence, and Zastawnik was not convicted of any offence in connection with Barbara Blatnik's death. No one else has been charged.

timeline.event: Barbara Blatnik is dropped off by a friend around midnight at Warner Road and Grand Division in Garfield Heights; she is not seen alive again.
