A Summit County grand jury indicts Zastawnik on charges of aggravated murder and murder.
Zastawnik dies while on bond, before trial; the charges end without a verdict.

name: Robert Pickton Victims
summary: Robert Pickton, a pig farmer from Port Coquitlam, British Columbia, was convicted in December 2007 of the second-degree murders of six women and sentenced to life in prison. Police began searching his farm on February 5, 2002. Twenty further first-degree murder charges were stayed in 2010. Pickton died on May 31, 2024, after an assault by another inmate in a Quebec prison.
lastSeen: Various dates, Port Coquitlam, British Columbia, Canada

sources.title: The Globe and Mail - Who was Robert Pickton? A timeline of events
Correctional Service Canada - Release of Investigation Findings related to the Death of Robert Pickton
Global News - 'I did it for the victims': Robert Pickton's killer tells court
Wikipedia - Robert Pickton
Pickton trial - Vancouver Sun

narrative: Robert Pickton operated a pig farm in Port Coquitlam, British Columbia, east of Vancouver. According to a timeline published by The Globe and Mail, the RCMP searched the property on February 5, 2002 under a warrant relating to firearms. The following day a joint task force of RCMP and Vancouver police officers sealed off the farm and began a much larger search connected with the disappearances of women from the Vancouver area.

Pickton was charged with a weapons offence on February 7, 2002, and on February 22 he was charged with two counts of first-degree murder. More counts were added as the search of the farm continued, and by May 2005 he stood charged with the first-degree murder of 27 women, The Globe and Mail reported. The charges were later divided so that six counts would be tried first.

The jury trial opened on January 22, 2007. The Globe and Mail reported that the Crown and defence presented 129 witnesses. On December 9, 2007, the jury convicted Pickton of six counts of second-degree murder; Wikipedia's account, citing court records, names the six women as Sereena Abotsway, Mona Wilson, Andrea Joesbury, Brenda Wolfe, Georgina Papin and Marnie Frey. Two days later he was sentenced to life in prison with no eligibility for parole for 25 years, the maximum for second-degree murder.

The British Columbia Court of Appeal rejected Pickton's appeal on June 25, 2009, and the Supreme Court of Canada upheld the convictions on July 30, 2010. On August 4, 2010, the remaining 20 first-degree murder charges were stayed, so those cases were never tried. Global News and other outlets have reported that Pickton told an undercover officer he had killed 49 women; that claim was never tested in court beyond the six counts.

A public inquiry into how police handled the reports of missing women released its findings on December 17, 2012. According to The Globe and Mail, it identified serious failures in the police investigations.

On May 19, 2024, Pickton was assaulted by another inmate at Port-Cartier Institution, a federal maximum-security prison in Quebec. He died on May 31, 2024, aged 74, the Correctional Service of Canada said. The service released the findings of its investigation on July 4, 2025, and accepted recommendations on inmates' access to items that could be used as weapons. Global News reported that the inmate, Martin Charest, pleaded guilty to first-degree murder on September 25, 2025 and was sentenced to life in prison with no parole eligibility for 25 years.

The remaining 20 first-degree murder charges are stayed.
The public inquiry into the missing women investigations releases its findings.
Pickton dies of injuries from a May 19 assault by another inmate at Port-Cartier Institution, Quebec.
Martin Charest pleads guilty to first-degree murder in Pickton's death and is sentenced to life in prison.

name: Tina Smith
summary: Tina Smith, 41, was found dead in her Roanoke County, Virginia home on December 6, 2010, and her 12-year-old daughter was missing. The girl was found safe four days later in San Francisco with Smith's boyfriend, Jeffrey Scott Easley. Easley pleaded no contest to capital murder on February 28, 2012, and was sentenced to life without parole. He died in custody in March 2021.
lastSeen: December 3, 2010, Salem area, Roanoke County, Virginia

sources.title: Roanoke County, VA - Jeffrey Scott Easley Pleads No Contest to Capital Murder

narrative: Tina Smith, 41, was found dead in her home in Roanoke County, Virginia, on December 6, 2010, according to a Roanoke County news release. Her 12-year-old daughter was not at the house, and an Amber Alert was issued the same day, ABC News reported. The county later stated that Smith died of blunt force trauma to the head, strangulation and suffocation.

Investigators focused on Jeffrey Scott Easley, Smith's boyfriend, who was also missing. According to WSET's reporting on search warrants filed in the case, Smith and her daughter were last seen in the Salem area on December 3, 2010, and police believed Smith was killed that night. ABC News reported that surveillance video dated December 3 showed Easley and the girl refuelling a vehicle. The search drew national media coverage over the following days.

On December 10, 2010, a shopper in San Francisco, Theresa Shanley, recognized the girl outside a Safeway supermarket and asked store staff to call police, according to ABC News. Easley was arrested and the child was returned safely to her family in Virginia. WSET reported that Easley waived extradition at a San Francisco court hearing on December 14, 2010, and was ordered returned to Virginia. He was initially held on abduction and credit card fraud charges and was later charged with capital murder.

On February 28, 2012, Easley entered a plea of no contest to capital murder during a motions hearing in Roanoke County Circuit Court, according to the county's release. He was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. As part of the agreement a charge of abduction with intent to defile was dropped. WSET quoted one of his defence attorneys describing the agreement as a good resolution, given that a capital murder trial could otherwise have exposed Easley to a death sentence. In its statement the county said that Easley had had substantial access to the girl for about five months before the killing and had gradually increased his influence over her.

Easley served his sentence at River North Correctional Center in Independence, Virginia. WSLS reported that he died on March 1, 2021, at Twin County Regional Hospital in Galax, Virginia. At the time of that report the medical examiner's office had not determined a cause of death, and the Virginia Department of Corrections had opened an investigation into the death.

The homicide victim in this case is Tina Smith. Her daughter, who was a minor at the time, survived and was returned to relatives. No one other than Easley was charged in connection with Smith's death.

timeline.event: Tina Smith and her daughter are last seen in the Salem area; police later say they believe Smith was killed that night.

name: Dorothy Jane Scott
summary: Dorothy Jane Scott, 32, vanished from the parking lot of UC Irvine Medical Center in Orange County, California, on the night of May 28, 1980, after months of anonymous calls from a man who alternately professed love and threatened her. Her car was found burning hours later. Her remains were discovered beside Santa Ana Canyon Road in Anaheim in August 1984. No one has been arrested.
lastSeen: May 28, 1980, UC Irvine Medical Center parking lot, Orange, California

sources.title: Orange County Register, Aug 16, 1984 - Remains are identified; mom missing since '80 (NewspaperArchive clipping, archived)
Orange County Register, Aug 7, 1984 - Human, dog bones are found (NewspaperArchive clipping, archived)

narrative: Dorothy Jane Scott, born April 23, 1948, was a single mother who lived in Stanton, California, with her aunt and young son and worked as a secretary for two jointly owned shops in Anaheim, according to Wikipedia's account, which draws on Los Angeles Times and Orange County Register reports. Her parents, Jacob and Vera Scott, lived in Anaheim and looked after her son while she worked.

In the months before she disappeared, Scott received calls at work from a man she could not identify. Her mother told the Orange County Register in 1984 that the caller swung between declarations of love and threats, and that shortly before the disappearance he said he would find her alone and cut her to pieces. The calls frightened Scott enough that she took up karate.

On the evening of May 28, 1980, Scott and a colleague, Pam Head, drove a co-worker, Conrad Bostron, to UC Irvine Medical Center, where he was treated for a black widow spider bite. According to Wikipedia, Bostron was discharged at about 11 p.m. and Scott went to fetch her car. Head and Bostron then saw her white 1973 Toyota station wagon speed toward them and out of the lot; dazzled by its headlights, they could not see who was driving. At about 4:30 a.m. the car was found on fire in an alley roughly ten miles away.

About two weeks later, a man telephoned the Register and said he had killed Scott because he had caught her with another man. The newspaper reported that he described details of her clothing that had not been made public. Scott's parents also received repeated calls from a man claiming to hold her or to have killed her. Vera Scott said the line was tapped but the caller never stayed on long enough to be traced.

On August 6, 1984, a construction foreman found partly charred human and dog bones in brush about 30 feet from Santa Ana Canyon Road in northeast Anaheim, the Register reported. A deputy coroner estimated they had lain there about two years, since a brush fire had crossed the site in 1982. Dental records identified the remains as Scott's on August 14, and her mother recognised a turquoise ring and a watch found with them. The coroner's office said the cause of death was unlikely to be determined from the skeletal remains.
No arrest has been made and the caller has never been publicly identified. The case remains unsolved.

In the months before her disappearance, Scott receives anonymous calls at work from a man who alternately professes love and threatens her.
Scott takes a co-worker to UC Irvine Medical Center; at about 11 p.m. she goes to fetch her car and is not seen again.

A memorial service is held (per Wikipedia).

name: Amy Lord
summary: Twenty-four-year-old Amy Lord was kidnapped from her South Boston apartment, forced to withdraw money from ATMs, then murdered. Edwin Alemany was convicted and sentenced to life.
lastSeen: July 23, 2013, South Boston, Massachusetts

sources.title: Amy Lord case - NBC Boston
Bing results listing Reuters, Boston Globe, Universal Hub (June 8-9, 2015) on the Alemany verdict

narrative: On July 23, 2013, Amy Lord, a 24-year-old graduate of the College of the Holy Cross, was kidnapped from her apartment in South Boston, Massachusetts. Surveillance footage later showed her being forced at knifepoint to withdraw cash from multiple ATMs across the Boston area.
Amy's body was found later that day in Hyde Park's Stony Brook Reservation. She had been stabbed multiple times. The brutal nature of the crime and the daylight kidnapping shocked the city.

Edwin Alemany, a 28-year-old with a long criminal history, was identified through ATM surveillance footage and DNA evidence. He had been released from custody just weeks before the murder despite a string of violent offenses.

Alemany was convicted of first-degree murder in 2015 and sentenced to life in prison without parole. The case prompted calls for reform to the criminal justice system's handling of repeat violent offenders.

timeline.event: Amy Lord kidnapped and murdered in Boston.
Edwin Alemany arrested.
Alemany convicted of first-degree murder; sentenced the next day to life without parole.

name: Vanessa Guillen
summary: Army specialist Vanessa Guillen was bludgeoned to death by fellow soldier Aaron Robinson at Fort Hood. The case exposed systemic failures in military sexual harassment reporting.
lastSeen: April 22, 2020, Fort Hood, Texas

sources.title: I Am Vanessa Guillen Act (archived copy)
Wikipedia - Murder of Vanessa Guillen

narrative: On April 22, 2020, twenty-year-old Army Specialist Vanessa Guillen disappeared from Fort Hood in Killeen, Texas, one of the largest military installations in the United States. Her family reported that she had told them she was being sexually harassed by a superior but was afraid to report it through official channels.

After a two-month search, Guillen's dismembered remains were found on June 30 near the Leon River, about 20 miles from Fort Hood. Evidence pointed to Specialist Aaron David Robinson, who had bludgeoned Guillen with a hammer in an armory room and then enlisted his girlfriend Cecily Aguilar to help dismember and dispose of the body.

When investigators attempted to arrest Robinson on July 1, he fled the post and fatally shot himself. Aguilar was arrested and in November 2022 pleaded guilty to accessory after the fact and three counts of making false statements. She was sentenced to 30 years in prison.

The case sparked a national reckoning about sexual harassment and assault in the U.S. military. The 'I Am Vanessa Guillen Act,' signed into law in 2021, reformed how the military handles sexual harassment complaints by removing the chain of command from the reporting process.

timeline.event: Vanessa Guillen disappears from Fort Hood.
Guillen's remains found near the Leon River.
Aaron Robinson dies by suicide as investigators close in.

name: Ann Marie Burr
summary: Eight-year-old Ann Marie Burr vanished from her Tacoma, Washington home. Serial killer Ted Bundy, who lived nearby as a teenager, has been speculated as a suspect but the connection was never proven.
lastSeen: August 31, 1961, her family home in Tacoma, Washington

sources.title: Disappearance of Ann Marie Burr - Wikipedia
Ann Marie Burr - Charley Project

narrative: On August 31, 1961, eight-year-old Ann Marie Burr vanished from her family's home on North 14th Street in Tacoma, Washington. Her parents discovered she was missing in the early morning hours after finding her bedroom window open and a side door unlocked. Despite an intensive search, she was never found.

The case attracted renewed attention years later when serial killer Ted Bundy, who had grown up in the same Tacoma neighborhood and would have been 14 years old at the time, was suggested as a possible suspect. Bundy denied involvement in the Burr disappearance before his execution in 1989, though he acknowledged he had been a troubled teenager.
DNA testing conducted in the 2000s was inconclusive. While the Ted Bundy theory remains popular in true crime circles, investigators have never been able to establish a definitive connection.
Ann Marie Burr's disappearance remains Tacoma's oldest unsolved missing child case. The Tacoma Police Department continues to maintain the case file.

Ted Bundy denies involvement before his execution.

name: Gannon Stauch
summary: Gannon Stauch, 11, was reported missing from his home near Colorado Springs on January 27, 2020; his remains were found in Florida that March. His stepmother, Letecia Stauch, was convicted of murder in May 2023 after a jury rejected her insanity plea. The Colorado Court of Appeals reversed the convictions on April 2, 2026, over a biased juror and ordered a new trial; the state has asked the Colorado Supreme Court to review.
lastSeen: January 27, 2020, his home in the Lorson Ranch area near Colorado Springs, Colorado

sources.title: Colorado Court of Appeals - People v. Stauch, 2026COA22 (opinion)
CBS News Colorado - Colorado woman's conviction for murder of stepson reversed, juror biased
KRDO - Letecia Stauch's overturned murder conviction appealed to the state Supreme Court
KKTV - Department of Law files appeal in Letecia Stauch case
KRDO - Letecia Stauch found guilty on all counts; sentenced to life without parole
CBS News Colorado - Letecia Stauch guilty on all counts

Wikipedia - Disappearance and murder of Gannon Stauch

narrative: Gannon Stauch, 11, was reported missing on January 27, 2020, from his family's home in the Lorson Ranch neighborhood near Colorado Springs, according to KRDO. Wikipedia's account of the case says his stepmother, Letecia Stauch, told authorities that he had left that afternoon to walk to a friend's house.

Investigators arrested Letecia Stauch on March 2, 2020, on a first-degree murder charge, Colorado Public Radio reported; Wikipedia gives the place of arrest as Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. On March 17, 2020, Gannon's body was found in a suitcase under a bridge in the Florida Panhandle, according to KRDO, which reported that the autopsy documented a gunshot wound, stab wounds and a skull fracture. CBS News Colorado reported that prosecutors also presented evidence of Gannon's blood on a piece of particle board found in a rural area and on the defendant's shoe.

Stauch pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, arguing that she had dissociative identity disorder. Her trial in El Paso County District Court, before Judge Gregory Werner, began in March 2023. On May 8, 2023, the jury rejected the insanity defense and found her guilty of first-degree murder after deliberation, first-degree murder of a child under 12 by a person in a position of trust, tampering with a deceased human body and tampering with physical evidence, according to KRDO and CBS News Colorado. She was sentenced to life in prison without parole, with additional consecutive terms for the tampering counts.

On April 2, 2026, a division of the Colorado Court of Appeals reversed the convictions and ordered a new trial. The published opinion, People v. Stauch, 2026COA22, held that the trial court committed structural error when it denied a defense challenge for cause to a prospective juror who then deliberated. News reports identified the juror as the relative by marriage of a deputy district attorney in the office that prosecuted the case; Colorado law requires removal of jurors related within the third degree to an attorney in the case. One judge dissented in part, concluding the defense had waived the issue. The court separately rejected Stauch's challenge to a search warrant.

The Colorado Department of Law petitioned the Colorado Supreme Court on June 29, 2026, to review the reversal, KKTV and KRDO reported. As of those July 2026 reports the court had not said whether it would take the case. If it declines, the case returns to the 4th Judicial District, where the district attorney's office has said it is prepared to try the case before a new jury. Stauch remains in custody. Because the convictions have been reversed, she is currently presumed innocent of the charges pending any retrial or reinstatement of the verdict.

name: Pamela Butler
summary: Pamela Butler, a 47-year-old Environmental Protection Agency analyst, vanished from her Washington, D.C. home in February 2009. Her boyfriend Jose Rodriguez-Cruz was arrested in 2017, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 12 years in prison. Her remains have never been recovered.

narrative: On February 12, 2009, forty-seven-year-old Pamela Butler, a computer analyst with the Environmental Protection Agency, was last seen at her home in northwest Washington, D.C. When she failed to report to work, colleagues became concerned and contacted police.

Police found Butler's home undisturbed, with her car, purse, and personal belongings still inside. Her three cats were found unattended. Despite a thorough investigation, no trace of Pamela was found for years.

Her boyfriend, Jose Rodriguez-Cruz, was arrested in April 2017. He admitted strangling Pamela in her home during an argument and said he buried her beside Interstate 95 in Virginia; the site had since been built over and her remains could not be recovered.

Rodriguez-Cruz pleaded guilty to second-degree murder in October 2017 and was sentenced to 12 years in prison. In 2020 he also pleaded guilty to the 1989 killing of his wife, Marta Rodriguez-Cruz. The case highlighted the challenges of solving missing person cases when the victim's body cannot be found.

name: Lori Hacking
summary: Lori Hacking, 27, was shot at her Salt Lake City apartment on July 19, 2004 by her husband, Mark Hacking, who reported her missing the same morning. He had invented a college degree and a medical school place. Her remains were found in the county landfill on October 1, 2004. He pleaded guilty to murder in April 2005 and was sentenced to six years to life.
lastSeen: July 19, 2004, her apartment in Salt Lake City, Utah

sources.title: Deseret News - Tearful ending: Mark Hacking gets 6-to-life prison term
Deseret News - 10 years after murder, Lori Hacking's mother forgives, but 'will never get over it'

Oxygen - Mark Hacking, Fake Medical Student, Told A Lie Worth Killing For
Wikipedia - Murder of Lori Hacking

narrative: Lori Hacking, 27, worked for Wells Fargo in Salt Lake City and had been married to Mark Hacking for five years. According to the Deseret News, she was about five weeks pregnant in July 2004. Mark Hacking had told those around him that he had been accepted to a medical programme at the University of North Carolina, according to Oxygen's account of the case.

On the morning of July 19, 2004, Mark Hacking called 911 and reported that his wife had not returned from a jog in the Memory Grove area. Hundreds of volunteers joined a search that drew national attention, KSL reported. The Deseret News later reported that on the day he made the report he had bought a new mattress, and that in the early hours of July 20 police found him unclothed outside a hotel, after which he was admitted to a psychiatric unit.

Investigators established that his account of his own life was false. According to the Deseret News, he had never graduated from the University of Utah and had not been admitted to any medical school. On July 24, 2004 he told his brothers that he had killed Lori and put her body in a trash bin, and the family passed this on through his attorney. Wikipedia's account of the case gives the date of his arrest as August 2, 2004, with a first-degree murder charge filed a week later.

Police searched the Salt Lake County landfill for weeks. Lori Hacking's remains were found there on October 1, 2004. Mark Hacking initially pleaded not guilty. On April 15, 2005 he pleaded guilty to first-degree felony murder, and, as reported at the time, admitted in court that he had intentionally shot his wife in the head with a .22 rifle on July 19, 2004. Obstruction of justice counts were dismissed as part of the plea.

On June 6, 2005, Third District Judge Denise Lindberg sentenced him to six years to life in prison, which was then the maximum term available under Utah law for the offence, and said he should serve a very long time. In Utah the Board of Pardons and Parole decides how long an inmate is actually held; in July 2005 the board said it would not consider him for parole until 2035.

The length of the minimum term prompted a change in state law. Utah legislators raised the minimum sentence for murder to 15 years to life in a measure known as Lori's Law, the Deseret News reported in a ten-year retrospective in which Lori's mother spoke about her daughter.

name: Leigh Matthews
summary: Leigh Matthews, a 21-year-old student, was kidnapped from the Bond University campus parking lot in Johannesburg on July 9, 2004. Her father paid a R50,000 ransom, but she was shot dead; her body was found near Walkerville on July 21. Donovan Moodley pleaded guilty in July 2005 and is serving life imprisonment. He was refused parole in December 2025.
lastSeen: July 9, 2004, Bond University campus parking lot, Morningside, Sandton, Johannesburg

sources.title: Wikipedia - Murder of Leigh Matthews
Eyewitness News - Family of Leigh Matthews hits out at parole board for recommending her killer's release

narrative: Leigh Matthews was a 21-year-old student reading for a BCom degree in finance at Bond University's South African campus in Morningside, Sandton, in Johannesburg. She had turned 21 the day before she was taken. According to the account summarised by Wikipedia, she was abducted from the university parking lot on Friday, July 9, 2004.

A ransom demand was made to her father, Rob Matthews, shortly afterwards. He left R50,000 at a drop-off point near the Grasmere toll plaza, south of Johannesburg. His daughter was not released. Her body was found on July 21, 2004, in open veld near Walkerville, close to the R82 road. She had been shot four times.
The investigation was later taken over by the detective Piet Byleveld. Police arrested Donovan Moodley, then 24 and also a Bond University student, on October 4, 2004.

Moodley pleaded guilty in the Johannesburg High Court on July 25, 2005, to murder, kidnapping and extortion, and was convicted on his plea. On August 4, 2005, he was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder, 15 years for the kidnapping and 10 years for the extortion. According to Wikipedia, he subsequently tried several times to have the conviction or sentence set aside, and the courts dismissed each attempt, the last in February 2012. Because the guilty plea meant the evidence was never tested at trial, Byleveld's stated belief that Moodley had not acted alone was never examined in court. No one else has been charged.

Moodley has applied for parole several times without success, according to Eyewitness News, which reported that on September 15, 2025, the Correctional Supervision and Parole Board recommended his release. Rob Matthews criticised the recommendation, saying the board had considered records covering only about a year and a half of Moodley's time in custody.

The recommendation still required review by the National Council for Correctional Services and a decision by the minister. In December 2025 the Department of Correctional Services announced that the minister, Pieter Groenewald, acting on the council's advice, had declined to grant parole. According to Eyewitness News, Moodley must complete further programmes before a new application can be considered, which is expected to take at least two years. He remains in prison.

name: Erica Parsons
summary: Erica Parsons, 13, of Rowan County, North Carolina, died in December 2011 but was not reported missing until July 30, 2013. Her remains were found near Pageland, South Carolina, in September 2016. Her adoptive mother, Casey Parsons, pleaded guilty to first-degree murder in August 2019 and received life without parole; her adoptive father, Sandy Parsons, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder that December.
lastSeen: November 2011, Salisbury, North Carolina

sources.title: Salisbury Post - Plea puts Casey Parsons in prison for life
Salisbury Post - Erica Parsons' adoptive dad to serve minimum of 33 years for murder, abuse, obstruction

Salisbury Post - Casey Parsons to begin life sentence for murder of adoptive daughter
Wikipedia - Murder of Erica Parsons

narrative: Erica Parsons was born in February 1998 and was raised from infancy by Sandy and Casey Parsons, relatives of her biological mother, who formally adopted her in 2000, according to Wikipedia's summary of court and news records. The family lived in Rowan County, near Salisbury, North Carolina.

Authorities said Erica was last seen by people outside the household in November 2011, when she was 13. According to the Salisbury Post's account of later court proceedings, she died on December 17, 2011, and her body was taken to South Carolina and buried in a shallow grave. No one reported her missing until July 30, 2013, when her adoptive brother Jamie Parsons went to the Rowan County Sheriff's Office. Her adoptive parents told investigators she had gone to live with a grandmother; CBS News reported that the sheriff later said the name and relationship they gave were not correct.

While the search continued, federal prosecutors charged the couple with fraud for continuing to collect adoption assistance and other government benefits after Erica was no longer in the home. Casey Parsons pleaded guilty to 15 federal counts and was sentenced to ten years. Sandy Parsons was found guilty at trial in 2014 and sentenced to eight years, according to CBS News.

On September 27, 2016, investigators from the sheriff's office and the FBI located skeletal remains in a rural area near Pageland, in Chesterfield County, South Carolina. The Salisbury Post reported that Sandy Parsons's cooperation led them to the site. The remains were identified as Erica's days later. The medical examiner ruled that she died of homicidal violence of undetermined means and documented malnutrition and multiple fractures in different stages of healing, the Salisbury Post reported.

A Rowan County grand jury indicted both adoptive parents on February 19, 2018, on charges of first-degree murder, felony child abuse, concealment of death and obstruction of justice. On August 2, 2019, Casey Parsons pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and the related charges and was sentenced to life in prison without parole. On December 17, 2019, Sandy Parsons pleaded guilty to second-degree murder, child abuse, concealment of death and obstruction of justice, and was sentenced to between roughly 33 and 43 and a half years. In court he acknowledged having turned a blind eye to the abuse, according to the Salisbury Post.

Both state sentences were ordered to follow the federal terms. The Salisbury Post reported in November 2023 that Casey Parsons had completed her federal sentence and was beginning her life term, and that Sandy Parsons was already in state custody with a projected release date in 2057.

name: Shannan Gilbert
summary: Shannan Gilbert disappeared at Oak Beach, Long Island on May 1, 2010; the search for her led to the discovery of the Gilgo Beach victims. Her remains were found in December 2011 and her cause of death is officially undetermined. Rex Heuermann pleaded guilty in April 2026 to seven Gilgo Beach murders, but he was never charged in Gilbert's death.
lastSeen: May 1, 2010, Oak Beach, Long Island, New York

sources.title: Shannan Gilbert - Wikipedia
Rex Heuermann arrest - NBC News
Wikipedia - Gilgo Beach serial killings

narrative: On May 1, 2010, twenty-four-year-old Shannan Gilbert, a sex worker from Jersey City, arrived at the Oak Beach community on Long Island's barrier island for an appointment arranged through Craigslist. During the encounter, she became distressed and fled the client's home, banging on neighbors' doors and making a frantic 911 call before running into the nearby marshland.

Shannan was never seen alive again. The search for her led police to make a shocking discovery: beginning in December 2010, investigators found the remains of multiple other victims along Ocean Parkway near Gilgo Beach, eventually uncovering at least 10 sets of human remains, revealing a serial killer had been operating on Long Island.

Shannan's body was found in the marsh near Oak Beach in December 2011. Her death was initially attributed to accidental drowning, though her family disputed this finding and believed she was a victim of the serial killer.

In July 2023, Rex Heuermann, an architect from Massapequa Park, was arrested in the Gilgo Beach case. He pleaded guilty to seven murders on April 8, 2026 and was sentenced on June 17, 2026 to seven consecutive life sentences without parole. He was not charged in connection with Shannan Gilbert, whose cause of death remains officially undetermined.

summary: Lena Chapin, 20, was last seen on February 14, 2006, at her apartment outside Steelville, Missouri. Relatives say she had described witnessing the 1999 death of her stepfather, Gary McCullough, who is also missing. In 2013 a civil jury found her mother, Sandy Klemp, and Kris Klemp liable for McCullough's death; no criminal charges have been filed in either case.
lastSeen: February 14, 2006, at her apartment outside Steelville, Missouri

sources.title: The Salem News - After 10 years missing, is Lena Chapin still alive?
The Salem News - Chapin disappearance back in focus after Unsolved Mysteries premiere

narrative: Liehnia May Chapin, known as Lena, was born in 1985 and grew up in the Salem area of Dent County, Missouri. According to The Salem News, she attended Salem High School and worked as a cake decorator at grocery stores in Salem and Steelville. By early 2006 she was 20, the mother of a young son, and living with her fiance in an apartment outside Steelville.

The Salem News reports that her fiance told detectives he left for work on the morning of February 14, 2006, and that when he came back that evening Chapin was gone and her mother was at the apartment removing belongings. Chapin has not been seen since. She was not formally reported missing for years: The Salem News states that the Dent County Sheriff's Office opened its file in March 2012, while Oxygen reports that her absence came to official attention in 2008, when she could not be located to testify in a lawsuit.

That lawsuit concerned her stepfather, Gary McCullough, who disappeared on May 11, 1999, from a ranch outside Cassville in Barry County. His truck was found several days later and he was declared legally dead in 2005, according to The Salem News. Relatives have said that Chapin told them she had seen what happened to McCullough. In a recorded conversation with McCullough's brother Albert, she said that her mother had killed him and that she had been made to help afterward, Oxygen reported. These are allegations; they have never been tested in a criminal court.

McCullough's family brought a wrongful-death suit against Chapin's mother, Sandy Klemp, and Kris Klemp. In 2013 a Stone County jury found both liable and awarded $7 million. The Salem News notes that Chapin's recorded statement was not presented to that jury, and that she had been summoned as a witness but was never served. A civil finding of liability is not a criminal conviction, and no one has been charged with a crime in connection with either disappearance. Oxygen reported that Sandy Klemp has declined to discuss the case publicly.

The case was featured in the Netflix revival of Unsolved Mysteries in 2020, in an episode titled Missing Witness. After it aired, a Dent County detective told The Salem News that the office had received new inquiries and was processing the information. The newspaper also reported that ground-penetrating radar had been used to search properties in Dent County.

No trace of Lena Chapin or Gary McCullough has been found, and no later developments were identified during this review. Chapin remains listed as a missing person by the Missouri State Highway Patrol, according to Oxygen. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Dent County Sheriff's Office.

name: Sandra Cantu
summary: Eight-year-old Sandra Cantu disappeared from the Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park in Tracy, California, on March 27, 2009. Her body was found ten days later in a suitcase in an irrigation pond. Neighbor Melissa Huckaby, a former Sunday school teacher, pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and kidnapping in May 2010 and was sentenced to life in prison without parole on June 14, 2010.
lastSeen: March 27, 2009, Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park, Tracy, California

sources.title: CNN - Huckaby gets life without parole in killing of daughter's playmate
ABC News - Melissa Huckaby Pleads Guilty to Sandra Cantu's Murder
NBC Bay Area - Melissa Huckaby Sentenced Monday
Wikipedia - Murder of Sandra Cantu

narrative: Sandra Cantu was an eight-year-old second grader who lived with her family at the Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park in Tracy, California. She disappeared from the park on March 27, 2009. According to the Wikipedia summary of the case, she was last recorded on the afternoon of that day near her home and was reported missing that evening, which prompted a large search of the area by police and volunteers.

Ten days later, on April 6, 2009, her body was found inside a suitcase recovered from an irrigation pond on a dairy farm. NBC Bay Area reported that the pond was about two miles from her home. CNN likewise reported that the suitcase was found in a pond ten days after the girl vanished.

Police arrested Melissa Huckaby, then 28, a neighbor in the same mobile home park whose young daughter was a playmate of Sandra's. ABC News reported that Huckaby was a former Sunday school teacher who lived with her grandparents and her daughter, and that her grandfather was the pastor of a nearby church. Prosecutors charged her with murder, kidnapping, lewd and lascivious acts on a child under 14, and rape by instrument, according to CNN, and the special circumstances alleged made her eligible for the death penalty. She initially pleaded not guilty. A gag order kept most of the evidence, including autopsy results, sealed while the case was pending.

On May 10, 2010, Huckaby changed her plea. According to ABC News and CNN, she pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and kidnapping and admitted the special circumstance of murder committed during a kidnapping, in an agreement that removed the possibility of a death sentence. The remaining charges, including the sexual assault allegations, were dropped as part of the plea agreement.

On June 14, 2010, San Joaquin County Superior Court Judge Linda Lofthus sentenced Huckaby, then 29, to life in prison without the possibility of parole, CNN reported. In court she apologized to the Cantu family, said that she alone was responsible for the girl's death, and said she could not explain why she had done it. She denied having sexually molested the child. The judge lifted the gag order at the hearing and said she would consider unsealing case documents.

NBC Bay Area reported that, according to a probation report, Huckaby claimed the girl had climbed into the suitcase as part of a game and that she later found her unresponsive; that account was her own and was not a finding of the court. Huckaby's conviction rests on her guilty plea, and no motive was established in court.

name: Ahmaud Arbery
summary: Ahmaud Arbery was chased and shot dead while jogging in Brunswick, Georgia by three white men. The case sparked national outrage over racial violence. All three were convicted of murder.
lastSeen: February 23, 2020, Satilla Shores neighborhood, Brunswick, Georgia

sources.title: Murder of Ahmaud Arbery - Wikipedia

narrative: On February 23, 2020, twenty-five-year-old Ahmaud Marquez Arbery was jogging through the Satilla Shores neighborhood near Brunswick, Georgia, when he was pursued by three white men in pickup trucks. Gregory McMichael, his son Travis McMichael, and their neighbor William 'Roddie' Bryan Jr. chased Arbery for several minutes before Travis McMichael fatally shot him with a shotgun.

The McMichaels claimed they suspected Arbery of committing burglaries in the neighborhood and were attempting a citizen's arrest. Bryan filmed the confrontation on his cellphone. Despite the video evidence, no arrests were made for over two months, as local prosecutors initially declined to press charges.

The cellphone video was leaked in May 2020, sparking national outrage and protests. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation took over the case, and all three men were arrested and charged with murder. The case became part of a broader national reckoning about racial violence and the criminal justice system.

In November 2021, all three defendants were found guilty of murder in state court. Travis McMichael and his father received life sentences without parole; Bryan received life with the possibility of parole. All three were subsequently convicted of federal hate crimes in February 2022.

summary: Pilot and flight instructor Kelsey Berreth was murdered on Thanksgiving Day by her fiancé Patrick Frazee in Woodland Park, Colorado. He burned her body. Frazee was sentenced to life.

narrative: On November 22, 2018, Thanksgiving Day, twenty-nine-year-old Kelsey Berreth, a pilot and flight instructor, was last seen on surveillance video entering a Woodland Park, Colorado Safeway store with her one-year-old daughter Kaylee. She was never seen again.

Kelsey's fiancé Patrick Frazee reported her missing on December 2 after her employer raised concerns. Text messages had been sent from Kelsey's phone for several days after her disappearance, leading investigators to initially believe she was alive. However, the texts had been sent by Frazee's girlfriend, Krystal Lee Kenney, at his direction.

Kenney became a key cooperating witness. She testified that Frazee had bludgeoned Kelsey to death with a baseball bat at her townhome and then enlisted Kenney to clean the crime scene and help dispose of the body, which was burned on Frazee's ranch. Kelsey's remains were never recovered.

Frazee was convicted of first-degree murder, solicitation of murder, and tampering with a body in November 2019. He was sentenced to life in prison without parole plus 156 years. Kenney pleaded guilty to tampering with evidence and was sentenced to three years.

narrative: On November 19, 2012, thirteen-year-old Dylan Redwine traveled from his mother's home in Colorado Springs to his father Mark Redwine's home near Bayfield, Colorado, for a court-ordered Thanksgiving visit. Dylan and his father had a strained relationship. Mark reported Dylan missing the following day.

The investigation focused on Mark Redwine, who had been the last person to see Dylan alive. Evidence revealed that Dylan had found disturbing photographs on his father's computer and had confronted him about them, providing a possible motive.

name: Heather Elvis
summary: Heather Elvis, 20, disappeared in Horry County, South Carolina, on December 18, 2013; her car was found at Peachtree Landing. Tammy Moorer (October 2018) and Sidney Moorer (September 2019) were each convicted of kidnapping and conspiracy and sentenced to 30 years. Murder charges were dropped in March 2016, and Elvis has never been found.
lastSeen: December 18, 2013, Horry County, South Carolina; her car was found at Peachtree Landing in Socastee

narrative: Heather Elvis was 20 years old when she disappeared in Horry County, South Carolina, in the early hours of December 18, 2013. According to the Wikipedia summary of the case, she lived in the Carolina Forest area and worked at restaurants in the Myrtle Beach area. She had been out on a date that evening and was dropped off at home at about 1:15 a.m.; she later spoke to her roommate by phone. Her car was found parked at Peachtree Landing, a boat ramp in the Socastee area. WMBF News reports the car was there by about 4 a.m. on December 18, while Wikipedia dates the discovery to December 19.

According to WMBF News, Elvis had been in a relationship with Sidney Moorer, a married man, from about July 2013 until late October or early November of that year. Prosecutors later argued that Sidney Moorer and his wife, Tammy Moorer, lured Elvis to the landing. The evidence described in the South Carolina Court of Appeals ruling, as reported by WMBF, included cellphone location data, surveillance video of a truck resembling the couple's travelling to and from the landing, and store video of Sidney Moorer buying a pregnancy test that morning.

Both Moorers were arrested on February 21, 2014, and charged with murder, kidnapping and other offences, according to Wikipedia. The murder charges were dismissed in March 2016; ABC News 4 attributed the dismissal to insufficient evidence. Sidney Moorer's first kidnapping trial, in 2016, ended with a jury unable to reach a verdict. In 2017 he was convicted of obstruction of justice and given a 10-year sentence.

On October 23, 2018, a jury found Tammy Moorer guilty of kidnapping and conspiracy to kidnap, and she received concurrent 30-year sentences, ABC News 4 reported. On September 18, 2019, a Horry County jury convicted Sidney Moorer of the same two charges at his retrial after roughly two hours of deliberation, and he was also sentenced to 30 years, according to WMBF News. Neither has been convicted of killing Elvis, and both have maintained that they were wrongly convicted.

The South Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed both convictions on June 7, 2023. WIS-TV reported that the state Supreme Court declined to review Sidney Moorer's case in April 2024 and Tammy Moorer's on October 3, 2024. Sidney Moorer filed an application for post-conviction relief in March 2025, and Tammy Moorer filed her own in early October 2025, each seeking a new trial. No ruling on either application was found during this review.

Heather Elvis has never been located. At Sidney Moorer's sentencing her father, Terry Elvis, told the court that nobody would tell the family where she was. Official projected release dates cited by local media are May 2043 for Tammy Moorer and March 2044 for Sidney Moorer.

name: Alissa Turney
summary: Alissa Turney, 17, disappeared in Phoenix on May 17, 2001, the last day of her junior year at Paradise Valley High School, and has never been found. Her stepfather, Michael Turney, was charged with second-degree murder in 2020. On July 18, 2023, a judge granted a judgment of acquittal during his trial, finding the evidence insufficient. He has denied any involvement.
lastSeen: May 17, 2001, Paradise Valley High School, Phoenix, Arizona

sources.title: NBC News (Dateline) - Charges dismissed against Michael Turney in connection with 17-year-old stepdaughter Alissa Turney's 2001 disappearance
ABC News - What happened to Arizona teen Alissa Turney, who disappeared in 2001
ABC News - 19 years after teen disappeared, stepfather arrested and charged with murder
Silent Witness - Missing Person / Suspicious Circumstance: Alissa Turney
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Alissa Turney

narrative: Alissa Turney was 17 when she disappeared on May 17, 2001, the last day of her junior year at Paradise Valley High School in Phoenix, Arizona. Her stepfather, Michael Turney, who according to Wikipedia's account had adopted her, reported her missing. He told police he had found a note in her room saying she was leaving for California. ABC News reported that he also said he received a phone call about a week later from a payphone in Riverside, California. Phoenix police initially treated the case as a runaway.

Investigators later pointed to circumstances that did not fit that explanation. According to ABC News, Alissa left behind her cellphone, personal items such as her hairbrush and makeup, and about $1,800 in a bank account that was never touched. Silent Witness, the Phoenix-area tip program, lists her case as a missing person under suspicious circumstances.

ABC News reported that detectives took a fresh look at the case after a Florida inmate made a confession in 2006 that proved to be false. NBC News reported that the Phoenix Police Department's Missing Persons Unit reopened the investigation in 2008 and concluded that foul play was involved. During a search of Michael Turney's home that year, police found more than two dozen explosive devices and 19 firearms, according to ABC News. Wikipedia's account says he was prosecuted over the devices, sentenced to 10 years and released in 2017. That case was separate from Alissa's disappearance.

Alissa's younger half-sister, Sarah Turney, campaigned publicly for charges, including through a podcast and social media posts that drew wide attention. In August 2020, Michael Turney, then 72, was arrested in Mesa, Arizona, after a Maricopa County grand jury indicted him for second-degree murder. He denied the allegations made against him, including claims reported by ABC News that Alissa had told a friend of attempted abuse.

The case went to trial in Phoenix in July 2023. According to NBC News, prosecutors rested on July 17 after five days of testimony, and the defense argued that the state had no physical evidence that Alissa was dead or that Michael Turney had caused her death. On July 18, 2023, Judge Sam Myers granted a defense motion for a judgment of acquittal under Rule 20 of the Arizona Rules of Criminal Procedure. ABC News quoted the judge as finding that substantial evidence did not exist to warrant a conviction. The Maricopa County Attorney's Office said it disagreed with the ruling but respected it.

Michael Turney was therefore not convicted, and no one else has been charged. Alissa Turney remains missing, and Silent Witness continues to ask for information under Phoenix police case number 2001-928.

name: Brian Carrick
summary: Brian Carrick, 17, vanished on December 20, 2002 after walking into Val's Foods, the Johnsburg, Illinois grocery store where he worked. His blood was found in and around a produce cooler, but his body has never been located. Co-worker Mario Casciaro was convicted of murder in 2013; an appellate court reversed the conviction in 2015 for insufficient evidence and he was released.
lastSeen: December 20, 2002, Val's Foods grocery store, Johnsburg, Illinois

sources.title: ABC News - What Happened to Brian Carrick? Unsolved Case of Illinois Teen Missing for 12 Years
ABC News - Mario Casciaro, Whose Murder Conviction in Missing Teen's Death Was Overturned
Northwest Herald (Shaw Local) - Brian Carrick, 17-year-old Johnsburg boy, remains missing 20 years
Wikipedia - Mario Casciaro

narrative: Brian Carrick was a 17-year-old junior at Johnsburg High School in McHenry County, Illinois. According to ABC News, he was the 11th of 14 children, and his family lived on Johnsburg Road across the street from Val's Foods, the town's grocery store, where he and several of his siblings worked as stock clerks.

December 20, 2002 was his day off, but ABC News reported that he went to the store that evening, passing his brother on the way in. The Northwest Herald places the last sighting at about 6:45 p.m. His mother learned the next day that he had not turned up for work. Hundreds of volunteers and several police agencies searched the area, and the store offered a $25,000 reward. According to the Northwest Herald, blood identified as Carrick's was found in and around the store's produce cooler and on boxes in a compactor behind the building, and investigators concluded that a crime had taken place in the cooler.

Investigators came to believe the disappearance was connected to a drug debt, ABC News reported. Mario Casciaro, a fellow stock clerk whose father co-owned the store, was charged with perjury in 2007 over his grand jury testimony and was acquitted in 2009. Another employee, Robert Render, was charged with concealing a homicide; that charge was dropped, and he died in 2012, according to ABC News.

In 2010 a third former employee, Shane Lamb, who was facing a prison term in a cocaine case, gave prosecutors a statement in exchange for immunity and a reduced sentence. He said Casciaro had asked him to confront Carrick about money and that he had struck Carrick. Casciaro was charged with murder in February 2010. His first murder trial ended with a hung jury in 2012. A second jury convicted him in April 2013 of first-degree murder by intimidation, and he was sentenced to 26 years. Casciaro has always maintained his innocence.

Lamb recanted in 2014, saying his account had been false. On September 17, 2015, the Illinois Second District Appellate Court unanimously reversed the conviction, finding the evidence too weak to support guilt beyond a reasonable doubt, and Casciaro was released from Menard Correctional Center on September 23, 2015, ABC News reported. According to Wikipedia, the Illinois Supreme Court left the reversal in place in March 2016; Casciaro later filed a civil rights suit, reached settlements with the county state's attorney's office and Johnsburg police, and became a licensed attorney in 2019.

No one stands convicted in the case. Carrick's mother died in 2009 and his father in 2014 without learning where their son is, the Northwest Herald reported on the 20th anniversary of the disappearance. His remains have not been found.

name: Holly Branagan
summary: Seventeen-year-old Moira "Holly" Branagan was stabbed to death in the kitchen of her family's home on Pine Top Trail in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on March 28, 1979. A grand jury reviewed the case from 2010 and police said in 2014 that they had a person of interest, but no one has been charged. In 2025 evidence was resubmitted for DNA testing with help from the Cold Case Foundation.
lastSeen: March 28, 1979, her home on Pine Top Trail, Bethlehem, Pennsylvania

sources.title: CNN - Grand jury dusts off 31 cold cases
NBC10 Philadelphia - DNA collection device could help solve 1979 cold case murder
WFMZ - Police ID suspect in 1979 killing of Bethlehem teenager
NBC10 Philadelphia - Who Killed Holly? 35 Years Later, Theory, No Evidence in Cold Case
6abc - 40 years later, police still hope to solve Holly Branagan murder
NBC10 Philadelphia - Who Killed Holly?
NBC10 Philadelphia - 'Somebody Knows Something' reexamines the murder of Holly Branagan

narrative: Moira "Holly" Branagan was a 17-year-old senior at Freedom High School in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. According to CNN, she sang in the school choir and planned to attend Penn State. Her mother had died of leukemia two years earlier, and she lived with her father and brother in a house on Pine Top Trail.

On March 28, 1979, she was alone in the house. CNN reported that her father was away on business in Atlantic City, New Jersey, and her brother was spending the night with a friend. Shortly before 5 p.m. she was on the telephone with a friend and ended the call by saying that someone was at the door. Her brother found her body on the kitchen floor the following morning. She had been stabbed repeatedly, and the blade of the knife had broken off in her back. NBC10 Philadelphia has reported that she was stabbed 18 times.

No one has ever been charged. NBC10 reported in 2009 that evidence sent to the FBI for analysis had produced no usable results at the time. In February 2010, Northampton County District Attorney John Morganelli presented the case to a special investigative grand jury convened to review about 31 unsolved homicides, CNN reported; Holly Branagan's was the first case it took up. An investigator for the district attorney's office told CNN that evidence collected in 1979 was being examined with newer DNA technology.

In March 2014, Bethlehem Police Chief Mark DiLuzio told WFMZ that, with the help of the grand jury, police had a person of interest, whom he described only as a man who had been an acquaintance of the family in the 1970s. Police did not name him. NBC10 reported at the same time that Morganelli said there was not evidence that would allow an arrest. In 2019 Morganelli told 6abc that retesting with updated DNA methods had still not allowed the case to be concluded, and that much of the crime scene evidence was tainted or no longer existed. According to 6abc, Holly's father, Richard Branagan, died in 2016.

NBC10 re-examined the case in its 2024 documentary series "Somebody Knows Something: Murder on Pine Top Trail." In May 2025, the station reported that Northampton County District Attorney Stephen Baratta and Bethlehem police were working with the Cold Case Foundation, a volunteer nonprofit, and had sent evidence to laboratories for new DNA testing. The effort includes the M-Vac, a wet-vacuum collection device that can recover genetic material from surfaces that swabs cannot reach, such as the handle of the knife. No results or arrests had been announced in the sources reviewed, and the case remains unsolved.

name: Sierah Joughin
summary: Twenty-year-old Sierah Joughin was abducted while bicycling in rural Ohio. James Worley, a convicted kidnapper, was convicted of her murder and sentenced to death.
lastSeen: July 19, 2016, County Road 6, Metamora, Fulton County, Ohio

sources.title: Murder of Sierah Joughin - Wikipedia
James Worley conviction - Toledo Blade
Sierah's Law - Ohio Legislature (archived copy)

narrative: On July 19, 2016, twenty-year-old Sierah Joughin went for a bicycle ride with her boyfriend near her home in rural Fulton County, Ohio. When her boyfriend turned back, Sierah continued riding alone. She never returned.

Sierah's bicycle was found on the road near the farm of James Daniel Worley, a 57-year-old with a 1990 conviction for abducting a woman on a bicycle in the same area. Investigators searched Worley's property and found Sierah's body buried in a shallow grave on his land.
Worley was arrested and charged with aggravated murder and kidnapping. Evidence included motorcycle parts matching a vehicle seen near the abduction site and traces of Sierah's DNA in Worley's home.

Worley was convicted in March 2018 and sentenced to death in April 2018. The case led to the passage of 'Sierah's Law' in Ohio, which created a publicly searchable database of violent offenders, expanding beyond the sex offender registry to include other violent criminals.

name: Mary Agnes Moroney
summary: Two-year-old Mary Agnes Moroney was taken from her family's South Side Chicago apartment on May 15, 1930 by a woman using the name Julia Otis and was never returned. In February 2023, consumer DNA tests linked her relatives to the family of Jeanette Burchard, a Florida nurse who died about 2003. The sheriff's office has not formally confirmed the match, and the abductor was never identified.
lastSeen: May 15, 1930, her family's apartment at 5200 South Wentworth Avenue, Chicago, Illinois

sources.title: Chicago Sun-Times - Mystery of missing Chicago girl Mary Agnes Moroney may be finally solved
Chicago Sun-Times - Mary Agnes Moroney case: Cook County sheriff's detective apparently solved mystery
WBEZ - Whatever happened to Mary Agnes Moroney? DNA tests appear to solve 1930s mystery of missing Chicago girl
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Mary Agnes Moroney

narrative: Mary Agnes Moroney was born on May 10, 1928 and lived with her parents, Michael and Katherine Moroney, in an apartment above a grocery store at 5200 South Wentworth Avenue on Chicago's South Side. According to the Chicago Sun-Times, her mother was 17 at the time and the family had very little money.

In May 1930 a woman who gave her name as Julia Otis visited the family, bringing food and gifts. On May 15, 1930 she asked to take the two-year-old out to buy clothing. The Sun-Times, citing family accounts, reports that the child was upset and did not want to go. The woman left with her and did not come back.

The family then received two letters. The first, in the name of Julia Otis, said the girl had been taken to California and would be brought back. The second was signed Alice Henderson, who described herself as Otis's cousin and wrote that Otis had lost her own husband and child. According to Wikipedia's summary of the case, investigators concluded that both letters were in the same handwriting. No one was ever charged.

The case returned to the news several times. In 1952 the Chicago Daily News reported that a 24-year-old woman, Mary McClelland, was the missing child, but Katherine Moroney did not accept her as her daughter, and the Sun-Times reports that DNA testing in 2008 showed McClelland was not related. Another woman located in 2018 was also ruled out by DNA. Michael Moroney died in 1957 and Katherine Moroney in 1962.

In June 2022 the case was assigned to Detective Jose Rodriguez of the Cook County Sheriff's Office under its missing persons project. According to the Sun-Times and WBEZ, consumer DNA tests then showed a cousin-level relationship between members of the Moroney family and Terri Arnold of Florida, whose mother, Jeanette Burchard, had been told by her stepfather that the woman who raised her was not her birth mother. Burchard's family records gave her birth date as April 14, 1928. She grew up partly in Chicago, worked as a nurse for more than 50 years, had three children and died in Florida at 75.

The findings were reported on February 17, 2023. Both families said they accepted that Burchard was Mary Agnes Moroney. The sheriff's office said it could not formally confirm the identification without exhuming Burchard and Katherine Moroney, and Arnold declined. The person who took the child has never been identified.

The family receives letters signed Julia Otis and Alice Henderson saying the child will be returned.

name: Rui Pedro
summary: Eleven-year-old Rui Pedro Teixeira Mendonça disappeared from Lousada, Portugal on March 4, 1998. Afonso Dias, acquitted at a first trial in 2012, was later convicted of kidnapping and sentenced to three years in prison; he was released in 2017. Rui Pedro has never been found and was declared legally dead in 2019.
lastSeen: March 4, 1998, Lousada, Porto District, Portugal

sources.title: Rui Pedro - Polícia Judiciária
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Rui Pedro Teixeira Mendonça

narrative: On March 4, 1998, eleven-year-old Rui Pedro Teixeira Mendonça disappeared from the town of Lousada in northern Portugal. The boy had been last seen in the company of a known local man, Afonso Dias, who was later convicted of kidnapping.

The investigation revealed deeply disturbing connections to a pedophilia network. A photograph allegedly showing Rui Pedro was found during an Interpol operation targeting child exploitation websites, but the identification was never conclusively confirmed.

Afonso Dias was acquitted at his first trial in 2012 but was subsequently convicted of kidnapping Rui Pedro and sentenced to three years in prison; he was released in March 2017 and never revealed the boy's whereabouts. The case became a national sensation in Portugal and exposed failures in the child protection system.
The case of Rui Pedro remains one of Portugal's most painful unsolved mysteries. It contributed to significant reforms in how Portugal handles missing children cases and child protection legislation.

name: Cheryl Grimmer
summary: Three-year-old Cheryl Grimmer was taken from outside the shower block at Fairy Meadow Beach, Wollongong, on January 12, 1970. A man was charged in 2017, but prosecutors dropped the case in 2019 after his 1971 confession, made as a teenager, was ruled inadmissible. In 2025 the case was included in a NSW parliamentary inquiry and in 2026 the DPP announced a review.
lastSeen: January 12, 1970, Fairy Meadow Beach, Wollongong, New South Wales, Australia

sources.title: Disappearance of Cheryl Grimmer - Wikipedia

narrative: On January 12, 1970, the Grimmer family, recent British immigrants to Australia, visited Fairy Meadow Beach near Wollongong, New South Wales. Three-year-old Cheryl went into a shower and changing block with her three older brothers. When the boys came out, Cheryl was gone.
A witness reportedly saw a man carrying a small child from the area, but the description was vague. Despite an immediate search and widespread publicity, Cheryl was never found.

The case lay dormant for decades until renewed investigation in the 2010s. In 2017, a man was arrested and charged with Cheryl's murder based on a witness statement from the 1970s. However, the charges were dismissed when the court ruled that the suspect's interview as a teenager in 1971 was inadmissible.
Cheryl Grimmer's disappearance remains one of Australia's most enduring cold cases. Her family, including her brothers who were present at the time, have continued to seek answers.

timeline.event: Cheryl Grimmer snatched from a beach shower block in Wollongong.
Suspect arrested but charges later dismissed.

name: Haleigh Cummings
summary: Five-year-old Haleigh Cummings was last seen on the evening of February 9, 2009, at her father's mobile home in Satsuma, Florida, and was reported missing early the next morning. The Putnam County Sheriff's Office said in April 2010 that it believed she was dead and treats the case as an unsolved homicide. She has never been found and no one has been charged.
lastSeen: February 9, 2009, her father's mobile home, Satsuma, Florida

sources.title: ABC News - Police Say 5-Year-Old Haleigh Cummings is Dead, Identify Persons of Interest
CNN - Cousins questioned in Haleigh search
WUFT - 7 Years Later, HaLeigh Cummings' Memory Still Rings In Putnam County
News4Jax - 11 years later: Still no trace of HaLeigh Cummings
News4Jax - St. Johns County sheriff brings attention to unsolved HaLeigh Cummings case
Yahoo News / Action News Jax - 'We do not forget:' 16 years since Haleigh Cummings' disappearance in Putnam County
WCJB - Over a decade later, HaLeigh Cummings still missing

narrative: Haleigh Ann-Marie Cummings, a kindergarten pupil, lived with her father, Ronald Cummings, in the Hermits Cove area of Satsuma in Putnam County, Florida. According to News4Jax, she was last known to be asleep on the evening of February 9, 2009, beside her younger brother, while her father worked an evening shift and his 17-year-old girlfriend, Misty Croslin, looked after the children.

CNN reported that Croslin told police she put the children to bed at about 8 p.m., went to sleep about two hours later, and woke at about 3 a.m. to find Haleigh gone and a cinder block propping open a back door. Haleigh was reported missing on February 10 and an AMBER Alert was issued. WUFT reported that law enforcement at local, state and federal level took part, that the volunteer group Texas EquuSearch organised search parties, and that about 1,000 people joined searches over several weeks.

Investigators said in August 2009 that the evidence had reduced the likelihood that a stranger was responsible, according to CNN, and that Haleigh's father and her mother, Crystal Sheffield, were not considered suspects. CNN also reported that authorities said physical evidence contradicted Croslin's account of the night and that she had not given a detailed account of those hours, while stopping short of naming her a suspect. Croslin has said in interviews that she does not know what happened.

Croslin and Ronald Cummings married after the disappearance and later separated. In January 2010 both were arrested with three other people in an undercover drug investigation that authorities described as separate from the missing-child case. WUFT, citing the Florida Department of Corrections, reported that Cummings received 15 years and Croslin 25 years for drug trafficking. Action News Jax reported that Cummings was released in October 2022 and arrested again that December on unrelated allegations.

In April 2010, divers and deputies searched the St. Johns River near Satsuma for several days. ABC News reported that Sheriff Jeff Hardy then announced that information received had led investigators to believe Haleigh was most likely dead, that the case was a homicide investigation, and that several unnamed persons of interest had been identified. No arrest followed.

Haleigh has not been found, and neither Croslin nor Cummings has been charged in connection with her disappearance. Her case is listed among Florida's unsolved AMBER Alerts, and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children has issued several age-progression images, the most recent in September 2024. The Putnam County Sheriff's Office continues to ask anyone with information to come forward.

name: Elsie Paroubek
summary: Elsie Paroubek, a Chicago girl of four or five, disappeared on April 8, 1911, while walking to her aunt's house. A month later her body was recovered from the drainage canal near Lockport, about 35 miles away. An inquest concluded she had probably been suffocated, though the official cause was recorded as unknown. No one was charged. Her photograph later figured in the work of artist Henry Darger.
lastSeen: April 8, 1911, near her home on South Albany Avenue, Chicago, Illinois

sources.title: Wikipedia - Elsie Paroubek
The Lineup - Elsie Paroubek
Grunge - The Bizarre Case Of Elsie Paroubek's Kidnapping
Wikipedia - In the Realms of the Unreal

narrative: Elsie Paroubek was the young daughter of Czech immigrants Frank and Karolina Paroubek and lived with her family on South Albany Avenue in Chicago. She was born in 1906, and accounts describe her as four or five years old in the spring of 1911; contemporary coverage generally gave her age as five.

On April 8, 1911, Elsie left home to visit her aunt, who lived a short distance away. According to accounts summarised by The Lineup and Grunge, she met her nine-year-old cousin and other neighbourhood children who were listening to an organ grinder. When the musician moved on, the other children followed him and Elsie stayed behind. She did not arrive at her aunt's house. Wikipedia's account, which draws on period newspapers, says her father reported her missing that evening.

The search lasted about a month and drew wide attention in Chicago and beyond. According to The Lineup, police first directed their efforts at Romani travellers after a witness reported seeing a child in a wagon, and later at Italian-American communities because of the organ grinder; none of these lines of inquiry produced evidence, and they reflected prejudices of the period. Wikipedia reports that rewards were offered by her father, a local judge and the governor of Illinois.

Elsie's body was found in the drainage canal near the power plant at Lockport, roughly 35 miles from Chicago, by plant employees. Wikipedia dates the discovery to May 8, 1911, while The Lineup and Grunge give May 9. Early reports suggested drowning, but the inquest heard that there was no water in her lungs, and concluded she had probably been suffocated by whoever took her. The official cause of death was nonetheless recorded as unknown.

Her funeral was held on May 12, 1911, on the lawn of the family home, with a crowd estimated at between 2,000 and 5,000 people, and she was buried at Bohemian National Cemetery. Several men were investigated, including one who died by suicide during the inquiry and whom police afterwards cleared, according to Wikipedia. No one was ever charged, and the case remains unsolved.

The case has a later connection to the Chicago outsider artist Henry Darger. According to Wikipedia's article on his manuscript In the Realms of the Unreal, Darger kept a newspaper photograph of Elsie published in May 1911 and was distressed when he lost it. Researchers have linked that loss to the character Annie Aronburg in his work.

timeline.event: Elsie Paroubek is born in Chicago to Frank and Karolina Paroubek.
A wide search begins; police pursue several theories and rewards are offered.
Elsie leaves home to visit her aunt, stops to listen to an organ grinder with other children, and disappears.
An inquest concludes she was probably suffocated; the official cause of death is recorded as unknown.
Her body is recovered from the drainage canal near the Lockport power plant (some accounts give May 9).
Her funeral is held at the family home, attended by thousands; she is buried at Bohemian National Cemetery.

name: Lacey Fletcher
summary: Lacey Fletcher, 36, was found dead on January 3, 2022 on a couch in her parents' home in Slaughter, Louisiana, after years of severe neglect. Her parents, Sheila and Clay Fletcher, were charged with second-degree murder; in February 2024 they pleaded no contest to manslaughter and were each sentenced to 40 years with 20 suspended.
lastSeen: January 3, 2022, found deceased in her parents' home, Slaughter, Louisiana

sources.title: Death of Lacey Fletcher - Wikipedia
Fletcher parents charged - NBC News

narrative: On January 3, 2022, first responders in Slaughter, Louisiana were called to the home of Clay and Sheila Fletcher, who reported that their 36-year-old daughter Lacey had died. What responders found was described as one of the most horrific scenes they had ever encountered.

Lacey Fletcher was found dead, fused to a couch in the living room. The coroner determined she had been sitting in the same spot for at least 12 years, developing severe pressure ulcers, malnutrition, and bone infections. She weighed only 96 pounds and had been living in her own waste.

Lacey had been diagnosed with autism and social anxiety as a child. Rather than seeking appropriate care, her parents had allowed her to deteriorate on the couch while they lived in the same house. Neighbors and officials had reportedly not checked on Lacey for years.

Both Clay and Sheila Fletcher were charged with second-degree murder; in February 2024 they pleaded no contest to the reduced charge of manslaughter and in March 2024 each received 40 years in prison with 20 years suspended. The case raised serious questions about the oversight of disabled adults and the failure of community systems to identify severe neglect.

timeline.event: Lacey Fletcher found dead in her parents' home.
Clay and Sheila Fletcher charged with second-degree murder.
Sheila and Clay Fletcher, who pleaded no contest to manslaughter on February 6, 2024, are each sentenced to 40 years with 20 suspended.

name: Carol Stuart
summary: Carol Stuart, 30 and pregnant, was shot in a car in Boston's Mission Hill on October 23, 1989 and died the next morning; her son, delivered by caesarean, lived 17 days. Her husband Charles blamed a Black gunman. After his brother told police the story was false, Charles Stuart died by suicide on January 4, 1990, before any charge was brought. Two wrongly suspected men received a city apology in 2023.
lastSeen: October 23, 1989, Mission Hill, Boston, Massachusetts

narrative: On the evening of October 23, 1989, Carol Stuart, a 30-year-old lawyer who was pregnant with her first child, was shot in the head while sitting in a car in the Mission Hill neighborhood of Boston. According to Boston.com, she and her husband, Charles Stuart, had just left a birthing class. Charles, who had a gunshot wound to the abdomen, called for help and told police that a Black man had forced his way into the car, robbed them and shot them both. NBC News reports that Carol died at the hospital the following morning. Her son was delivered by caesarean section and lived for 17 days.

Charles Stuart's description of the attacker set off a large police operation in Mission Hill. According to NBC News and WBUR, officers stopped and searched many Black men in the neighborhood, even though some investigators had doubts about the husband's account. Two men were publicly linked to the shooting. Alan Swanson was arrested first and then cleared. Willie Bennett was taken into custody afterwards, and in late December 1989 Charles Stuart picked him out as the attacker. Boston.com reports that neither man was ever formally charged with the shooting, although both were named as suspects in news coverage.

The account fell apart at the start of January 1990. According to Wikipedia's summary of contemporary reporting, Charles's brother Matthew Stuart went to Boston homicide detectives on the evening of January 3 and said the carjacking story was untrue. He said he had met his brother in Mission Hill on the night of the shooting and had been handed a bag that contained Carol's handbag, jewellery and a revolver, which he later helped to dispose of. Matthew said he had believed he was helping with an insurance fraud and had not known that Carol would be harmed.

On the morning of January 4, 1990, Charles Stuart left his car on the Tobin Bridge and jumped to his death; his body was recovered the same day. He was never charged or tried, so no court ruled on his guilt, but prosecutors dropped Bennett as a suspect and the authorities have since treated Charles Stuart as the person responsible. Wikipedia states that Matthew Stuart pleaded guilty in November 1992 to obstruction of justice and insurance fraud and received a sentence of three to five years, and that a friend, Jack McMahon, pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact. Matthew Stuart was not charged with taking part in the killing.

The case is remembered in Boston mainly for the way the false accusation was handled. In December 2023 the Boston Globe published a long re-investigation alongside an HBO documentary series. On December 20, 2023, Mayor Michelle Wu formally apologized on behalf of the city to Swanson, Bennett and their families, calling what was done to them unjust and racist. In September 2025, according to WBUR, the city paid a settlement of $150,000, with $100,000 going to Bennett and $50,000 to Swanson.
