name: Kathleen Peterson
summary: Kathleen Peterson, 48, was found dead at the foot of a staircase in her Durham, North Carolina, home on December 9, 2001. Her husband, novelist Michael Peterson, said she fell; he was convicted of first-degree murder in 2003, but a judge ordered a new trial in 2011 over misleading blood-evidence testimony. In 2017 he entered an Alford plea to manslaughter, maintaining his innocence, and was freed on time served.
lastSeen: December 9, 2001, her home in the Forest Hills neighborhood of Durham, North Carolina

sources.title: ABC11 - Sister blasts Durham novelist Michael Peterson as he accepts plea deal in wife's death
CBS17 / Associated Press - Michael Peterson accepts plea deal, walks free
WRAL - Judge rules that SBI agent's bias violated Peterson's rights
ABC News - Novelist Michael Peterson, Convicted of Wife's Murder, Is Released From Prison and Will Get New Trial
Wikipedia - Michael Peterson trial

narrative: Kathleen Peterson, a Nortel Networks executive, died on December 9, 2001, at the home in Durham, North Carolina, that she shared with her husband, Michael Peterson, a novelist, former newspaper columnist and one-time mayoral candidate. According to ABC News, Michael Peterson called 911 that morning and said he had found his wife unconscious at the bottom of a staircase. He maintained that she had fallen after drinking wine and taking Valium.

Police who responded were suspicious because of the amount of blood at the scene, ABC News reported. An autopsy found multiple lacerations to her scalp, and then-District Attorney Jim Hardin said the injuries could only have come from repeated blunt force trauma. Peterson was charged with murder. Wikipedia's account of the case, citing the autopsy, gives her age as 48.

The trial took place in 2003, and on October 10 of that year a Durham County jury convicted Peterson of first-degree murder. He was sentenced to life in prison without parole. ABC11 reported that the prosecution obtained the conviction without a murder weapon or a clear motive, although witnesses testified about financial problems and about Peterson's bisexuality. Jurors also heard about the 1985 death in Germany of a family friend who was likewise found at the bottom of a staircase.

A central prosecution witness was Duane Deaver, a bloodstain analyst for the State Bureau of Investigation. The SBI dismissed Deaver in January 2011 after an independent review of the state crime lab, according to WRAL. In December 2011, after a hearing, Superior Court Judge Orlando Hudson, who had presided over the original trial, ordered a new trial and Peterson was released on a $300,000 bond. In a written ruling reported by WRAL in May 2012, Hudson found that Deaver had misled the court and jury about his expertise and the reliability of his tests, and that this had a substantial effect on the verdict. Deaver's attorney disputed those findings.

In November 2016 Hudson declined a defense request to dismiss the case, and a retrial was scheduled for May 2017. Instead, on February 24, 2017, Peterson entered an Alford plea to manslaughter, a plea in which a defendant maintains innocence while accepting that prosecutors have enough evidence to convict. The judge found he had already served his time and he left court a free man, the Associated Press reported.

District Attorney Roger Echols said it remained the state's position that Peterson was responsible for his wife's death and that the plea was arranged in consultation with her family. Peterson and his attorney, David Rudolf, said he was innocent and had not received a fair trial. Kathleen Peterson's sister, Candace Zamperini, and her daughter, Caitlin Atwater, have said they believe he is guilty; Atwater reached a $25 million wrongful-death settlement with him in 2007, in which he admitted no guilt, ABC11 reported.

name: Holly Maddux
summary: Helen "Holly" Maddux, 30, was last seen in Philadelphia on September 9, 1977; her body was found in March 1979 in a trunk in the apartment of her former partner, Ira Einhorn. Einhorn fled before his 1981 trial, was convicted in absentia in 1993, arrested in France in 1997 and extradited in 2001. A Philadelphia jury convicted him of first-degree murder in October 2002, and he died in prison in 2020.
lastSeen: September 9, 1977, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

NBC News - Earth Day co-founder killed, composted girlfriend

The Guardian - 'He was a guru like there never have been gurus'

narrative: Helen "Holly" Maddux grew up in Tyler, Texas, the oldest of five siblings, and graduated from Bryn Mawr College, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer. She had been in a relationship of about five years with Ira Einhorn, a well-known figure in Philadelphia's counterculture of the 1960s and 1970s. NBC News reported that she had ended the relationship and moved to New York, and that on September 9, 1977 she went back to the Philadelphia apartment the two had shared to collect her belongings. She was not seen again. She was 30.

According to NBC News, when police asked Einhorn about her some weeks later, he said she had gone out to a neighborhood co-op and had not come back. The Inquirer reported that her parents hired a retired FBI agent to look for her, and that his report led Philadelphia police to search Einhorn's apartment in the Powelton neighborhood in March 1979. The Guardian and NBC News both describe a neighbor's complaint about a foul-smelling liquid coming through the ceiling below Einhorn's closet. Inside the locked closet, detectives found a steamer trunk containing her remains, packed with newspapers and Styrofoam.

Einhorn was arrested and charged with murder. He was released on $40,000 bail, a decision the Inquirer says shocked the Maddux family. In 1981, shortly before his trial was due to begin, he left the country. The Guardian reported that he lived in Ireland and later in Sweden. In 1993 a Philadelphia court tried him in absentia, convicted him of first-degree murder and sentenced him to life imprisonment.

Investigators traced him to France in 1997, where, according to the Guardian, he was living under the name Eugene Mallon. A French court at first refused extradition because French law entitles a person tried in absentia to a new trial. Pennsylvania then passed a law allowing such a retrial, and the Daily Pennsylvanian reported that Maddux's siblings travelled to France to testify at a later extradition hearing. Einhorn was returned to the United States in July 2001.

At his trial in Philadelphia in October 2002, Einhorn testified in his own defense and denied killing Maddux. The jury found him guilty of first-degree murder after deliberating for about two and a half hours, the Daily Pennsylvanian reported, and the conviction carried a mandatory sentence of life without parole. Einhorn died of natural causes on April 3, 2020 at the State Correctional Institution at Laurel Highlands, aged 79, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections as quoted by the Inquirer. Maddux's father died in 1988 and her mother two years later, before the case was concluded.

name: Susan Berman, Kathleen Durst & Morris Black
summary: Writer Susan Berman, 55, was found shot in her Los Angeles home on December 24, 2000. A jury convicted real estate heir Robert Durst of her murder in 2021, but the conviction was vacated after he died in January 2022 with an appeal pending. He was indicted, never tried, for the 1982 murder of his wife Kathleen, and was acquitted of murdering Morris Black in Texas.
lastSeen: December 2000, at her home in the Benedict Canyon area of Los Angeles, California (Susan Berman)

narrative: Susan Berman, a 55-year-old writer, was found dead in her home in the Benedict Canyon area of Los Angeles on December 24, 2000. According to CBS News, she had been shot at close range in the back of the head. An anonymous note sent to Beverly Hills police directed officers to a body at her address and misspelled the city's name as "Beverley".

Berman was a longtime friend of Robert Durst, a member of a New York real estate family. Durst's first wife, Kathleen McCormack Durst, disappeared on January 31, 1982, at the age of 29, according to the Westchester County District Attorney's Office. She was a medical student at the time, has never been found, and was declared legally dead in 2017, PBS NewsHour reported.

In 2001 Durst was living in Galveston, Texas, where he shot his neighbor Morris Black and dismembered the body, which was recovered from Galveston Bay. Durst told a Texas jury that the gun went off during a struggle, and he was acquitted of murder in 2003. He served a prison term for offenses connected with the disposal of the body, PBS NewsHour reported.

Durst took part in the HBO documentary series The Jinx, whose makers found a letter in his handwriting carrying the same misspelling as the anonymous note. He was recorded on a live microphone saying "killed them all, of course." He was arrested in New Orleans in March 2015, the night before the final episode was broadcast.

At trial in Los Angeles, prosecutors argued that Berman was killed because she was preparing to tell investigators that she had helped Durst with a false alibi after his wife vanished. Durst testified, acknowledged writing the note, and denied killing Berman. The jury found him guilty of first-degree murder on September 17, 2021, and he was sentenced on October 14, 2021 to life in prison without parole.

The Westchester County District Attorney's Office filed a complaint against Durst on October 19, 2021, and a grand jury indicted him on November 1, 2021 for second-degree murder in the death of Kathleen Durst. He died in custody in California on January 10, 2022, aged 78, before that case could be tried. Because his appeal in the Berman case was still pending, a Los Angeles Superior Court judge vacated that conviction on February 25, 2022, according to Oxygen. As a result, no conviction stands against Durst for any of the three deaths.

name: Sarah Stern
summary: Sarah Stern, 19, was strangled at her Neptune City, New Jersey, home on December 2, 2016, during a robbery, and her body was thrown from the Route 35 bridge; it has never been recovered. Former classmate Liam McAtasney was convicted in February 2019 and sentenced to life without parole. Preston Taylor pleaded guilty to helping and received 18 years.
lastSeen: December 2, 2016, her home in Neptune City, New Jersey

sources.title: ABC News - Liam McAtasney sentenced to life without parole for murdering friend Sarah Stern

narrative: Sarah Stern, 19, was last seen at her home in Neptune City, New Jersey, on December 2, 2016. According to ABC7 New York, her car was found hours later, unoccupied and with the keys in the ignition, on the Route 35 bridge between Neptune and Belmar. The location of the car at first raised the possibility that she had taken her own life, and her body was not found in the searches that followed.

According to reporting on the appellate record, a former classmate, Anthony Curry, went to police in January 2017 and said that Liam McAtasney had described a plan to rob and kill Stern around Thanksgiving, before she disappeared. Working with investigators, Curry met McAtasney in Bradley Beach on January 31, 2017, and the conversation was secretly recorded on video. ABC News reported that on the recording McAtasney said the killing had taken about half an hour. McAtasney and his roommate, Preston Taylor, were arrested the following day.

Prosecutors said McAtasney strangled Stern at her home in order to steal money she had found that had belonged to her late mother. According to ABC News, prosecutors alleged he expected to find between $50,000 and $100,000 but took roughly $10,000; other outlets put the amount at about $8,000. Taylor, who had been Stern's prom date, admitted that he helped McAtasney move her body and throw it from the bridge into the Shark River. He pleaded guilty to robbery, conspiracy, desecrating human remains, hindering apprehension and evidence tampering, and testified for the prosecution.

McAtasney was tried in Monmouth County Superior Court in Freehold. In late February 2019 a jury found him guilty on all seven counts: first-degree murder, felony murder, robbery, conspiracy, desecrating human remains, hindering apprehension and tampering with physical evidence. On June 21, 2019, he was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole, plus ten years. One week later, on June 28, 2019, Taylor was sentenced to 18 years. NBC New York reported that Judge Richard English later declined to reduce Taylor's sentence; prosecutors had asked for 15 years, while Stern's father said he believed the term should have been longer.

The conviction has been tested on appeal twice. According to the Asbury Park Press reporting carried by Yahoo News, a New Jersey appellate panel upheld McAtasney's convictions and sentence in a ruling announced on October 27, 2023. On November 6, 2025, an appellate panel also upheld the denial of his petition for post-conviction relief. Stern's body has never been recovered, and the same reporting described the case as only the second murder prosecution in Monmouth County brought without a body.

name: Macin Smith
summary: Seventeen-year-old Macin Smith left his family's home in St. George, Utah, on the morning of September 1, 2015, and did not arrive at Desert Hills High School. He left his phone, laptop and wallet behind, and a handwritten note was later found in the wallet. St. George police say the case remains open; no confirmed sighting has been reported and no one has been charged.
lastSeen: September 1, 2015, his family's home in St. George, Utah

sources.title: St. George News - 'Help us bring him home': Loved ones plead for answers 11 years after Macin Smith's disappearance

narrative: Macin Smith was 17 and a senior at Desert Hills High School when he disappeared from St. George, Utah, on September 1, 2015. According to the Polly Klaas Foundation listing, he was born on April 7, 1998, and was 6 feet 4 inches tall and about 200 pounds, with blond hair and blue eyes. The Deseret News reported that the family had moved to St. George from Canada in April 2015.

According to St. George News, Macin left home that Tuesday morning, presumably for school, but did not attend any of his classes. The Deseret News and KSL reported that his father told police he had taken away Macin's cellphone and laptop the night before as a consequence for staying up late. Wikipedia's summary of contemporary coverage says his parents heard him moving around the house that morning and reported him missing that evening; that detail rests on Wikipedia alone.

Macin's wallet was also left behind. The Deseret News reported that a three-page handwritten note was later found inside it, and described it as a suicide note. Wikipedia dates the discovery to September 7, 2015. More than 200 volunteers searched the area around the family home, according to Wikipedia, and the Polly Klaas Foundation listing states that he may be in the local area or may have travelled to Las Vegas, Nevada.

In May 2019, KSL and the Deseret News reported on search warrant affidavits filed by St. George police. According to those reports, the warrants said detectives were investigating possible criminal homicide, referred to discrepancies in statements made by Macin's parents, and showed that a GPS tracker had been authorised for his father's truck in 2017. A police spokeswoman told the Deseret News that no one in the investigation was considered a suspect. Both parents told reporters they had nothing to hide and welcomed the scrutiny. No one has been charged.
Reported sightings in Utah and California in 2016 and 2017 were never confirmed, according to Wikipedia. His case was featured on the Investigation Discovery series Disappeared in 2017.

In September 2026, St. George News marked the eleventh anniversary of the disappearance. A family friend who runs the Macin's Army Facebook page told the outlet there had not been a single credible or confirmed lead or sighting in eleven years. Age-progressed images showing how he might look at 28 have been circulated. St. George police told the outlet that the case remains open and active and asked anyone with information to call the department at 435-627-4300.

name: Joey Lynn Offutt
summary: Joey Lynn Offutt, 33, was found to be missing on July 12, 2007, when a deliberately set fire destroyed her home in Sykesville, Pennsylvania, and the body of her six-week-old son was found inside. Her car turned up days later in State College. She was declared legally dead in 2016; she has never been found and no one has been charged.
lastSeen: Discovered missing July 12, 2007, from her home on Fugate Drive, Sykesville, Jefferson County, Pennsylvania; state police give July 4, 2007 as the last confirmed sighting

narrative: At about 4 a.m. on July 12, 2007, neighbors found the home of Joey Lynn Offutt on Fugate Drive in Sykesville, Jefferson County, Pennsylvania, on fire. After the fire was put out, firefighters found the body of an infant in the bathtub. According to Pennsylvania State Police appeals reported by WTAJ and Explore Jefferson, DNA testing identified the child as Offutt's six-week-old son, and investigators determined that he had died before the fire began. The Crime Junkie podcast's case summary gives the boy's name as Alexis Brolin III.

Offutt, who was 33, was not in the house, and nothing indicated that she had been at home when the fire started. Her purse and identification were recovered from the debris, according to the state police account. Investigators concluded that the fire had been set deliberately with an accelerant. Her two older children, aged two and nine, were not in the house at the time.

Her car, a red 1994 Saturn with Virginia license plates, was also missing. State police say it was found abandoned on July 15, 2007, near the Nittany Gardens apartments in State College, where Offutt had lived before moving to Sykesville; a 2016 WJAC report put the discovery four days after the fire. State College is roughly a two-hour drive from Sykesville.

Accounts differ on when she was last seen. Recent state police appeals give July 4, 2007, as the last time she was seen at her home, while WJAC's 2016 report described her as last seen in the early hours of July 12. What is not disputed is that her disappearance came to light at the fire.

In June 2016 Offutt was declared legally dead at her mother's request. A state trooper told WJAC that year that the family had sought the declaration for the sake of her children and that the investigation remained active. WJAC also reported that the family had offered a $25,000 reward. The case has been featured on America's Most Wanted and on Investigation Discovery's Disappeared.

Pennsylvania State Police have continued to publicize the case, including appeals in March 2025 and January 2026 that mention a reward of up to $5,000. Police have said they believe Offutt met with foul play and is dead. Her remains have not been found, and no one has been charged in connection with her disappearance, the fire or her son's death.

name: Madeline Kingsbury
summary: Madeline Kingsbury, 26, disappeared on March 31, 2023, after dropping her two children at daycare in Winona, Minnesota. Her remains were found on June 7, 2023, near Mabel in Fillmore County. Adam Fravel, the children's father, was convicted of first- and second-degree murder in November 2024 and sentenced to life without parole; the Minnesota Supreme Court upheld the conviction in April 2026.
lastSeen: March 31, 2023, Winona, Minnesota

narrative: Madeline Kingsbury was a 26-year-old mother of two who lived in Winona, Minnesota, and worked at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, according to MPR News. She disappeared on March 31, 2023. MPR News reported that she was last seen dropping her children at a Winona daycare together with Adam Fravel, her former partner and the children's father.

Her disappearance prompted a large search and drew national attention. According to a criminal complaint described by Fox 9, Fravel told police that he left the home at about 10 a.m. that day to take items to his parents' house near Mabel, turned back partway, and assumed Kingsbury had gone to work with someone else because her vehicle was still at the home. Fox 9 reported that the complaint cited surveillance footage that investigators said was inconsistent with that account.

On June 7, 2023, a deputy found human remains off Highway 43 near Mabel, in Fillmore County. According to the Minnesota Supreme Court's later opinion, the remains were wrapped in a bedsheet, and the cause of death was determined to be homicidal violence, most likely asphyxiation. Fravel was arrested the same day, and on June 9, 2023, prosecutors filed two counts of second-degree murder in Winona County, Fox 9 reported. He was later indicted on four counts, including two of first-degree murder.

The trial was moved from Winona to the Blue Earth County Justice Center in Mankato because of pretrial publicity, according to MPR News. After a trial of about three weeks, the jury found Fravel guilty on November 7, 2024, of first-degree premeditated murder, first-degree murder involving a past pattern of domestic abuse, second-degree intentional murder and second-degree felony murder.

On December 17, 2024, Fravel was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. MPR News reported that Kingsbury's family addressed the court and that Fravel maintained at sentencing that he was innocent.

Fravel appealed, arguing among other points that hearsay statements had been wrongly admitted. The Minnesota Supreme Court heard arguments in January 2026 and on April 29, 2026, affirmed the convictions, holding that the evidence was sufficient to prove premeditation and intent and that the other claims lacked merit or were harmless, according to the published opinion and reports by Fox 9 and KTTC.

name: Mary Boyle
summary: Six-year-old Mary Boyle disappeared on March 18, 1977, near her grandparents' farm at Cashelard, outside Ballyshannon, County Donegal, Ireland. She had followed her uncle part of the way to a neighbour's house and turned back alone. No trace of her has been found, no one has been charged, and hers is described as Ireland's longest-running missing person case.

narrative: Mary Boyle was six years old when she disappeared on March 18, 1977, while visiting her grandparents at Cashelard, near Ballyshannon in County Donegal. An Garda Siochana's missing-person notice states that she was wearing a lilac hand-knitted cardigan, brown jeans and black wellington boots.

According to the Irish Times, Mary was last seen at about 3:30 p.m. leaving her grandparents' home. She was following her uncle, who was returning a ladder to a neighbour's house. About halfway there she told him she was turning back, and she was not seen again. Wikipedia's account, drawing on press reports, says the neighbouring farm was roughly 400 yards away across a hillside and that the walk back should have taken only a few minutes.

Searches of the surrounding land began the same day and continued for years. According to Wikipedia, gardai drained a lake behind the house and nearby bogs were searched. The BBC reported that a fresh review of the case began in 2011 and involved a number of searches assisted by forensic and geology experts.

On October 21, 2014, a 64-year-old man was arrested in connection with the disappearance. The BBC reported that he was released without charge the following day and that a file would be sent to the Director of Public Prosecutions. No charge followed. In July 2016 gardai carried out a dig on land in County Donegal close to where Mary was last seen; TheJournal.ie reported that it was understood no new evidence was found. The same month it was confirmed that the Garda Serious Crime Review Team would re-examine the case, and gardai later said that review was completed in 2017.

Mary's family has taken different views of what happened. TheJournal.ie reported in 2017 that her mother, Ann Boyle, said she did not want an inquest and wished to believe her daughter was still alive, while Mary's twin sister, Ann Doherty, has said she believes Mary was killed and has campaigned for an inquest. In March 2018 supporters handed the Donegal coroner a petition with more than 10,000 names asking for one, according to the Irish Times.

Gardai renewed their appeal in March 2018, saying the investigation remained live. On the 46th anniversary in March 2023, Ann Doherty appealed again for information, saying her aim was to find her sister and give her a burial. Gardai said then that the investigation was continuing under a senior investigating officer in Ballyshannon. No one has been charged, and Mary Boyle has not been found.

name: Anne Marie Fahey
summary: Delaware Governor's scheduling secretary Anne Marie Fahey was murdered by her lover Thomas Capano, a prominent attorney. He disposed of her body at sea. Capano was sentenced to death.

narrative: On June 27, 1996, thirty-year-old Anne Marie Fahey, a scheduling secretary for Delaware Governor Tom Carper, disappeared after dinner with her secret lover Thomas Capano, a prominent Wilmington attorney and former deputy attorney general.
Fahey had been trying to end the relationship with Capano, who was married with four daughters. Friends and family reported she was afraid of him. When she didn't appear at work, police were called.

The investigation revealed that Capano had shot Fahey in his home, then enlisted his brother Gerry to help dispose of the body. They placed her in a large cooler, took a boat into the Atlantic, and dumped her overboard after weighing the cooler with chains. The cooler resurfaced and was found empty.

Capano was convicted of first-degree murder in 1999 and sentenced to death—Delaware's first death sentence in decades. His sentence was later commuted to life without parole. He died in prison in 2011.

name: Lisa Ziegert
summary: Lisa Ziegert, 24, who worked at a middle school, was abducted from her evening job at a card shop in Agawam, Massachusetts, on April 15, 1992, and found dead four days later. Gary Schara was arrested in September 2017 after DNA from his toothbrush matched a profile from the evidence. He pleaded guilty to first-degree murder on September 25, 2019, and received a life sentence.
lastSeen: April 15, 1992, a card and gift shop on Walnut Street Extension, Agawam, Massachusetts

narrative: Lisa Ziegert, 24, worked at a middle school in Agawam, Massachusetts, and had a second job in the evenings at a card and gift shop on Walnut Street Extension. According to the Hampden District Attorney's Office, she was abducted from the shop during the early evening of April 15, 1992. The next morning the store's day clerk arrived to find the shop open with its lights on and Ziegert's car parked where it had been the evening before, and reported her missing. The money in the register, her purse and her school materials appeared undisturbed.

On April 19, 1992, which was Easter Sunday, a passerby found her body in woods off Suffield Street in Agawam, about four miles from the shop, the District Attorney's Office said. The office stated that she had been sexually assaulted and killed, and her death was ruled a homicide. Agawam police, Massachusetts State Police detectives, the state crime laboratory and the FBI took part in an investigation that continued for 25 years.

A single-source male DNA profile was developed from evidence, but according to the District Attorney it was run repeatedly against state, national and international databases without a match. In September 2016 District Attorney Anthony Gulluni announced that Parabon NanoLabs had used DNA phenotyping to predict the unknown man's ancestry and appearance, and released composite images. Investigators then went back to their lists of persons of interest, which totalled more than 300 names, and picked out people who had not given DNA samples. Gary E. Schara of West Springfield was among them; his former wife had given his name to investigators in March 1993.

In August 2017 a grand jury was asked to authorise the collection of DNA samples. On September 13, 2017, state troopers went to Schara's home to serve paperwork and left word with his roommate. The following day, according to the District Attorney's account, Schara's girlfriend brought police handwritten notes he had left for her, in which he admitted abducting, raping and killing a young woman 25 years earlier, along with a letter of apology addressed to the Ziegert family. His car was found that night at a hospital in Stafford Springs, Connecticut.

On September 16, 2017, the state crime laboratory reported that DNA from a toothbrush seized from Schara's home matched the profile from the evidence, and he was arrested at a medical facility in Connecticut. A Hampden County grand jury indicted him on December 8, 2017, for first-degree murder, aggravated kidnapping and aggravated rape. Prosecutors later dropped the kidnapping and rape counts because the statutes of limitations had expired. On September 25, 2019, Schara, then 50, pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and began a life sentence.

name: Sophie Sergie
summary: Sophie Sergie, 20, of Pitkas Point, Alaska, was found sexually assaulted, stabbed and shot in a dormitory bathroom at the University of Alaska Fairbanks on April 26, 1993. Genetic genealogy led to the February 2019 arrest of former student Steven Downs in Maine. A Fairbanks jury convicted him in February 2022 and he was sentenced to 75 years; his appeal was argued in April 2025.

narrative: Sophie Sergie was a 20-year-old Alaska Native woman from Pitkas Point, a village in western Alaska. According to the Alaska Department of Law, she had been a University of Alaska Fairbanks student and was taking a semester off in the spring of 1993. Alaska's News Source reported that she had travelled to Fairbanks for orthodontic work and was staying with a former roommate in Bartlett Hall, a campus dormitory.

According to the Department of Law, Sergie was killed in the early hours of April 26, 1993, and her body was found that afternoon in a bathtub in the women's bathroom on the second floor of Bartlett Hall. The department's account states that she had been sexually assaulted, stabbed in the face and shot in the back of the head at close range. The killing happened shortly before finals week, in a building full of students, but investigators did not identify a suspect, and the case stayed open for about 25 years.

In 2018, investigators turned to genetic genealogy. According to the Department of Law, analysis of DNA from the scene pointed to Steven Harris Downs through a profile that an aunt of his had placed on an open genealogy website. Downs had attended the university from 1992 to 1996 and lived in Bartlett Hall at the time of the killing, Alaska Public Media reported. He was arrested in Auburn, Maine, in mid-February 2019 and charged with murder and sexual assault, according to WABI, and was extradited to Alaska in August 2019, according to Alaska's News Source.

The trial began in Fairbanks on January 12, 2022. Alaska's News Source reported that the defense pointed to other hairs and fingerprints found at the scene and disputed that a firearm seized from Downs's home in Maine was the murder weapon. After two days of deliberation, the jury found Downs guilty of first-degree murder and first-degree sexual assault on February 10, 2022.

On September 26, 2022, Superior Court Judge Thomas Temple sentenced Downs to 67 years for the murder and eight years for the sexual assault, to be served consecutively, for a total of 75 years. According to the Department of Law, he becomes eligible for discretionary parole after 25 years.

Downs has appealed. Alaska Public Media reported that the Alaska Court of Appeals heard oral argument in April 2025 on three issues: whether the warrantless search of a genealogy database violated privacy rights, whether the trial court wrongly excluded testimony about a statement attributed to another person, and whether evidence about a revolver should have been admitted. The court said it would rule at a later date. No decision had been located when this record was checked in September 2026, and the conviction stands.

name: Wayne Nance Victims
summary: Wayne Nance, a Missoula furniture mover, is suspected by investigators of at least six killings in western Montana between 1974 and 1985. He was never charged: he died on September 4, 1986, after being shot by Doug Wells, whom he had attacked at home along with Wells's wife Kris. Three unidentified victims tied to the case were later named, the last, Janet Lee Lucas, in 2021.
lastSeen: Various dates, 1974-1985, Missoula and Ravalli counties, Montana

narrative: Wayne Nathan Nance was a furniture mover in Missoula, Montana, who investigators believe was responsible for at least six killings in Missoula and Ravalli counties. He was never arrested, charged or tried for any of them. According to the Missoula County Sheriff's Office, as reported by NBC Montana, he was killed by an intended victim in 1986 before any case against him could be brought, so the allegations have never been tested in court.

The earliest death attributed to him is that of Donna Pounds, 39, who was shot in her home near Missoula in April 1974. According to The Lineup's account, Nance was a friend of her teenage son and witnesses placed him near the house, but there was not enough evidence for an arrest at the time; Wikipedia gives the date as April 11, 1974.

During the 1980s the remains of three unidentified young women were found in the Missoula area and given nicknames based on nearby landmarks. One, found in 1980, was identified in 1985 as Devonna Nelson, 15, according to Wikipedia. A second, found in 1984, was identified in 2006 as Marcella Bachmann, 16. The third, found by a hunter south of Missoula in September 1985 with two gunshot wounds to the skull, was identified in May 2021 as Janet Lee Lucas, 23, of Spokane, Washington, through genetic genealogy work by the sheriff's cold case unit and the laboratory Othram. The sheriff's office said at the time that it was reviewing the Nance file for any link to Lucas.

On December 12, 1985, Michael and Teresa Shook were killed in their home in Ravalli County. According to The Lineup, the intruder tried to set the house on fire while the couple's three young children were inside; the children were rescued the next morning and survived. Items taken from the Shook home were found among Nance's belongings after his death.

Late on September 3, 1986, Nance went to the Missoula home of Doug Wells, his manager at the furniture store, and Wells's wife Kris. Accounts in The Lineup and Wikipedia say he struck and stabbed Doug Wells and tied up both of them. Wells freed himself, loaded a rifle he had been repairing and shot Nance. Both of the Wellses survived. Nance died in hospital the following day.

Searches after his death produced the evidence on which investigators based their conclusions. Because there was no trial, the number of victims remains an estimate, and authorities have continued to ask the public for information, most recently about Lucas's movements in 1983 and 1984.

name: Jessica Dishon
summary: Jessica Dishon, 17, vanished from her family's driveway in Bullitt County, Kentucky, on the morning of September 10, 1999, and was found beaten and strangled 17 days later. A neighbor's 2003 trial ended in a mistrial and the charges were dismissed. Her uncle, Stanley Dishon, entered an Alford plea to first-degree manslaughter in 2015 and received 20 years; he maintains his innocence.
lastSeen: Morning of September 10, 1999, in the driveway of her family's home near Shepherdsville, Bullitt County, Kentucky

narrative: Jessica Dishon was a 17-year-old high school senior living with her family in Bullitt County, Kentucky, near Shepherdsville. On the morning of September 10, 1999, she disappeared from the driveway of her home as she was preparing to leave for school. Police have said she was dragged from her car, according to Louisville station WDRB.

Her body was found 17 days later, about seven miles from her home, in an area known as the Salt River bottoms. WAVE 3 News and WDRB reported that she had been beaten and strangled. WDRB has described the original investigation as badly flawed.

A neighbor of the family was arrested and charged with her killing in 2001. His trial ended in a mistrial in 2003, and the charges were dismissed, the Associated Press reported. WAVE later described him as a man wrongly accused. The case then went unresolved for a decade.

In 2013 the Bullitt County Sheriff's Office reopened the matter after two jail inmates separately told investigators that Jessica's uncle, Stanley Dishon, had said he killed her. According to WAVE and WDRB, the informants said he feared she would disclose that he had sexually abused her. He was arrested on October 2, 2013, and charged with murder. WDRB reported that the evidence was circumstantial and rested largely on the informants' accounts, together with relatives' descriptions of his behaviour at the time.

In January 2015, at a hearing in Bardstown, Stanley Dishon entered Alford pleas to first-degree manslaughter in Jessica's death and to sexual assault counts in separate cases. Under an Alford plea a defendant does not admit guilt but accepts that the evidence could lead to conviction. On March 26, 2015, a Bullitt Circuit Court judge sentenced him to 20 years in prison, followed by five years of probation, and ordered him to register as a sex offender.

Dishon has continued to deny killing his niece. In a 2019 interview from the Kentucky State Penitentiary he told WDRB that he was at work that morning and had pleaded guilty on his lawyers' advice. His attorneys had said at the time of the plea that they believed he was not the killer but that he faced a possible life sentence in the abuse cases. The Kentucky Innocence Project told WDRB it had declined his 2017 request for help. His conviction stands.

narrative: Lisa Michelle Stebic, 37, disappeared from her home in Plainfield, Illinois, a suburb southwest of Chicago, on April 30, 2007. Plainfield Deputy Police Chief Mark Eiting told Fox News that she was last seen at about 6 p.m. that Monday. Her two children, then aged 10 and 12, had been home when she returned from work but were out when she vanished, he said. ABC7 Chicago reported that a neighbor reported her missing on May 1, 2007.

According to Fox News, which cited the Chicago Tribune, her husband, Craig Stebic, said he was working in the backyard at the time and believed someone had picked her up. She regularly exercised at the Plainfield North High School track. Only her purse and cell phone were missing, and police said neither the phone nor her credit cards were used afterwards. A family spokeswoman, Melanie Greenberg, later told ABC7 that her car had been left in the garage.

The couple were in the middle of a divorce and were living separately within the same house, Fox News reported. ABC7 reported that Lisa Stebic was last seen on the same day her divorce attorney sent eviction papers intended to remove her husband from the home. Police said in the first days that there were no signs of foul play and that no suspicious vehicles or people had been seen near the house. Craig Stebic gave the family computer to investigators voluntarily, and in May 2007 police said he was cooperating and had not been named a suspect; his lawyer advised him not to take a polygraph. He filed an emergency motion for sole custody of the children that month, and the FBI joined the search.

According to Wikipedia, which cites Chicago Sun-Times reporting from July 2007, Plainfield police later described Craig Stebic as a person of interest. He has never been named a suspect or charged, and relatives quoted by Fox News said he denied any involvement. In October 2007 the FBI added her case to its kidnapped and missing persons website.

No trace of Lisa Stebic has been found. CBS Chicago reported in 2013 that her family presumes she is dead. On the tenth anniversary in 2017, ABC7 reported that the family was offering a $75,000 reward and that the Plainfield Police Department's tip line remained open. Wikipedia quotes Plainfield Police Chief John Konopek as saying in 2019 that investigators were closer than at the start and still considered Craig Stebic a person of interest, and cites a 2026 WGN Radio interview in which Greenberg described the matter as a very cold case. As of September 2026 no one has been charged.

name: Patrick Warren Sr.
summary: Patrick Warren Sr., 52, was shot and killed by Killeen, Texas police officer Reynaldo Contreras on January 10, 2021, after his family called for help during a mental health crisis. A Bell County grand jury declined to indict the officer in May 2021. A federal court granted the officer summary judgment in the family's civil rights lawsuit in March 2026; the family has appealed.

narrative: Patrick Warren Sr., 52, died on January 10, 2021, after being shot by Killeen Police Officer Reynaldo Contreras outside the Warren family home on Carrollton Avenue in Killeen, Texas. NBC News reported that Warren had started a landscaping business after losing a job at a local plant during the pandemic. He was unarmed.

According to the family's account reported by NBC News, relatives had called for help the previous day, a mental health officer responded, and Warren went voluntarily to a hospital for evaluation before returning home. When they called again on January 10, they said they wanted a mental health professional rather than a patrol officer. The family's attorney, Lee Merritt, said a mental health call should not have ended in a death.

A federal magistrate judge's March 2026 report, which relied on the officer's body camera recording, summarised the encounter as follows. Dispatch told Contreras that the call might involve a mental health issue and that the caller said there were no firearms in the house. He stepped inside briefly, went back outside and waited for backup. Warren then opened the door and walked toward him, and the officer backed away while giving commands. Contreras fired his Taser more than once; Warren got up and kept approaching. The report states that Contreras warned he would shoot and fired three shots as Warren lunged at him, about 32 seconds after Warren opened the door. Warren died at a hospital a short time later.

Killeen police released the body camera video in January 2021. Police Chief Charles Kimble disputed parts of the family attorney's description of the encounter while acknowledging, according to KWTX, a breakdown in how police and mental health services intersect. The Texas Rangers investigated the shooting and presented the case to a Bell County grand jury, which declined to indict Contreras in May 2021. KWTX reported that he had returned to work on administrative duty in April 2021.

Warren's widow, Bobbie Warren, filed a federal lawsuit in the Western District of Texas on December 21, 2022, alleging excessive force in violation of the Fourth Amendment. Court records show the City of Killeen was dismissed as a defendant on August 1, 2023. On March 11, 2026, Magistrate Judge Dan MacLemore recommended granting the officer's motion for summary judgment, which asserted qualified immunity, and on March 31, 2026, District Judge Alan Albright adopted the recommendation and entered judgment for Contreras. The family filed a notice of appeal to the Fifth Circuit on April 8, 2026; the docket shows the appeal still open as of late September 2026.

No one has been charged or convicted in connection with Warren's death. His son, Patrick Warren Jr., told KWTX on the first anniversary that he wanted better training for officers who respond to mental health calls.

narrative: Charles Calixtus Morgan was the president of an escrow company in Tucson, Arizona. In the months before his death, he reported being stalked and followed. He painted his car a different color, began wearing a bulletproof vest, and taped emergency cash to his body.

Morgan first disappeared on March 22, 1977, returning home three days later. He vanished again on June 7, and on June 18, 1977, he was found dead in the desert about 40 miles west of Tucson. He had been shot once in the back of the head with his own revolver. He was wearing a bulletproof vest, and investigators found a two-dollar bill bearing Spanish surnames and a map.

The circumstances were bizarre enough that police initially couldn't determine if it was murder or suicide. The positioning of the wound and the gun suggested suicide might be physically possible but unlikely given the other circumstances.
Investigation suggested Morgan may have been involved in laundering money for drug traffickers and became a liability. His case was featured on 'Unsolved Mysteries' but has never been solved.

narrative: Jennifer Lynn Servo was born in 1979 and grew up in Columbia Falls, Montana. According to a CBS News 48 Hours report, she joined the U.S. Army Reserve to help pay for college, worked for television stations in Missoula while studying, and graduated from the University of Montana's journalism program in May 2002. That summer she took her first full-time reporting job at KRBC-TV in Abilene, Texas, more than 1,700 miles from home.

CBS reported that a boyfriend she had met through the Army Reserve followed her to Abilene, and that the relationship ended soon afterwards when she learned he had left a fiancee in Montana. He moved to a separate apartment in the city.

On the night of September 15, 2002, Servo left work at about 11:30 p.m. and went shopping with a colleague, according to Wikipedia's summary of reporting by Oxygen and the Abilene Reporter-News. They left the store around 12:30 a.m. and she spoke to a friend by phone at 1:39 a.m. on September 16. When she failed to appear at work she was checked on, and on September 18 she was found dead in the bathroom of her apartment. The autopsy found she had been strangled and had suffered blunt force trauma. Investigators told CBS there was no sign of a break-in, which led them to believe she knew her killer.

Abilene police collected fingerprints, blood and DNA evidence and took samples from several people close to her. In 2008 a detective told CBS that the department did not have probable cause for an arrest. Local station KTAB/KRBC reported that police said in 2014 they were pursuing new leads without elaborating, and Wikipedia notes that evidence was later sent to private laboratories for further DNA testing.

In 2024 the department's cold case unit reworked the file with the television series Cold Justice. The Abilene Reporter-News reported on April 29, 2024, that detectives re-interviewed witnesses, said on the programme that the colleague who had been with her that night was cleared, and announced that they would present a case against her former boyfriend to the district attorney's office, which was considering charges or a grand jury. The newspaper noted that anyone accused is presumed innocent. The former boyfriend has not been charged.

No arrest has been made. Servo's family, including her mother Sherry Abel and her father Norm Olson, have continued to press for a resolution, and a scholarship in her name was established at the University of Montana. Tips can be given to Abilene Crime Stoppers.

name: Damon and Devon Routier
summary: Brothers Devon Routier, 6, and Damon Routier, 5, were fatally stabbed in their home in Rowlett, Texas, on June 6, 1996. Their mother, Darlie Routier, who said an intruder attacked them, was convicted of capital murder in Damon's death on February 1, 1997, and sentenced to death. She was never tried for Devon's death, maintains her innocence, and DNA testing in the case has continued.
lastSeen: June 6, 1996, family home on Eagle Drive in Rowlett, Texas

narrative: Devon Routier, 6, and his brother Damon, 5, were fatally stabbed in the early hours of June 6, 1996, in the downstairs living room of their family's home on Eagle Drive in Rowlett, Texas, a suburb east of Dallas. According to Wikipedia's account, a 911 call from the house was received at 2:31 a.m. Their mother, Darlie Routier, then 26, had wounds to her neck and upper body and was treated at Baylor University Medical Center in Dallas, the Dallas Morning News reported. Her husband, Darin, and the couple's infant son, Drake, were upstairs and were not hurt.

Darlie Routier told police that she had been asleep on a couch near the boys and woke to find a man in dark clothing, who fled toward the garage. In the 911 call she said someone had broken in and stabbed her and her children, according to the Associated Press.

Rowlett police arrested her on June 18, 1996, twelve days after the killings, saying her account did not match the evidence at the scene. A Dallas County grand jury indicted her on two counts of capital murder on June 28. A detective testified at a pretrial hearing that blood was found near the kitchen sink but none near the garage window or outside the house, the Dallas Morning News reported. Because of pretrial publicity, the trial was moved to Kerrville.

The trial began in January 1997. Prosecutors chose to try her only for Damon's death, a capital charge based on the killing of a child under six, which prosecutor Greg Davis described as the simpler case to prove. They argued she was angry about family money problems and had cut herself to mislead police. Jurors were also shown video of a graveside gathering for Devon's birthday, held eight days after the killings. On February 1, 1997, the jury convicted her of capital murder, and on February 4 she was sentenced to death. She has not been tried for Devon's death.

Routier has always maintained that she is innocent, and her former husband has publicly supported her. According to Wikipedia, her direct appeal and a habeas corpus petition were rejected, and courts allowed further DNA testing in 2008 and again in later years. In November 2018, NBC 5 reported that a third round of testing was under way by agreement of both sides. Her attorney said then that the results so far had not established the presence of an intruder, and that a bloody fingerprint had yielded no DNA because of degradation. The Dallas County District Attorney's office said it remained confident in the conviction.
As of 2026, Wikipedia reports that the test results are still pending. Routier remains on death row in Texas and no execution date has been reported.

name: Israel Keyes Victims
summary: Israel Keyes confessed to killing Samantha Koenig, 18, abducted in Anchorage on February 1, 2012, and Bill and Lorraine Currier, who vanished from Essex, Vermont, in June 2011. He died by suicide in jail on December 2, 2012, before trial. The FBI believes he killed 11 people between 2001 and 2012; most have not been identified and the Curriers' bodies have not been found.
lastSeen: Various dates and locations across the United States

narrative: Samantha Koenig, 18, disappeared at about 8 p.m. on February 1, 2012 from the Common Grounds Espresso stand in Anchorage, Alaska, where she was working, according to a timeline published by the Anchorage Daily News. A security camera recorded her abduction, CBS News reported. In the following weeks her debit card was used and, on February 24, a text message demanding ransom was sent from her phone.

Card activity led investigators to Israel Keyes, an Anchorage resident who was by then travelling in the southern United States. He was arrested on March 13, 2012 in Lufkin, Texas. On April 2, FBI divers recovered Koenig's body from Matanuska Lake, north of Anchorage. A federal indictment made public on April 18 charged Keyes with kidnapping resulting in death, possession of ransom money and use of a stolen debit card, the Anchorage Daily News reported.

While in custody Keyes spoke repeatedly with investigators. According to the U.S. attorney for Alaska, as quoted by the Anchorage Daily News, he said he had killed Koenig, a Vermont couple and five other people. The couple were Bill and Lorraine Currier, who were last seen at their home in Essex, Vermont, on the evening of June 8, 2011. Vermont State Police say the evidence indicated they had not left voluntarily. Authorities said they were able to corroborate enough of Keyes's account to be convinced he was responsible. He was never charged in their deaths, and their bodies have not been located.

Keyes was found dead in his cell at the Anchorage jail on the morning of December 2, 2012, in what authorities described as a suicide. He had not been tried for any killing. At a briefing that day, officials said publicly for the first time that they believed he was a serial killer whose victims were strangers chosen at random, and that he had described four killings in Washington state and one in New York state.

In August 2013 the FBI released a timeline of Keyes's travels and said it believed he had committed 11 murders across the United States between 2001 and 2012, according to KTRE's report on the release. The bureau said he flew to distant cities, rented cars and drove long distances, and that he had buried caches of weapons and other items around the country in advance. CBS News reported in 2021 that the FBI believes Debra Feldman, 49, last seen in Hackensack, New Jersey, on April 8, 2009, was also a victim, although agents said they had no forensic evidence and her body has not been found.
The remaining victims have not been identified. The FBI has asked anyone with information about Keyes's movements to come forward.

name: Jennifer Pan
summary: Bich Ha Pan was shot dead and her husband Hann Pan badly wounded in a staged home invasion at their Markham, Ontario home on November 8, 2010. Their daughter Jennifer Pan and three co-accused were convicted in 2014 of first-degree murder and attempted murder. The murder convictions were overturned on appeal, a ruling upheld by the Supreme Court of Canada in 2025, and Pan later pleaded guilty to manslaughter; the attempted murder convictions stand.
lastSeen: November 8, 2010, York Region, Ontario, Canada

sources.title: Jennifer Pan - Wikipedia
A Daughter's Deadly Deception - book
Wikipedia - Killing of Bich Pan

narrative: On November 8, 2010, Bich Ha Pan was shot and killed and her husband Huei Hann Pan was critically wounded during what appeared to be a home invasion robbery in their Markham, Ontario home. Their daughter Jennifer, 24, told police that intruders had entered and demanded money.

However, investigators noticed inconsistencies in Jennifer's account. Cell phone records and other evidence revealed that Jennifer had orchestrated the attack. She had hired hitmen through her boyfriend Daniel Wong to kill her parents.

Jennifer's motive stemmed from years of living a double life. She had lied to her strict immigrant parents about graduating high school, attending college, and having a career as a pharmacist. When her parents discovered the deception and tried to separate her from her boyfriend, she planned the murders.

Jennifer Pan, Daniel Wong, David Mylvaganam and Lenford Crawford were convicted of first-degree murder and attempted murder in December 2014 and sentenced to life with no parole eligibility for 25 years; a fifth accused, Eric Carty, was dealt with separately. In 2023 the Ontario Court of Appeal ordered a new trial on the murder counts, and the Supreme Court of Canada upheld that order in 2025.

name: Karla Brown
summary: Karla Brown, 22, was found dead in the basement of the Wood River, Illinois, house she had moved into the day before, on June 21, 1978. John Prante was arrested in 1982 and convicted of her murder in 1983, in a trial that included bite mark testimony, and was sentenced to 75 years. He was released in December 2019. In 2023 the Illinois Supreme Court rejected his innocence and due process claims.
lastSeen: June 21, 1978, at her home in Wood River, Illinois

sources.title: FindLaw - People v. Prante (Illinois Supreme Court, 2023)
FindLaw - People v. Prante (Illinois Appellate Court, Fifth District, 2021)
Illinois State Bar Association - People v. Prante (May 18, 2023)
The Cinemaholic - Karla Brown Murder: Where is John Prante Now?

narrative: On June 20, 1978, Karla Brown, 22, and her fiance, Mark Fair, spent the day moving into a house they had bought in Wood River, Illinois. According to the facts set out by the Illinois Supreme Court in People v. Prante, Fair came home from work at about 5 p.m. on June 21 and found her body in the basement laundry room. She was bent over with her head and shoulders inside a metal barrel filled with water. Her hands were tied behind her back with an extension cord and two socks were knotted around her neck. She had cuts to her face, a broken jaw and bruising.

The first autopsy attributed her death to strangulation. A later examination by a second pathologist concluded that she had drowned. Police interviewed John Prante, who had been at a neighbouring house that day, on June 24 and July 5, 1978, but no one was charged and the investigation stalled.

In 1980 a forensic dentist, Dr. Homer Campbell, reviewed photographs and told police he saw bite marks on Brown's right collarbone. Her body was exhumed on June 1, 1982, and the court record states that police publicised the exhumation and the bite mark theory. Witnesses then reported that Prante had described the condition of the body, including marks on the shoulder, soon after the killing. Prante was arrested on June 8, 1982.

He was tried before a jury in Madison County in the summer of 1983. Campbell testified that Prante's teeth were consistent with the marks. The jury found Prante guilty of murder and he received an extended sentence of 75 years. His conviction was upheld on direct appeal, and petitions he filed in 1993 and 2002 were dismissed. Testing he requested in 2017 produced no interpretable DNA profile and no fingerprint match.

Prante was released from prison in December 2019 after about 36 years, The Cinemaholic reported. He has continued to maintain his innocence. In 2018 he had asked to file a new post-conviction petition, arguing that scientific reviews had discredited bite mark comparison. In April 2021 the Illinois Appellate Court, Fifth District, ruled that he could pursue a due process claim on that basis.

On May 18, 2023, the Illinois Supreme Court reversed that part of the ruling. It held that a due process claim of this kind requires an allegation that the state knowingly used false testimony, and it upheld the rejection of his actual innocence claim, finding that other evidence, including his knowledge of details of the scene, remained. The court sent three remaining claims, including ineffective assistance of counsel, back to the appellate court. The conviction has not been overturned.

name: Mary Day
summary: Mary Louise Day, 13, vanished from her family's home in Seaside, California, in the summer of 1981 and was not reported missing for more than a decade. Police opened a suspected homicide inquiry in 2002. In November 2003 a woman with identification in her name was stopped in Phoenix, and DNA showed she was the daughter of Mary's mother. Seaside police closed the case in 2017. No one was charged.
lastSeen: Summer 1981, her family's home in Seaside, California

sources.title: CBS News - Mary Day mystery: Could a suspected murder victim, back from the dead, really be an impostor?
CBS News - The mysterious disappearance of Mary Day
CBS News - Detectives thought 13-year-old Mary Day was murdered, so who was the woman claiming to be her?

narrative: Mary Louise Day was born on February 19, 1968 in Little Falls, New York. According to CBS News, her mother, Charlotte, married William Houle, a soldier whose posting took the family to Hawaii in 1978; Mary's father died later that year. In December 1980 Mary was placed in protective custody there after a finding of physical abuse. The Houles moved to Seaside, California, near Fort Ord, in January 1981, and Mary rejoined them that summer.

She disappeared from the Seaside home later in 1981, at age 13. Her parents did not report her missing. CBS News reports that her younger sister Kathy told investigators years later that Mary had been beaten by her stepfather the night before she was last seen, and that her mother said she had run away. Accounts differ on the exact date, and no police record was made at the time.

Another sister, Sherrie, who had been adopted by a different family, filed a missing persons report as an adult in the early 1990s; sources give the year as 1992 or 1994. Seaside police opened a full investigation in 2002, led by Detective Joe Bertaina. In 2003 cadaver dogs alerted in the backyard of the former family home and a child's shoe was found, but no remains were recovered. The Houles were interviewed in Kansas. According to CBS News, detectives believed at that stage that Mary had been killed. No charges were filed.

In November 2003 police in Phoenix, Arizona, stopped a pickup truck carrying stolen plates. One passenger had a recently issued Arizona identification card in the name of Mary Day with the matching birth date. Seaside's police chief at the time, Steve Cercone, told CBS's 48 Hours he suspected an impostor. A DNA test showed the woman was the biological daughter of Charlotte Houle.

Doubts continued for years. CBS News reports that the woman spoke with a Southern accent, could not recall parts of her childhood, and gave inconsistent accounts of where she had been; she said she had run away and had lived under other names. A retired detective brought in later, Mark Clark, suggested she might be a different daughter of Charlotte Houle. Cadaver dogs alerted again in 2008 at a second former Houle residence at Fort Ord, and again nothing was found.

In 2017 Acting Chief Judy Veloz reviewed the case and interviewed the woman in Missouri. CBS News reports that a photograph showing Mary alive after 1981, together with a facial comparison, led the department to conclude that she was Mary Louise Day and to close the case. She died nine days after the interview.

Her remains were recovered a month later from a shallow grave in the Spenceville Wildlife Area in Nevada County, California; she died of blunt force head injuries. Los Angeles police named her boyfriend, Christopher Spotz, as the suspect. He shot himself after a police pursuit and was never charged or tried.
lastSeen: February 23, 2018, her apartment in Hollywood, California

narrative: Adea Shabani was a 25-year-old acting student and aspiring model who, according to People magazine's reporting, was originally from Macedonia and had been in Los Angeles for less than two years. NBC News reported that she was seen at a coffee shop near her Hollywood apartment on the morning of Friday, February 23, 2018, and that surveillance footage later showed her leaving her apartment building with her boyfriend, Christopher Spotz, 33.

Friends and relatives could not reach her over the weekend, and the concern grew when she missed the first session of her acting class the following Monday, NBC News reported. According to KABC, she was reported missing on February 25. The Los Angeles Police Department's homicide detectives took over the investigation.

According to the Sierra Sun, Spotz told investigators that the two had argued and that Shabani got out of his vehicle in Santa Clarita. Los Angeles police said they found nothing to corroborate that account. The newspaper reported that Spotz was named a person of interest on March 1, that he had returned to Los Angeles on February 24, and that he drove to Colorado with his fiancee some days later.

On March 22, 2018, officers tried to stop a Toyota Tacoma that Spotz was driving. NBC News and People reported that the pursuit ran from Hesperia to the Corona area of Riverside County, where Spotz shot himself. Most outlets date his death to March 22; the Sierra Sun gives March 23. He was never charged in connection with Shabani's death.

The investigation then led detectives to the Spenceville Wildlife Area in Nevada County, in Northern California, where a shallow grave was located in the Dry Creek area on March 26 and the remains were recovered the next day, according to the Sierra Sun. The remains were identified as Shabani's on March 28 through her tattoos, and the death was ruled a homicide. In May 2018 the Nevada County chief deputy coroner said the cause of death was massive blunt force injuries to the head. Detectives believed she was buried on or about February 23 or 24.

LAPD Captain William Hayes said publicly that investigators believed Spotz was involved in her death and described him as the suspect. Because Spotz died before any charge was filed, no court has ruled on his responsibility, and police did not release a motive.

name: Ashley Ellerin
summary: Michael Gargiulo was convicted in August 2019 of murdering Ashley Ellerin, a 22-year-old fashion design student who was stabbed 47 times in her Hollywood home on February 21, 2001. He was also convicted of a 2005 murder and a 2008 attempted murder and was sentenced to death on July 16, 2021. Actor Ashton Kutcher, who had plans with Ellerin that night, testified at the trial.
lastSeen: February 21, 2001, her home on Pinehurst Road, Hollywood Hills, Los Angeles, California

CBS News - The Hollywood Ripper: How "48 Hours" helped crack the case of convicted serial killer Michael Gargiulo

narrative: Ashley Ellerin was a 22-year-old fashion design student living in a rented house on Pinehurst Road in the Hollywood Hills area of Los Angeles. On the evening of February 21, 2001, she was stabbed to death inside the house. According to CBS News, her roommate found her body early the next morning on the steps outside her bathroom; she had been stabbed 47 times.

Ellerin had arranged to go out that evening with actor Ashton Kutcher. Kutcher later testified that he spoke to her by phone earlier in the evening, arrived late at about 10:45 p.m., and got no answer at the door. He said he looked through a window, saw what he took to be spilled red wine on the floor, and left assuming she had gone out without him. CBS News reported that Ellerin's father had visited her earlier the same day.

According to CBS News, Ellerin had met Michael Gargiulo, an air conditioning repairman who lived a few blocks away, when he offered to help her with a flat tire, and friends said he afterwards turned up at the house uninvited. Detectives looked at him early on, but there was little physical evidence and no DNA linking him to the scene, and the case stalled for years.

Gargiulo was arrested by Santa Monica police in June 2008 after Michelle Murphy was attacked in her apartment and fought off her assailant; blood left at the scene yielded his DNA, according to Wikipedia's summary of the case. He was then charged with murdering Ellerin and with the December 2005 murder of Maria Bruno, 32, who lived in the same El Monte apartment complex as him. Prosecutors argued that he lived close to each victim.

His trial opened in Los Angeles Superior Court in May 2019. On August 15, 2019, after about three days of deliberation, the jury found him guilty of two counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted murder. The same jury recommended death that October. After delays that NBC News attributed to procedural issues and the pandemic, Judge Larry P. Fidler imposed the death sentence on July 16, 2021.

Gargiulo is separately charged in Illinois with the August 1993 killing of Tricia Pacaccio, 18, in Glenview. Cook County authorities charged him in 2011, and he was extradited from California in September 2024 and ordered held pending trial. No verdict in that case was found as of September 2026, and he is presumed innocent of that charge.

name: Brittney Wood
summary: Nineteen-year-old Brittney Wood vanished while on her way to meet her uncle in Mobile, Alabama. The investigation uncovered a massive family sexual abuse ring. Brittney has never been found.
lastSeen: May 30, 2012, Mobile, Alabama
narrative: On May 30, 2012, nineteen-year-old Brittney Wood disappeared in Mobile, Alabama, after leaving her mother's home to meet her uncle, Donnie Holland. Holland was found dead the same day from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The investigation into Brittney's disappearance uncovered a massive child sexual abuse ring within her own extended family. Multiple family members were charged with sexual abuse of children within the family, including abuse of Brittney from a young age.

Investigators believe that Brittney may have been killed because she was prepared to testify against family members in the abuse cases. Donnie Holland is the primary suspect in her disappearance, but his death prevented any confession or prosecution.

Despite extensive searches, including draining ponds and searching wooded areas, Brittney Wood has never been found. More than a dozen of her family members have been convicted of sexual abuse charges.

name: Cieha Taylor
summary: Cieha Taylor, 28, was last seen about 4 p.m. on February 6, 2020 in Plant City, Florida, after dropping her boyfriend at a home on Cowart Road. Around three hours later her car was found on railroad tracks at East Trapnell Road with the engine running and her phone and wallet left behind. The Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office says the case is open. She has not been found.
lastSeen: February 6, 2020, Cowart Road, Plant City, Hillsborough County, Florida

narrative: Cieha Taylor was 28 and worked at a call centre in Plant City, Florida, east of Tampa. According to NBC's Dateline, she was about 5 feet 6 inches tall with shoulder-length auburn hair, and was last known to be wearing a striped dress in gray, white, blue and red, possibly with a pink sweater.

On February 6, 2020, at about 4 p.m., she dropped her boyfriend at a residence on Cowart Road in Plant City, a short distance from her workplace. That is the last confirmed sighting. At about 7 p.m. the same day her black Toyota Solara was found roughly a mile away, on the railroad tracks at East Trapnell Road. The engine was running and no one was with the car.

Accounts of what was left behind differ slightly. Dateline reported that her cell phone and debit card were inside the vehicle. Fox 13 and Spectrum Bay News 9 reported that the driver's door was open, her purse or wallet was inside and her phone was on the ground nearby.

According to Bay News 9, the car was at first moved to the side of the road without a missing person report being taken, and her mother, Canitha Taylor, later drove it home. The family reported Cieha missing on February 9, 2020, and the vehicle was processed for evidence after that. The Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office classified her as missing and endangered. Dateline reported that deputies interviewed her boyfriend, described as the last person known to have seen her. No one has been named by the sheriff's office as a suspect.

About three weeks after the disappearance, her shoes were found on a drainage pipe near the tracks. ABC Action News reported that one month on, the sheriff's office and Homeland Security searched the area. Relatives and volunteer groups have carried out their own searches since.

In February 2022, Fox 13 reported a $10,000 reward for information, and Crime Stoppers offered up to $5,000 more, according to Bay News 9. In April 2024 the sheriff's office told Bay News 9 that the case remained open and active. Her family maintains a Facebook page, Finding Cieha, to keep attention on the case. No later development was found as of September 2026. Anyone with information is asked to call the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office at 813-247-8200.

name: Girly Chew Hossencofft
summary: Girly Chew Hossencofft disappeared from Albuquerque in 1999 during a divorce from her husband Diazien, who claimed to be a government scientist with alien DNA. He pleaded guilty to her murder in 2002; her body has never been found.
lastSeen: September 9, 1999, her apartment in Albuquerque, New Mexico

sources.title: Murder of Girly Chew Hossencofft - Wikipedia

narrative: On September 9, 1999, thirty-six-year-old Girly Chew Hossencofft, a Malaysian-born woman, disappeared from her apartment in Albuquerque, New Mexico. She was in the process of divorcing her husband, Diazien Hossencofft, who claimed to be a government scientist with extraterrestrial DNA.

Blood evidence was found in Girly's apartment, but her body was never recovered. The investigation revealed that Diazien had enlisted his girlfriend, Linda Henning, to help murder Girly. Diazien had been telling followers he was a genius scientist conducting alien research.

Diazien Hossencofft pleaded guilty to the murder in January 2002, avoiding the death penalty, and was sentenced to life in prison plus 61 years. Linda Henning was convicted of first-degree murder, kidnapping and related charges in October 2002 and sentenced to 73 years.
The case was notable for its bizarre cast of characters, including followers who believed Diazien's claims about alien DNA and government conspiracies.

name: Jessie Davis
summary: Jessie Davis, 26 and nearly nine months pregnant, was killed at her home in Lake Township, Stark County, Ohio, on June 14, 2007. Her body was found nine days later in a Summit County park. Bobby Cutts Jr., a Canton police officer and the father of her children, was convicted in February 2008 and sentenced to life in prison with parole eligibility after 57 years.
lastSeen: June 14, 2007, her home in Lake Township, Stark County, Ohio

sources.title: ABC News - Jury Spares Ex-Cop Who Killed Pregnant Girlfriend
WPVI / Associated Press - Cutts sentenced to life in prison
WOIO Cleveland 19 - Remembering Jessie Davis, One Year Later
Corrections1 / Associated Press - Mother who forgives daughter's killer fights for his release
Wikipedia - Murder of Jessie Davis

narrative: Jessie Marie Davis, 26, lived in Lake Township in Stark County, Ohio, near North Canton, with her two-year-old son, Blake. In June 2007 she was close to full term in her second pregnancy and expecting a daughter she intended to name Chloe. According to WOIO (Cleveland 19), she was killed at her home on June 14, 2007.

Her mother, Patty Porter, went to the home on June 15 and found Blake alone, the residence in disarray and no sign of her daughter, WOIO reported. Wikipedia's account adds that bleach had been spilled and furniture overturned. ABC News reported that the boy told officers, "Mommy's in the rug." Thousands of volunteers joined the search that followed, which drew national coverage.

The father of both children was Bobby Cutts Jr., then a Canton police officer. Nine days after Davis was last seen, on June 23, 2007, Cutts led investigators to her body, which had been wrapped in a comforter and left in a park about 25 miles away; Wikipedia identifies it as Hampton Hills Metro Park in Summit County. He was arrested the same day. A former high school classmate, Myisha Ferrell, was also arrested. According to Wikipedia, she pleaded guilty in November 2007 to obstruction of justice and complicity to gross abuse of a corpse and received a two-year prison sentence.

Cutts stood trial in Stark County Common Pleas Court in February 2008. He testified that Davis died accidentally when he struck her in the throat with his elbow during an argument, and that he panicked afterwards, ABC News reported. Prosecutors argued that he killed her to avoid paying child support, according to the Associated Press report carried by WPVI.

On February 15, 2008, the jury returned guilty verdicts. ABC News reported that Cutts was convicted of murder in the death of Davis and of aggravated murder in the death of the unborn child; Wikipedia lists further convictions for aggravated burglary, gross abuse of a corpse and child endangering. The jury declined to recommend the death penalty. On February 27, 2008, Judge Charles Brown Jr. imposed a life sentence under which Cutts must serve 57 years before he can be considered for parole.

Davis's mother publicly forgave Cutts and asked for leniency at sentencing. In 2017 the Associated Press reported that she had arranged prison visits between Cutts and his son and was advocating for his early release, which the report described as unlikely. No later change in his conviction or sentence was found.

name: Sherin Mathews
summary: Three-year-old adopted Indian girl Sherin Mathews was reported missing in Richardson, Texas. Her adoptive father Wesley Mathews later admitted to killing her. He was sentenced to life.
lastSeen: October 7, 2017, family home in Richardson, Texas

sources.title: Wesley Mathews conviction - NBC DFW

narrative: On October 7, 2017, Wesley Mathews reported his three-year-old adopted daughter Sherin missing from their home in Richardson, Texas. He initially claimed he had sent her outside at 3 a.m. as punishment for not drinking her milk, and that she had disappeared.
Sherin had been adopted from India in 2016. She had developmental disabilities and was small for her age. The circumstances of the report immediately raised suspicions.

Sherin's body was found in a culvert near the family home on October 22. Wesley Mathews eventually changed his story, admitting that he had force-fed Sherin milk and she had choked and died. He said he disposed of her body in a panic.

Wesley Mathews was convicted of injury to a child and sentenced to life in prison. His wife Sini Mathews was initially charged with child abandonment but the charges were dropped. The case raised questions about the oversight of international adoptions and the treatment of adopted children with disabilities.
