name: Daniel Holtzclaw Victims
summary: Oklahoma City police officer Daniel Holtzclaw was convicted on December 10, 2015, of 18 of 36 counts, including four of first-degree rape, for sexually assaulting eight Black women while on patrol. Thirteen women testified against him. The inquiry began after a woman reported an assault during a traffic stop on June 18, 2014. He was sentenced to 263 years, and his appeals were rejected in 2019 and 2020.
lastSeen: Assaults reported between December 2013 and June 2014, northeast Oklahoma City, Oklahoma

sources.title: The Guardian - Daniel Holtzclaw: former Oklahoma City police officer guilty of rape
NBC News - Ex-Oklahoma City cop Daniel Holtzclaw found guilty of rapes

Supreme Court of the United States - Docket No. 19-843, Holtzclaw v. Oklahoma

narrative: Daniel Holtzclaw was a patrol officer with the Oklahoma City Police Department who worked an evening shift, from 4 p.m. to 2 a.m., in the north-east of the city. According to Wikipedia's summary of the case, the offences for which he was tried took place between December 2013 and June 2014.

The investigation started with a single complaint. NBC News reported that a woman in her fifties came forward after an encounter with Holtzclaw on June 18, 2014. Wikipedia states that she had been stopped in her car at about 2 a.m. and reported the assault to police straight away. Sex crimes detectives then reviewed Holtzclaw's record of name checks on police databases and contacted women he had looked up, Wikipedia says, and GPS records from his patrol car were used to place him at the locations the women described, as CBS News also reported. Holtzclaw was arrested on August 21, 2014, and was dismissed from the department before his trial.

He was charged with 36 counts, among them first- and second-degree rape, forcible oral sodomy, sexual battery, procuring lewd exhibition, burglary, indecent exposure and stalking. Thirteen women, all of them Black, testified at a trial lasting about a month in late 2015. According to NBC News, several said he had threatened them with arrest over outstanding warrants or drug paraphernalia. The defence challenged the credibility of the accusers, and Holtzclaw did not give evidence.

On December 10, 2015, after about 45 hours of deliberation, the jury convicted him on 18 counts and acquitted him on the other 18, The Guardian and CBS News reported. The guilty verdicts related to eight of the thirteen women and comprised four counts of first-degree rape, one of second-degree rape, four of forcible oral sodomy, six of sexual battery and three of procuring lewd exhibition. The jury recommended sentences totalling 263 years, and the judge imposed that term on January 21, 2016, according to CBS News and Wikipedia.

Holtzclaw has maintained his innocence. His appeal questioned, among other things, the DNA evidence: Wikipedia notes that skin-cell DNA from one accuser was found on his uniform trousers and that the defence attributed it to indirect transfer. The Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals upheld the convictions on August 1, 2019. The US Supreme Court docket for case 19-843 shows that his petition for review was denied on March 9, 2020.

Because he was acquitted on half of the counts, the allegations of five of the thirteen women did not result in convictions. The record here describes only the conduct for which he was found guilty as established.

US Supreme Court denies his petition for certiorari.

name: Lauren Smith-Fields
summary: Lauren Smith-Fields, 23, was found dead in her Bridgeport, Connecticut apartment on December 12, 2021 after a first date with a man she met on a dating app. The medical examiner ruled the death an accident caused by fentanyl, prescription drugs and alcohol. Police opened a criminal investigation in January 2022; no charges have been reported. Her family sued the city over the police response.
lastSeen: December 12, 2021, her apartment in Bridgeport, Connecticut

sources.title: NPR - Conn. police probe death of Lauren Smith-Fields, found dead after a date in December
ABC News / Good Morning America - Lauren Smith-Fields' family calls for justice, cause of death released

Wikipedia - Death of Lauren Smith-Fields

narrative: Lauren Smith-Fields, a 23-year-old Black woman, lived alone in an apartment in Bridgeport, Connecticut. According to a police report described by ABC News, officers were called to the apartment just after 6:30 a.m. on December 12, 2021 and found her lying on the floor, not breathing. The 911 call was made by a man who told officers he had met her on a dating app three days earlier and that this was their first meeting in person. He said they had been drinking tequila, that she had become unwell during the evening, and that both later fell asleep; when he woke in the morning she was unresponsive. Officers described him as frantic and visibly shaken. He has not been charged with any offence.

Smith-Fields' family says the police never told them she had died. Her mother, Shantell Fields, told a Connecticut legislative committee that she went to the apartment on December 13 after being unable to reach her daughter and learned of the death from the landlord, the Connecticut Mirror reported. The family and their lawyer, Darnell Crosland, accused the Bridgeport Police Department of failing to collect evidence properly and of treating the case dismissively because of her race.

On January 24, 2022 the Connecticut Office of the Chief Medical Examiner ruled that Smith-Fields died of acute intoxication from the combined effects of fentanyl, promethazine, hydroxyzine and alcohol, and classified the death as an accident. Crosland said the family did not accept that the finding answered how the drugs were obtained or ingested. According to NPR, Bridgeport police then opened a criminal investigation through the narcotics and vice division, with assistance from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, into the factors that led to her death.

Mayor Joseph Ganim referred the handling of the case to internal affairs. ABC News reported that two detectives, Kevin Cronin and Angel Llanos, were placed on administrative leave at the end of January 2022 over the handling of this case and that of Brenda Lee Rawls, another Black woman found dead in Bridgeport the same day, and that both cases were reassigned. The Connecticut Post later reported that both detectives were reinstated. The two cases led to a 2022 change in Connecticut law requiring police to notify next of kin within 24 hours, according to CT Insider.

In December 2023 Shantell Fields filed a federal civil rights lawsuit seeking more than $30 million from the city, five police officers and Bumble Inc., the Connecticut Post reported. WSHU reported that in June 2026 the Bridgeport City Council approved a settlement under which $30,000 would go to the Smith-Fields family. In February 2023 the family told CT Insider they were still waiting for police records and had been told only that the investigation was open. No arrest or charge in connection with her death was found in the sources consulted.

name: Shanquella Robinson
summary: Twenty-five-year-old Shanquella Robinson died on a group trip to Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. Video showed her being beaten by a friend. Her death was ruled homicide but no extradition has occurred.
lastSeen: October 29, 2022, a vacation rental in San José del Cabo, Mexico

sources.title: Wikipedia - Killing of Shanquella Robinson

narrative: On October 29, 2022, twenty-five-year-old Shanquella Robinson of Charlotte, North Carolina died while on a vacation trip with friends in San José del Cabo, Mexico. Her companions initially told her mother she had died of alcohol poisoning.

Video emerged showing Shanquella being brutally beaten by one of her friends in the vacation rental. The Mexican autopsy determined her cause of death was severe spinal cord injury and atlas luxation—consistent with a violent beating.
Mexican authorities issued an arrest warrant for one of Shanquella's travel companions, but as of 2024, no extradition has been carried out by the United States.
The case highlighted jurisdictional complications in international homicide cases and raised questions about accountability when Americans are killed abroad by other Americans.

name: Hart Family
summary: Six adopted children aged 12 to 19 died on March 26, 2018, when Jennifer Hart drove the family's SUV off a cliff on Highway 1 near Westport, California, with her wife Sarah also inside. A coroner's inquest jury ruled in April 2019 that the women died by suicide and the children at the hands of another. The crash came days after a child-welfare visit to their Washington home. Devonte Hart's remains were never found.
lastSeen: March 26, 2018, Highway 1 pullout near Westport, Mendocino County, California

sources.title: The Mendocino Voice - Inquest jury finds Hart parents intentionally killed themselves and their six adopted children (includes sheriff's release)
The Press Democrat - Jury finds Hart family crash on Mendocino Coast was murder-suicide
OPB - Hart Parents Intentionally Killed Adopted Children, Jury Rules
Wikipedia - Hart family murders

narrative: Jennifer and Sarah Hart, both 38, and their six adopted children died when the family's SUV went over a coastal cliff beside Highway 1 near Westport, in Mendocino County, California, on March 26, 2018. The children were Markis, 19, Hannah, 16, Devonte, 15, Jeremiah, 14, Abigail, 14, and Ciera, 12, according to the Mendocino County Sheriff's Office. The Press Democrat reported that the couple had adopted two sets of three siblings from foster care in Texas.

The family had drawn the attention of child-welfare authorities in several states. According to Wikipedia's summary of contemporary reporting, Sarah Hart pleaded guilty to an assault charge in Minnesota after one of the girls reported being hurt in 2010, and Oregon authorities looked into the family in 2013 without reaching a conclusion about the children's safety. After the family moved to Woodland, Washington, neighbors reported that Hannah and Devonte had come to them asking for help, the Press Democrat reported.

On March 23, 2018, a child protective services worker went to the Woodland home at about 5:30 p.m. and got no answer, according to inquest testimony reported by the Press Democrat. The family was on the road by about 8:30 that evening and reached Fort Bragg, California, the next day. A California Highway Patrol investigator testified that a man sleeping in a camper at the same pullout heard a vehicle arrive at about 11 p.m. on March 25 and heard an engine revving at about 3 a.m. on March 26.

Highway patrol analysts testified that data from the vehicle showed it had been stopped, then accelerated at full throttle to about 20 mph before leaving the cliff, and that no mechanical defect was found. According to testimony reported by the Press Democrat and OPB, Jennifer Hart had a blood-alcohol level of 0.10 percent, Sarah Hart had a toxic level of diphenhydramine, the active ingredient in Benadryl, and several of the children had enough of the drug to make them sleep. Searches on Sarah Hart's phone during the trip asked about overdoses and drowning.

The two women and three of the children, Markis, Jeremiah and Abigail, were found at the crash site. Ciera's remains washed ashore about ten days later, and partial remains of Hannah were found the following month, the Press Democrat reported. Devonte's remains have not been found; a Mendocino County judge declared him and Hannah dead in March 2019.

Sheriff-Coroner Tom Allman convened a coroner's inquest, the county's first in 52 years, on April 3, 2019. On April 4 the 14-member jury unanimously found that Jennifer and Sarah Hart died by suicide and that each of the six children died at the hands of another person, other than by accident. The sheriff's office said the children's death certificates would record homicide. Because both adults died, there was no criminal prosecution.

narrative: On February 2, 2018, Gloria Satterfield, 57, the longtime housekeeper for the Murdaugh family, was found with severe head injuries at the Murdaugh home in Hampton County, South Carolina. Alex Murdaugh claimed she tripped over his dogs on the front steps.
Gloria died on February 26 from her injuries. Alex Murdaugh encouraged her sons to file a wrongful death suit against him, directing them to his friend/attorney Cory Fleming.

name: Don Lewis
summary: Millionaire exotic animal owner Don Lewis vanished in Tampa, Florida on August 18, 1997 and was declared legally dead in 2002. The Netflix series 'Tiger King' revived interest in the case and aired accusations against his wife Carole Baskin, who denies any involvement and has never been charged. The case remains unsolved.
lastSeen: August 18, 1997, his home in Tampa, Florida

sources.title: Tiger King - Netflix
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Don Lewis

narrative: On August 18, 1997, Jack Donald 'Don' Lewis, a 59-year-old millionaire who owned numerous exotic animals in Tampa, Florida, vanished. His van was later found at a small airport, but there was no evidence he boarded a plane.

Lewis's wife Carole (now Carole Baskin) inherited his estate after he was declared legally dead in 2002. His family accused her of involvement in his disappearance and contested the will, which they claimed had been forged.

The case received renewed attention in 2020 with the Netflix series 'Tiger King,' in which Joe Exotic accused Baskin of murdering Lewis and feeding him to her big cats. Baskin has always denied any involvement.
In 2020, the case was officially reopened by the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office. Despite new leads and increased scrutiny, no charges have been filed and Don Lewis has never been found.

timeline.event: Don Lewis disappears from Tampa.

name: Mallory Beach
summary: Mallory Beach, 19, died when a boat carrying six young people struck a bridge at Archers Creek near Beaufort, South Carolina, early on February 24, 2019. Her body was found on March 3. Paul Murdaugh, 19, was charged with boating under the influence causing death and pleaded not guilty; the charges were dropped after he was shot dead in June 2021. No one was tried.
lastSeen: February 24, 2019, Archers Creek, Beaufort County, South Carolina

sources.title: CBS News - Mallory Beach death: Inside the boat crash that killed S.C. teen
GBH / NPR - Murdaugh boat crash suit ends in a $15 million settlement for family of teen who died
WTOC - Mallory Beach's father questions boat crash investigation 5 years after her death
Wikipedia - Death of Mallory Beach
Wikipedia - Murdaugh family

narrative: Mallory Beach, 19, was one of six young people aboard a boat that struck the bridge at Archers Creek, near Parris Island in Beaufort County, at about 2:20 a.m. on February 24, 2019. According to CBS News, the others on board were Paul Murdaugh, Morgan Doughty, Anthony Cook, Connor Cook and Miley Altman. NPR reporting carried by GBH said the group had been returning from an oyster roast and that the boat hit a channel marker and the bridge pilings. Beach was thrown into the water.

A search lasted eight days. Her body was found on March 3, 2019, about five miles from the bridge. Wikipedia's article on the case, citing local reporting, says two volunteers found her and that the cause of death was drowning.

On April 18, 2019, Paul Murdaugh, then 19, was charged with three felony counts of boating under the influence, one for causing Beach's death and two for causing great bodily injury to other passengers. He pleaded not guilty and was released on bond. CBS News reported that a hospital test taken some hours after the crash put his blood alcohol level at about three times the legal limit. The case never went to trial: Paul Murdaugh and his mother, Maggie, were shot dead at the family's property on June 7, 2021, and the charges against him were then dropped. The allegations were therefore never tested in court.

Beach's family has questioned how the crash was investigated. In a 2024 interview with WTOC, her father, Phillip Beach, said he believed the investigation had been interfered with; he pointed to the absence of alcohol from the official accident report and to the removal of an investigator whose wife had a connection to the Murdaugh family's law firm. The South Carolina Attorney General's office would neither confirm nor deny to WTOC that any investigation of those concerns existed. No one has been convicted of obstructing the inquiry.

The family pursued a wrongful-death suit alleging that Paul Murdaugh, who was under age, bought alcohol at a Parker's convenience store using his older brother's identification. According to CBS News, a judge approved a settlement with Maggie Murdaugh's estate in January 2023. In July 2023 Parker's agreed to pay $15 million to settle the Beach family's claim, with further payments to the surviving passengers, and CBS reported that Alex Murdaugh settled with the family in October 2024. Alex Murdaugh was convicted in March 2023 of murdering his wife and son; according to Wikipedia, the South Carolina Supreme Court overturned those convictions in May 2026 and prosecutors have said they intend to retry him.

name: Dena Dean
summary: Fifteen-year-old Dena Dean was found stabbed to death in a park in Tamworth, England on her way to school. Despite extensive investigation, her killer has never been identified.
lastSeen: February 5, 2001, Wigginton Park, Tamworth, Staffordshire, England
narrative: On February 5, 2001, fifteen-year-old Dena Dean was found stabbed in Wigginton Park in Tamworth, Staffordshire, England. She had been walking through the park on her way to school.
Dena had been stabbed multiple times. Despite hundreds of witnesses being in the area at the time, no one reported seeing the attack.
Staffordshire Police launched a massive investigation, interviewing thousands of people and conducting extensive forensic analysis. DNA evidence was recovered but has not led to a match.
The case remains open. Police have issued periodic appeals for information and conducted cold case reviews. No suspect has ever been publicly identified.

timeline.event: Dena Dean found stabbed in Wigginton Park.

name: Jorge Torres Jr.
summary: Jorge Torres Jr. was found dead inside a suitcase in Winter Park, Florida. His girlfriend Sarah Boone claimed he died during a hide-and-seek game. She filmed him begging to be let out.
lastSeen: February 23, 2020, their apartment in Winter Park, Florida

sources.title: Wikipedia - Murder of Jorge Torres

narrative: On February 23, 2020, Sarah Boone called 911 to report that her boyfriend Jorge Torres Jr., 42, was dead inside a suitcase in their Winter Park, Florida apartment. She claimed they had been playing hide-and-seek while drinking and she had fallen asleep.
Police found videos on Boone's phone that told a different story. In the recordings, Torres can be heard begging to be let out, saying he couldn't breathe. Boone is heard laughing and taunting him.
The medical examiner determined Torres died of suffocation. His death was ruled a homicide.
Boone was charged with second-degree murder. The case was delayed extensively as she cycled through multiple attorneys. She was convicted in 2024 and sentenced to life in prison.

timeline.event: Jorge Torres Jr. found dead in a suitcase.

name: RJR Maintenance Murders
summary: Four people were murdered at RJR Maintenance in Mandan, North Dakota. Chiropractor Chad Isaak, a tenant of the property management company, was convicted after his car was caught on surveillance.

narrative: On April 1, 2019, four people were found shot and stabbed at RJR Maintenance & Management in Mandan, North Dakota. The victims were property manager Robert Fakler (52), and employees Adam Fuehrer (42), Bill Cobb (50), and Lois Cobb (45).

Surveillance cameras in the area captured a distinctive pickup truck and SUV near the business at the time of the murders. The vehicles were traced to Chad Isaak, 44, a chiropractor from Washburn, North Dakota.
Isaak was a tenant of the property management company. He had disputes with management about property maintenance issues. Bloody clothing and a knife matching the crime were found in his home.
Isaak was convicted of four counts of murder in 2021 and sentenced to four consecutive life sentences without parole. His motive was never fully established beyond the landlord-tenant dispute.

name: Jordan Neely
summary: Jordan Neely, a 30-year-old homeless man experiencing a mental health crisis on a New York City subway train, died after being placed in a chokehold by fellow passenger Daniel Penny on May 1, 2023. Penny's manslaughter charge was dismissed after the jury deadlocked, and he was acquitted of criminally negligent homicide on December 9, 2024. The case sparked debate about mental health, homelessness, and self-defense.
lastSeen: May 1, 2023, F train, Broadway-Lafayette station, Manhattan, New York City

sources.title: Death of Jordan Neely - Wikipedia
Wikipedia - Killing of Jordan Neely

narrative: On May 1, 2023, Jordan Neely, 30, a homeless man known for his Michael Jackson impersonations, boarded an F train in Manhattan and began yelling that he was hungry and tired and didn't care if he went to prison. Witnesses said he threw his jacket on the floor.

Daniel Penny, 24, a Marine veteran, placed Neely in a chokehold from behind. Other passengers helped restrain Neely. Penny held the chokehold for approximately six minutes. Neely was pronounced dead at the hospital.
Penny was charged with second-degree manslaughter and criminally negligent homicide. The case became highly politicized, with some calling Penny a hero and others calling it unjustified killing.

In December 2024 the second-degree manslaughter charge was dismissed at prosecutors' request after the jury deadlocked on it (December 6), and the jury then acquitted Penny of criminally negligent homicide (December 9). The verdict further polarized public opinion.

narrative: On June 2, 2018, chef and instructor Daniel Brophy was found shot dead in the kitchen of the Oregon Culinary Institute in Portland where he taught early morning classes.

Investigation revealed that his wife Nancy Crampton Brophy, a self-published romance novelist, had purchased a gun and a ghost gun kit in the months before the murder. Surveillance footage placed her near the culinary school at the time of the killing.

Nancy had written a blog post in 2011 titled 'How to Murder Your Husband,' in which she discussed various methods and motives for spousal murder. The trial judge excluded the essay from evidence, ruling it inadmissible on the first day of trial.

Nancy Brophy was convicted of second-degree murder on May 25, 2022 and sentenced to life with the possibility of parole after 25 years. Prosecutors argued the motive was financial, pointing to life insurance policies totaling about $1.4 million.

narrative: On June 6, 2019, seventeen-year-old Nikki Kuhnhausen, a transgender girl, disappeared from Vancouver, Washington. She was last seen getting into a car with a man identified through social media as David Bogdanov.
Bogdanov initially denied knowing Nikki but cell phone records placed them together. He later admitted they had a sexual encounter and he killed her after discovering she was transgender.
Nikki's remains were found in a wooded area of Clark County in December 2019, six months after her disappearance. She had been strangled.
Bogdanov was convicted on August 27, 2021 of second-degree murder and malicious harassment, Washington's hate-crime offense, and was sentenced on September 9, 2021 to about 20 years in prison.

name: Dayton Shooting
summary: Nine people were killed and 17 wounded by gunfire when Connor Betts, 24, opened fire in Dayton's Oregon District at about 1:05 a.m. on August 4, 2019. Police officers on patrol nearby shot and killed him about 32 seconds after the first shot. The FBI closed its investigation in November 2021, finding he acted alone. A friend was sentenced to 32 months on federal firearms charges.
lastSeen: August 4, 2019, Oregon District, Dayton, Ohio

sources.title: Time - Dayton Shooting Lasted Just 32 Seconds and Left 9 Dead
Ideastream Public Media - FBI concludes investigation into the 2019 mass shooting in Dayton's Oregon District
Dayton 24/7 Now - Criminal investigation into Oregon District mass shooting has closed
WCPO - Memorial honoring victims unveiled on 5-year anniversary of Oregon District shooting in Dayton
Wikipedia - 2019 Dayton shooting

narrative: At about 1:05 a.m. on August 4, 2019, a gunman opened fire on East Fifth Street in the Oregon District, a nightlife area of Dayton, Ohio. According to Time, the shooting lasted from 1:05:35 to 1:06:07 a.m. The attacker, 24-year-old Connor Betts of Bellbrook, wore body armour and a mask and carried an AR-15-style .223 calibre firearm fitted with a 100-round drum magazine. He fired about 41 rounds.

Nine people were killed: Lois Oglesby, 27; Saeed Saleh, 38; Derrick Fudge, 57; Logan Turner, 30; Nicholas Cumer, 25; Thomas McNichols, 25; Beatrice Warren-Curtis, 36; Monica Brickhouse, 39; and the gunman's 22-year-old sibling, named by authorities as Megan Betts. Seventeen people were wounded by gunfire, according to the FBI's closing summary as reported by Ideastream, and news reports put the total number injured at 27, including people hurt while fleeing.

Six Dayton police officers who were already on patrol in the district ran toward the gunfire and shot Betts as he approached the entrance of the Ned Peppers bar. Time reported that the officers fired 65 rounds. In January 2020, Montgomery County Prosecutor Mat Heck Jr. announced that the case would not go to a grand jury because a review by his office had found it clear that the officers acted in self-defence and in defence of others, Dayton 24/7 Now reported. The criminal review was then closed.

A friend of the gunman, Ethan Kollie, was prosecuted in federal court. Kollie pleaded guilty to illegally possessing firearms and to lying on a federal firearms transaction form, and in February 2020 he was sentenced to 32 months in prison. Investigators said he had helped Betts obtain firearm parts, body armour and the drum magazine. He was not charged with taking part in the attack.

The FBI and Dayton police announced the end of their investigation in late November 2021. The inquiry involved more than 125 interviews and the review of about 400 hours of security video, and was slowed by encrypted digital evidence. According to Ideastream's report on the findings, the FBI concluded that Betts acted alone, was not directed by any organisation or aligned with a specific ideological group, and had fantasised about mass shootings and murder-suicide for years. Investigators found no indication that he had told family or friends what he intended, and said he had probably broken federal law by lying about drug use when he bought the weapon.
A permanent memorial to the victims, called the Seed of Life, was unveiled in the Oregon District on August 4, 2024, the fifth anniversary of the attack, WCPO reported.

timeline.event: At about 1:05 a.m. Connor Betts opens fire in Dayton's Oregon District, killing nine people; police shoot and kill him about 32 seconds after the first shot.

name: Joel & Lisa Guy Sr.
summary: Joel Guy Sr., 61, and Lisa Guy, 55, were stabbed to death and dismembered at their home in west Knox County, Tennessee, over Thanksgiving weekend 2016. Their son, Joel Guy Jr., was convicted on October 2, 2020, of first-degree murder and abuse of a corpse and received two consecutive life sentences plus four years. Prosecutors said the motive was financial.
lastSeen: November 25, 2016, at their home on Goldenview Lane in west Knox County, Tennessee

sources.title: ABC7 Chicago / Associated Press - Man charged with killing, dismembering parents after Thanksgiving
WVLT - Knox Co. parents found dissolving in 'diabolical stew of human remains,' investigators say
WVLT - Who is Joel Guy Jr.?
The Daily Beast - Convicted Murderer Who Dismembered Parents Sentenced to Additional 4 Years Behind Bars
Wikipedia - Murders of Joel and Lisa Guy

narrative: Joel Michael Guy Sr., 61, and his wife Lisa Guy, 55, lived on Goldenview Lane in the Hardin Valley area of west Knox County, Tennessee. Guy Sr. was a civil engineer originally from Surgoinsville, and the couple were preparing to retire to a home in Hawkins County, WVLT reported. Their son, Joel Michael Guy Jr., then 28, lived in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and came to the house for Thanksgiving 2016 along with other relatives.

The Knox County Sheriff's Office said the couple were last seen on Friday, November 25, and were believed to have been killed that day or the next, according to an Associated Press report carried by ABC7 Chicago. Wikipedia's account of the trial evidence gives the date as Saturday, November 26. On Monday, November 28, Lisa Guy's supervisor called 911 after she failed to arrive at work, and deputies carrying out a welfare check found the couple's remains inside the house.

Both had been stabbed many times and dismembered. Prosecutors told the jury that Guy Sr. had 42 sharp-force injuries and Lisa Guy 31, and that remains had been placed in containers of corrosive liquid, WVLT reported. Guy Jr. was arrested on a fugitive warrant at his Baton Rouge apartment on Tuesday, November 29, 2016, after being placed under surveillance by the FBI and sheriff's deputies.

The trial opened in Knox County on September 28, 2020. Prosecutors argued the killings were planned and the motive was money. Relatives testified that the parents intended to stop supporting their son financially once they retired. According to WVLT, investigators recovered a notebook containing a list of steps to take before and after the killings and notes about Lisa Guy's $500,000 life insurance. Wikipedia's account says the defence presented no evidence.

On October 2, 2020, the jury found Guy Jr. guilty of first-degree premeditated murder, felony murder and abuse of a corpse in relation to both parents, according to Wikipedia's summary of local reporting. He received two consecutive life sentences. The Daily Beast reported that Judge Steve Sword later added four years for the abuse of a corpse counts and said the defendant had shown no remorse.

Wikipedia, citing the Knoxville News Sentinel, reports that an appeal was rejected in May 2023 and that Guy Jr. is held at Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee. No later change to the convictions or sentence was found.

name: Stephen Smith
summary: Nineteen-year-old Stephen Smith was found dead on a rural Hampton County road in July 2015. His death was initially treated as a hit-and-run, though no vehicle debris was found. South Carolina investigators reopened the case in 2021 and announced in 2023 that it is being investigated as a homicide; no one has been charged.
lastSeen: July 8, 2015, Sandy Run Road, Hampton County, South Carolina

sources.title: Death of Stephen Smith - Wikipedia
Smith case - FITSNews
Wikipedia - Murdaugh family

narrative: On July 8, 2015, nineteen-year-old nursing student Stephen Smith was found dead in the middle of Sandy Run Road in rural Hampton County, South Carolina. He was a gay young man in a small, conservative community.

The initial investigation classified his death as a hit-and-run, but the pathologist noted that his injuries were inconsistent with a vehicle strike—there was no vehicle debris, no road rash, and his shoes were still on.

During the original investigation, the Murdaugh name appeared in investigators' notes as unverified rumor. No member of the Murdaugh family has been named a suspect or charged, and Buster Murdaugh has publicly denied any involvement in Stephen's death.

In June 2021, SLED opened an investigation into Stephen's death based on information gathered during the Murdaugh double-homicide inquiry. In March 2023 SLED announced it was treating the death as a homicide, and his body was exhumed for an independent autopsy. No arrests have been made.

name: Russell Williams Victims
summary: Col. Russell Williams, commander of Canadian Forces Base Trenton, pleaded guilty in October 2010 to the first-degree murders of Cpl. Marie-France Comeau and Jessica Lloyd in eastern Ontario, along with two sexual assaults and 82 break-in offences. He was arrested on February 7, 2010, and on October 21, 2010 received two life sentences with no parole eligibility for 25 years.
lastSeen: November 2009 (Brighton) and January 28, 2010 (Belleville), Ontario, Canada

sources.title: CBC News - Williams gets 2 life terms for 'despicable crimes'
CBC News - Col. Russell Williams timeline

Wikipedia - Russell Williams (criminal)

narrative: Russell Williams was a colonel in the Canadian Forces and the commander of Canadian Forces Base Trenton in eastern Ontario, described by the CBC as Canada's largest military air base. According to a CBC biography, he was born in England on March 7, 1963, and moved to Canada as a child. In October 2010 he pleaded guilty to 88 criminal charges, including two counts of first-degree murder.

The offences he admitted began with break-ins. He pleaded guilty to 82 counts of breaking and entering and attempted breaking and entering at homes in Ottawa, Belleville and Tweed, which the CBC reported involved thefts of a fetishistic nature. In September 2009 two women in Tweed, where Williams had a cottage, were confined and sexually assaulted in their homes in separate incidents on September 17 and September 30, according to the CBC's timeline of the case.

Cpl. Marie-France Comeau, a member of the military who lived in Brighton, Ontario, was found dead in her home on November 25, 2009, and her death was ruled a homicide. The CBC gave her age as 38. Jessica Lloyd, 27, of Belleville sent a text message to a friend late on January 28, 2010, and did not arrive at work the next day. Police appealed for help and searched the area for more than a week.

Williams was arrested in Ottawa on February 7, 2010, and charged with both murders and the two Tweed sexual assaults. Lloyd's body was found the next day off a road in Tweed, and sources told the CBC that Williams had led police to it. According to Wikipedia's account, police had stopped Williams during a roadside canvass a few days earlier and matched the tires on his vehicle to tracks found near Lloyd's home, and he confessed during a long interview on February 7 conducted by Detective Sergeant Jim Smyth of the Ontario Provincial Police. On April 29, 2010, he was charged with 82 further offences relating to the break-ins.

Williams pleaded guilty to all charges in Ontario Superior Court in Belleville on October 18, 2010. After the Crown presented an agreed statement of facts over two days, he was formally convicted. On October 21, Justice Robert F. Scott sentenced him to two terms of life in prison with no chance of parole for 25 years, 10 years for each of the sexual assault and forcible confinement counts, and one year for each of the 82 other charges. Williams told the court he was deeply ashamed and apologized to the families of the two women. The Crown did not seek a dangerous offender designation.

On October 22, 2010, Governor General David Johnston agreed to revoke Williams's commission, stripping him of his rank. The chief of the defence staff said the military would also remove his medals, recover his pay from the date of his arrest and release him for service misconduct, while noting that there were no legal grounds to revoke his pension. In November 2010 the Canadian Forces burned his uniforms at CFB Trenton. He began his sentence at Kingston Penitentiary.

summary: Fashion mogul Peter Nygard was arrested for racketeering and sex trafficking charges involving dozens of women. He was convicted in Canadian courts of sexual assault.

sources.title: Peter Nygard - Wikipedia

narrative: Peter Nygard, a Finnish-Canadian fashion mogul worth hundreds of millions, was arrested in Winnipeg, Manitoba on December 14, 2020 on federal charges in the United States, including racketeering and sex trafficking.

Allegations spanned decades. Nygard was accused of using his wealth and fashion empire to lure young women—some underage—to his properties in the Bahamas and elsewhere, where they were drugged and sexually assaulted.

Nygard faced charges in both the U.S. and Canada. At his Toronto trial he was convicted on November 12, 2023 of four counts of sexual assault, and on September 9, 2024 he was sentenced to 11 years in prison. Further proceedings in Canada and the United States were still pending.
The case was often compared to Jeffrey Epstein's, with Nygard similarly using wealth, power, and a network of employees to facilitate the abuse of vulnerable women over many years.

name: Derrick Todd Lee Victims
summary: Derrick Todd Lee was convicted in 2004 of murdering Geralyn DeSoto and Charlotte Murray Pace and was sentenced to death for the Pace killing. Authorities linked him by DNA to the deaths of other women in the Baton Rouge and Lafayette areas of Louisiana between 1998 and 2003. He was arrested in Atlanta on May 27, 2003, and died in custody on January 21, 2016.
lastSeen: Various dates between 1998 and 2003, Baton Rouge and Lafayette areas, Louisiana

sources.title: WBRZ - Timeline of events: Serial killer Derrick Todd Lee
CNN - Serial killings suspect described as charming (May 29, 2003)
WAFB - Officials confirm convicted serial killer Derrick Todd Lee has died (archived)
WAFB - 10 years ago DNA linked Derrick Todd Lee to serial killings
Wikipedia - Derrick Todd Lee

narrative: Between 2001 and 2003 a series of killings of women in and around Baton Rouge, Louisiana, was tied together by DNA. According to a timeline published by WBRZ, Gina Wilson Green was found raped and strangled in her home on Stanford Avenue, near Louisiana State University, on September 24, 2001. Geralyn DeSoto, 21, was found dead at home by her husband on January 14, 2002. Charlotte Murray Pace, 22, was found stabbed to death in her apartment on May 31, 2002.

WAFB reported that in July 2002 the Louisiana State Police crime lab found the same unknown DNA profile at the Green and Pace scenes, and the Baton Rouge police chief announced that a single killer appeared to be responsible. That same month Pam Kinamore, 44, was taken from her home; her body was found days later near the Whiskey Bay exit of Interstate 10. Trineisha Dene Colomb, 23, was abducted from Lafayette in November 2002, and LSU graduate student Carrie Lynn Yoder, 26, was abducted in March 2003. WBRZ reported that DNA linked all of these cases.
On July 9, 2002, Diane Alexander was attacked in her home in Breaux Bridge and survived when her son arrived. She helped police produce a composite sketch.

According to CNN, police in Zachary, north of Baton Rouge, had long regarded Lee as suspicious in connection with two local cases from 1992 and 1998, and obtained a court order for a sample of his DNA on May 5, 2003. After the composite sketch was released, Zachary officers urged the task force to have his sample tested quickly. It matched. An arrest warrant for the murder of Carrie Yoder was issued on May 26, 2003, and Atlanta police arrested Lee the next day. He was returned to Louisiana that week. Wikipedia's account states that investigators had earlier focused on white men because of an offender profile and witness reports; that point is not confirmed in the other sources opened.

On August 10, 2004, a West Baton Rouge Parish jury convicted Lee of the second-degree murder of Geralyn DeSoto, and he received a life sentence. A second jury convicted him of the first-degree murder of Charlotte Murray Pace, and he was sentenced to death in October 2004. He was not tried for the other killings. WAFB reported that he was suspected in seven deaths between 1998 and 2003, including that of Randi Mebruer of Zachary, who disappeared in 1998.

Lee remained on death row at the Louisiana State Penitentiary. A corrections department spokeswoman told WAFB that he died on the morning of January 21, 2016, at a hospital where he had been taken several days earlier. He was 47. The prosecutor in the DeSoto trial said Lee had denied responsibility to the end.

name: Waneta Hoyt Children
summary: Waneta Hoyt murdered her five children between 1965 and 1971, presenting each death as SIDS. Her case was cited in medical literature supporting SIDS research before the truth emerged.
lastSeen: 1965-1971, Owego, Tioga County, New York

sources.title: Waneta Hoyt - Wikipedia

narrative: Between 1965 and 1971, Waneta Hoyt of Owego, New York lost all five of her children—Erik, James, Julie, Molly, and Noah—to what was diagnosed as Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS). Each child died between the ages of 48 days and 28 months.

A prominent pediatrician published Hoyt's cases in medical literature as evidence supporting theories about SIDS and genetic vulnerability. The cases were influential in shaping medical understanding of infant death for decades.
In 1994, a prosecutor reopened the cases. Under interrogation, Hoyt confessed to smothering all five children, saying she killed them because she couldn't tolerate their crying. She later recanted.

Hoyt was convicted of five counts of second-degree murder in 1995 and sentenced to 75 years to life. She died in prison in 1998. The case led to reforms in how infant deaths are investigated and how SIDS is diagnosed.

name: Yingying Zhang
summary: Yingying Zhang, a 26-year-old visiting scholar from China at the University of Illinois, was abducted from a bus stop in Urbana on June 9, 2017, and killed. Brendt Christensen, a former physics graduate student, was convicted in federal court in June 2019 and sentenced to life in prison without release. Her remains have not been recovered; they are believed to lie in a landfill near Danville.
lastSeen: June 9, 2017, near North Goodwin Avenue and West Clark Street, Urbana, Illinois

narrative: Yingying Zhang came to the United States from China in April 2017 as a visiting scholar at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where she worked in the Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences. According to CNN, relatives said she hoped to become a university professor, and she kept in regular contact with her parents by video call.

On the afternoon of June 9, 2017, Zhang, 26, was on her way to sign an apartment lease. CNN, citing court documents, reported that she was last seen getting into a car at a bus stop. Wikipedia's account of the investigation says that security cameras recorded her entering a black Saturn Astra in Urbana shortly after 2 p.m., having missed a bus, and that investigators traced the car through registration records to Brendt Christensen, a Champaign resident who had recently left the university's physics graduate program.

Her disappearance drew wide attention in China and among Chinese students in the United States. Her family travelled to Illinois and, CNN reported, offered a reward of up to 40,000 dollars. The FBI arrested Christensen on June 30, 2017, according to Wikipedia, and a federal grand jury indicted him on a charge of kidnapping resulting in death, along with counts of making false statements to investigators.

The trial was held in federal court in June 2019. In his opening statement Christensen's own attorney told jurors that his client had killed Zhang, so the central question became the penalty. The jury found him guilty that month. Jurors could not agree unanimously on a death sentence, and on July 18, 2019, the judge sentenced him to life in prison without the possibility of release. At sentencing Zhang's father asked Christensen to say where his daughter was.

The answer became public on August 7, 2019. According to WTTW and CBS Chicago, Christensen's lawyers had given prosecutors his account in November 2018 under an agreement that it would not be used at trial. By that account, he put her remains in garbage bags in a dumpster outside his Champaign apartment the day after the killing; the contents were collected days later and taken to a private landfill near Danville, in Vermilion County, where they were compacted and have since been buried under more than 30 feet of refuse.

The family's attorney said any attempt at recovery would be complicated and costly, with no certainty of success, and Zhang's father acknowledged that finding her might be impossible. In August 2019 the family and the university announced Yingying's Fund, an endowment to help international students and their families in crisis, Illinois Public Media reported.

narrative: On May 24, 2012, Luka Magnotta murdered Jun Lin, a 33-year-old Chinese international student, in his Montreal apartment. Magnotta filmed the murder, dismemberment, and acts of necrophilia, then posted the video online.
Magnotta mailed body parts to the offices of political parties and elementary schools in Ottawa and Vancouver. A torso was found in a suitcase behind Magnotta's apartment building.
Magnotta fled to France and then Germany, where he was arrested at an internet café in Berlin on June 4, 2012, while reading news articles about himself.

Magnotta was convicted of first-degree murder in 2014 and sentenced to life with no parole eligibility for 25 years. The case was the subject of the Netflix documentary 'Don't F**k with Cats,' which traced how internet sleuths identified Magnotta before the murder through animal cruelty videos.

narrative: Stephen Port, a chef from Barking, East London, murdered four young men between June 2014 and September 2015 by administering lethal doses of the drug GHB. He met his victims through dating apps.
The four victims—Anthony Walgate (23), Gabriel Kovari (22), Daniel Whitworth (21), and Jack Taylor (25)—were all found dead in or near a churchyard in Barking, near Port's flat.

Despite the similarities in location and circumstances, police initially treated each death as non-suspicious, attributing them to drug overdoses. This failure was later condemned as reflecting institutional homophobia.

Port was convicted of four murders, four rapes, and multiple sexual assaults in 2016 and sentenced to a whole-life order. A subsequent inquest found that police failures contributed to the deaths of at least three victims.

narrative: Peter Sutcliffe, known as the Yorkshire Ripper, murdered 13 women and attempted to murder seven others across northern England between 1975 and 1980. His victims included sex workers and women walking alone at night.

Sutcliffe was caught in January 1981 when police found him with a sex worker in Sheffield. He was convicted of 13 murders and sentenced to 20 concurrent life sentences. He was given a whole-life tariff in 2010.
The investigation was one of the largest and most criticized in British police history. Mistakes included ignoring a key tip and being misled by hoax letters and tape recordings from 'Wearside Jack.'
Sutcliffe died on November 13, 2020 at HMP Frankland, Durham, from COVID-19. He had tested positive and refused treatment. His death came 39 years into his imprisonment.

name: Grace Millane
summary: British backpacker Grace Millane was strangled in a central Auckland hotel apartment on the night of December 1-2, 2018, the eve of her 22nd birthday, after a date with a man she met on Tinder. Jesse Kempson was found guilty of her murder in November 2019 and sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 17 years. His appeal was dismissed in December 2020.

narrative: Grace Millane, a university graduate from Essex, England, was travelling through New Zealand as part of a round-the-world trip when she was killed in Auckland. According to a timeline published by RNZ, she arrived in the country on November 20, 2018. On December 1, the day before her 22nd birthday, she sent her family a photograph of a Christmas tree at Sky City, which was the last contact they had with her.

That evening she met a man she had matched with on the dating app Tinder. RNZ's court reporting says police later assembled CCTV footage showing the pair visiting bars in the central city before going to his apartment in the CityLife Hotel. Wikipedia's summary of the evidence puts the last footage of her at 9:41 pm. When birthday messages went unanswered, her family reported her missing on December 5, and her father travelled to Auckland to appeal for information.

Police announced a homicide inquiry on December 8, 2018, and arrested and charged a 26-year-old man the same day. According to RNZ, he first told detectives they had parted at about 10 pm, then said she had died in his apartment and that he had moved her body. Her remains were found on December 9 in a suitcase in a shallow grave in the Waitākere Ranges, west of Auckland. CCTV shown at trial recorded him wheeling a suitcase out of the hotel about 24 hours after she had entered it.

The trial opened in the High Court at Auckland on November 4, 2019. The prosecution said he strangled her; the defence said her death was an accident during consensual sexual activity. A pathologist told the court that the neck bruising would have required sustained force. After about five hours of deliberation the jury returned a unanimous guilty verdict on November 22, 2019. On February 21, 2020, he was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum non-parole period of 17 years.

The defendant's name was suppressed in New Zealand throughout the trial because he faced further charges. RNZ reported that in two judge-alone trials in October and November 2020 he was found guilty of eight charges of violent and sexual offending against a former partner and of raping another woman, and received prison terms of seven and a half years and three and a half years.

The Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the murder conviction and sentence on December 18, 2020. On December 22, 2020, the Supreme Court declined a further application and name suppression lapsed, allowing New Zealand media to identify him as Jesse Shane Kempson. According to Wikipedia, the Supreme Court refused leave to appeal the murder conviction in June 2021.

name: Ivan Milat (Backpacker Murders)
summary: Seven backpackers aged 19 to 22, from Australia, Germany and Britain, disappeared while hitchhiking from Sydney between December 1989 and April 1992; their bodies were found in the Belanglo State Forest in 1992 and 1993. Ivan Milat was arrested in May 1994, convicted of all seven murders in July 1996 and given seven consecutive life sentences. He died in prison in October 2019.
lastSeen: December 1989 to April 1992, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

narrative: Seven young travellers who had set out to hitchhike from Sydney between 1989 and 1992 were found dead in the Belanglo State Forest, south-west of Sydney in New South Wales. According to ABC News, they were Deborah Everist and James Gibson, both 19, from Victoria; Simone Schmidl, 21, from Germany; Anja Habschied, 20, and Gabor Neugebauer, 21, a couple also from Germany; and Caroline Clarke, 21, and Joanne Walters, 22, from Britain. ABC News reported that all had been travelling south along the Hume Highway.

Everist and Gibson were last seen in Sydney in December 1989, SBS News reported. Schmidl disappeared in January 1991 while hitchhiking towards Melbourne, and Habschied and Neugebauer left Kings Cross in December 1991. Clarke and Walters left a Kings Cross hostel in April 1992. Their bodies were the first to be found, in September 1992. The remains of Everist and Gibson were located in October 1993, and those of Schmidl, Habschied and Neugebauer in November 1993. The Guardian reported that the bodies had been covered with branches and leaf litter. Several victims had been stabbed and two had been shot in the head.

A key witness was Paul Onions, a British backpacker. On January 25, 1990 he accepted a lift near Liverpool from a man who called himself Bill. When the driver produced a gun near the turn-off to the forest, Onions ran and was picked up by a passing motorist. He reported the attack that day. After reading about the discoveries in the forest, he contacted New South Wales police again on November 13, 1993, according to ABC News, and in 1994 he identified Ivan Milat from police photographs.

Police surrounded Milat's home at Eagle Vale, on the outskirts of Sydney, on May 22, 1994 and arrested him. Clive Small, who led the investigation, wrote in the Sydney Morning Herald that the search of the property had taken weeks to plan. ABC News reported that officers found clothing, camping equipment and other possessions of the victims, together with weapons and ammunition.

Milat was charged with seven counts of murder and with the abduction of Onions. After a trial lasting about four months, a jury found him guilty of all charges in July 1996. He was sentenced to seven consecutive life terms, plus six years for the abduction, without the possibility of parole. The sentencing judge, Justice David Hunt, said the victims had been treated with callous indifference.

Milat never admitted to the murders. He was diagnosed with terminal cancer of the oesophagus and stomach in May 2019 and died in the hospital wing of Long Bay jail at 4.07am on October 27, 2019, aged 74, according to Corrective Services NSW. Former detectives told ABC News they suspected him of other killings, but he was not charged with any further murders.

lastSeen: October 16, 2021, in her family's tent at the Blowholes campsite, Macleod, north of Carnarvon, Western Australia

narrative: Cleo Smith, aged four, lived in the coastal town of Carnarvon, Western Australia, with her mother, stepfather and baby sister. In October 2021 the family went camping at the Quobba Blowholes, a remote site north of the town and about 900 kilometres north of Perth. According to BBC News, it was the first night of their holiday.

Cleo was last seen by her mother when she woke during the night and asked for water. When her parents got up at about 6:00 am on October 16, she and her sleeping bag were gone. ABC News reported that the tent's zip had been opened to a height the child could not have reached. A land, air and sea search began that day, and a task force of more than 100 officers was formed. After about a week the Western Australian government offered a reward of A$1 million.

The BBC reported that campers had heard a car leaving the campground at about 3:00 am, and that detectives worked through statements from people at the campsite, CCTV footage and phone data. Reporting on the later sentencing, the BBC said the breakthrough reportedly came when a mobile phone was traced to a tower near the campsite around the time she was taken.

At about 1:00 am on November 3, 2021, police forced their way into a locked house in Carnarvon, a short drive from the family's home, and found Cleo alone in a room. According to ABC News, she told the officers her name, and Police Commissioner Chris Dawson said the man taken into custody had no connection to her family. She was reunited with her parents the same day.

Terence Darrell Kelly, then 36, was charged the following day with forcibly taking a child under 16. On January 24, 2022, he pleaded guilty to child stealing by video link to Carnarvon Magistrates Court, ABC News reported. On April 5, 2023, Chief Judge Julie Wager of the Perth District Court sentenced him to 13 years and six months in prison, describing the offence as being at the highest level of seriousness. The court heard that he kept Cleo for the full 18 days in a bedroom with a door altered to lock from outside. The judge also acknowledged severe childhood trauma and neurological impairment in his background. He must serve more than 11 years before he can be considered for parole.

Kelly appealed against the length of the sentence. On September 30, 2024, the Western Australian Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, with one of the three judges dissenting on the question of whether the sentence was manifestly excessive, according to ABC News.

name: April Jones
summary: Mark Bridger was convicted on 30 May 2013 of abducting and murdering five-year-old April Jones, who was taken from the Bryn-y-Gog estate in Machynlleth, Wales, on 1 October 2012. He received a whole-life order at Mold Crown Court. April's body was never found; bone fragments and her blood were recovered at his cottage in Ceinws.
lastSeen: October 1, 2012, at about 7:15 p.m., Bryn-y-Gog estate, Machynlleth, Powys, Wales

narrative: April Jones, aged five, was abducted on the evening of 1 October 2012 while playing on her bicycle with friends on the Bryn-y-Gog estate in Machynlleth, a market town in Powys, mid-Wales. According to a timeline published by The Guardian, she was taken at about 7:15 p.m., and a seven-year-old friend told police that April had got into a vehicle. Her mother, Coral Jones, called 999 at 7:29 p.m. and the first officer arrived minutes later.

Dyfed-Powys Police declared a critical incident, and residents began searching that night. The BBC reported that the operation became the largest missing person search in UK police history, covering around 650 areas and drawing help from 45 other forces. The child witness's account led detectives to Mark Bridger, a local man who had recently moved into a rented cottage in the village of Ceinws, a few miles from Machynlleth. He was arrested on the afternoon of 2 October 2012 on suspicion of abduction and was arrested on suspicion of murder on 5 October after DNA testing identified April's blood in the cottage.

Bridger told police, and later the jury, that he had accidentally run April over and could not remember what he had done with her body. At trial the court heard that fragments of bone consistent with a juvenile human skull were found in the ashes of his wood burner, that April's blood was found in several places in the cottage, and that the property had been extensively cleaned. The BBC also reported that indecent images of children were found on his computer.

The trial opened at Mold Crown Court on 29 April 2013. On 30 May 2013 the jury unanimously found Bridger, then 47, guilty of abduction, murder and perverting the course of justice after a little over four hours of deliberation. Mr Justice Griffith Williams sentenced him to life imprisonment with a whole-life order, meaning he will not be considered for release. Bridger later applied for permission to appeal against the sentence, but the Judicial Office confirmed in January 2014 that he had abandoned the application.

April's body has never been recovered. Police ended the search on 22 April 2013, shortly before the trial. After the verdict the BBC reported that Bridger had told a prison chaplain he had put the body in a river; that account was not placed before the jury. A funeral was held at St Peter's Church in Machynlleth on 26 September 2013, attended by hundreds of people. According to Wikipedia, the Welsh Government bought the cottage in Ceinws in August 2014 and it was demolished that November.

narrative: On October 11, 2014, Jennifer Laude, a 26-year-old transgender Filipina woman, was found dead in a motel bathroom in Olongapo City, Philippines. She had been drowned in a toilet.

U.S. Marine Private First Class Joseph Scott Pemberton was identified as the last person with Jennifer. He told investigators he discovered she was transgender during an intimate encounter and 'felt repulsed.'
The case ignited protests about the Visiting Forces Agreement between the U.S. and the Philippines. Pemberton was convicted of homicide (not murder) by a Philippine court and sentenced to 6-12 years.

In 2020, Philippine President Duterte controversially granted Pemberton an absolute pardon after he had served nearly six years. The decision was condemned by LGBTQ+ advocates and Filipino nationalists.

name: Otto Warmbier
summary: American student Otto Warmbier was detained in North Korea for 17 months and returned to the U.S. in a vegetative state. He died days later. North Korea claimed he contracted botulism.

sources.title: Otto Warmbier - Wikipedia

narrative: Otto Warmbier, a 22-year-old University of Virginia student, was detained in North Korea in January 2016 during a tourist visit. He was sentenced to 15 years hard labor for allegedly stealing a propaganda poster from his hotel.

In June 2017, North Korea released Warmbier in a state of unresponsive wakefulness. He had been in this condition for over a year, unknown to the outside world. North Korea claimed he contracted botulism and fell into a coma after taking a sleeping pill.

Warmbier died on June 19, 2017, six days after returning to the United States. Doctors found no evidence of botulism. The exact cause of his brain injury remains unknown—possibilities include torture, poisoning, or an attempted suicide.

A U.S. federal judge ruled North Korea liable for Warmbier's torture and death in 2018, awarding his family over $500 million in damages. The full circumstances of what happened to Otto in custody may never be known.

name: Jamal Khashoggi
summary: Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was killed and dismembered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul by a team of Saudi agents. Eight people were convicted in a closed Saudi trial. A declassified 2021 U.S. intelligence assessment concluded that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman approved an operation to capture or kill him; the crown prince denies ordering the killing and has never been charged.

narrative: On October 2, 2018, Saudi journalist and Washington Post columnist Jamal Khashoggi entered the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey to obtain papers for his upcoming marriage. He never came out.

Turkish intelligence determined that a 15-member team of Saudi agents, including a forensic doctor with a bone saw, had been dispatched to Istanbul. They killed Khashoggi within minutes of his entering the consulate and dismembered his body.

U.S. media reported in November 2018 that the CIA had concluded Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) ordered the killing, and a declassified U.S. intelligence assessment released in February 2021 stated that he approved an operation to capture or kill Khashoggi; he denies ordering the killing and has not been charged. Saudi Arabia initially denied knowledge, then claimed it was a rogue operation, then admitted the killing.

Eight Saudi nationals were convicted in a Saudi court (five sentenced to death, later commuted to 20 years). The case was widely seen as a politically motivated assassination meant to silence a prominent critic of the Saudi regime.

narrative: On November 1, 2006, former Russian FSB officer Alexander Litvinenko, who had defected to the UK and become a vocal critic of Putin, met two Russian contacts at the Millennium Hotel in London. He became violently ill that evening.

Litvinenko was poisoned with polonium-210, an extremely rare radioactive substance. It took doctors nearly three weeks to identify the poison. Litvinenko died on November 23 in University College Hospital.

On his deathbed, Litvinenko accused Vladimir Putin of ordering his murder. The British public inquiry and, in 2021, the European Court of Human Rights found that Andrei Lugovoy and Dmitri Kovtun carried out the poisoning; neither man was ever tried and both denied involvement.

A 2016 British public inquiry concluded that the operation was 'probably approved' by Putin and FSB director Nikolai Patrushev. Russia refused to extradite Lugovoy, who denies involvement; Kovtun, who also denied involvement, died in Moscow on June 4, 2022.

narrative: On March 4, 2018, former Russian military intelligence officer Sergei Skripal, 66, and his daughter Yulia, 33, were found unconscious on a bench in Salisbury, England. They had been poisoned with Novichok, a military-grade nerve agent.
The nerve agent had been applied to the front door handle of Sergei's home. A police officer, Detective Sergeant Nick Bailey, was also contaminated and hospitalized. All three survived.

In June 2018, two unrelated individuals found a discarded perfume bottle containing Novichok. Dawn Sturgess died after spraying herself with it, thinking it was perfume. Her partner Charlie Rowley survived.

British authorities identified two GRU officers—'Alexander Petrov' and 'Ruslan Boshirov' (aliases)—through CCTV and travel records. Investigative journalists later identified them as Colonel Anatoliy Chepiga and Dr. Alexander Mishkin. Russia denied involvement.

name: Junko Furuta
summary: Junko Furuta, a 17-year-old high school student from Misato, Saitama, was abducted on November 25, 1988, and held for about 40 days in a house in Adachi, Tokyo, where she died on January 4, 1989. Her body was recovered from a concrete-filled drum on March 29, 1989. Four teenagers were tried and convicted; on appeal in 1991 the longest sentence was raised to 20 years.
lastSeen: November 25, 1988, Misato, Saitama Prefecture, Japan (abducted while cycling home)

sources.title: Wikipedia - Murder of Junko Furuta
Unseen Japan - Furuta Junko: The Horrific Murder That Tested Japan
Tokyo Reporter - Junko Furuta killer again on trial: Chaos in the courtroom

narrative: Junko Furuta was a 17-year-old senior at Yashio-Minami High School who lived in Misato, Saitama Prefecture. According to the account summarised by Wikipedia and Unseen Japan, she was cycling home on the evening of November 25, 1988, when two teenage boys stopped her. One knocked her from her bicycle and the other approached her as though offering help. She was sexually assaulted and then taken to the home of one of the boys in the Ayase area of Adachi ward, Tokyo.

She was kept in an upstairs room of that house for roughly 40 days. Court findings reported by those sources describe repeated rape, beatings, burning and starvation carried out mainly by four youths aged 16 to 18, with other young men taking part in some of the sexual assaults. Some outlets, including Tokyo Reporter, give the period as 44 days, but the interval between the abduction and her death is 40 days.

Furuta died on January 4, 1989. Wikipedia gives the cause as traumatic shock following a further assault. The following day the youths wrapped her body, placed it in a metal drum, filled the drum with concrete and left it on vacant land in Wakasu, Koto ward.

The killing came to light through an unrelated investigation. According to Unseen Japan, two of the group were arrested in January 1989 over another offence, and the death was disclosed during police questioning about a separate rape case. Police recovered the drum on March 29, 1989, and the body was identified by fingerprints. The remaining members of the group were arrested afterwards.

The four principal defendants were tried in the adult criminal courts even though they were minors. In July 1990 the Tokyo District Court imposed a 17-year term on the defendant treated as the leader and shorter indeterminate terms on the others. Prosecutors had asked for life imprisonment for the leader. In July 1991 the Tokyo High Court increased three of the sentences, to 20 years, five to nine years and five to seven years, and left the fourth at five to ten years. Wikipedia reports that the parents of the lead defendant paid 50 million yen in compensation to the Furuta family.

The case is known in Japan as the concrete-encased high school girl murder case. Unseen Japan reports that the weekly magazine Shukan Bunshun published the defendants' names in 1989 despite the anonymity normally given to juveniles, and that criticism of the sentences fed a later debate that led Japan to lower the age of criminal responsibility from 16 to 14. All four men were eventually released. According to Tokyo Reporter and Wikipedia, three of them were later arrested for new offences, including one who received a suspended sentence in 2019 over a 2018 assault in Kawaguchi, Saitama.

name: Natascha Kampusch
summary: Ten-year-old Natascha Kampusch was kidnapped on her way to school in Vienna and held captive by Wolfgang Priklopil for over eight years in a basement dungeon. She escaped in 2006.

narrative: On March 2, 1998, ten-year-old Natascha Kampusch was abducted on her way to school in Vienna, Austria. Her kidnapper, Wolfgang Přiklopil, imprisoned her in a purpose-built dungeon beneath his house in Strasshof an der Nordbahn.
For over eight years, Natascha was held in a 54-square-foot cell. As she grew older, Přiklopil allowed her more freedom within the house during the day but continued to abuse her.
On August 23, 2006, while Přiklopil was distracted by a phone call as Natascha cleaned his car in the garden, she ran away and alerted a neighbor. She was 18 years old.

Přiklopil fled when he realized Natascha had escaped and killed himself by jumping in front of a train that same evening. Natascha has since become an author and media personality, though she has expressed complicated feelings about her captor.

narrative: On November 15, 2004, Peter Porco was attacked with a fireman's axe while sleeping in his Delmar, New York home. His wife Joan was also struck but survived. In a bizarre detail, Peter apparently got up after the attack and went about his morning routine—making his lunch, getting the newspaper—before collapsing and dying.
When a paramedic asked Joan Porco if her son Christopher did this, she nodded yes. But after recovering, Joan denied Chris was responsible and became his staunchest defender.

Evidence showed Chris had driven from his college at the University of Rochester, used a stolen key, and attacked his parents over disputes about money and forged loans. Toll records placed his car on the route.
Chris Porco was convicted of second-degree murder and attempted murder in 2006 and sentenced to 50 years to life. Joan Porco testified in his defense.

narrative: On August 29, 1995, Mark Winger called 911 claiming that a shuttle driver named Roger Harrington had broken into his Springfield, Illinois home and was beating his wife Donnah with a hammer. Mark said he shot Harrington to save Donnah.
Donnah died from her injuries. Mark was hailed as a hero—a husband who tried to save his wife. He collected insurance money and remarried.

Four years later, Mark's friend DeAnn Schultz went to police. She revealed that Mark had been having an affair with her and had expressed a desire to get rid of Donnah. She also disclosed that Mark had deliberately lured Harrington to the house.

name: Joe Andriano
summary: Joe Andriano, who was terminally ill with cancer, was killed in his Phoenix apartment on October 8, 2000. He had been struck at least 23 times on the head and stabbed in the neck, and sodium azide was found in his blood. His wife, Wendi Andriano, was convicted of first-degree murder in 2004 and sentenced to death; her appeals have so far failed and she remains on Arizona's death row.
lastSeen: October 8, 2000, apartment in the Ahwatukee area of Phoenix, Arizona

sources.title: FindLaw - State v. Andriano (Arizona Supreme Court, 2007)
vLex - Andriano v. Shinn, No. CV-16-01159-PHX-SRB (D. Ariz. 2021)
ABC15 Arizona - Woman kills husband seriously ill with cancer

Death Penalty Information Center - Women on death row

narrative: Joe Andriano lived with his wife, Wendi, and their two children in an apartment complex in the Ahwatukee area of Phoenix, where she worked as the property manager. According to the Arizona Supreme Court's 2007 opinion in State v. Andriano, he had been diagnosed in 1998 with adenoid cystic carcinoma, which had spread to his lungs, and he was terminally ill by the autumn of 2000.

The court's summary of the trial evidence says the couple went to a barbecue on October 7, 2000, and returned home around midnight. At about 2:15 a.m. Wendi Andriano called a co-worker to the apartment, where Joe was lying on the floor, vomiting and struggling to breathe. Paramedics who arrived after a first emergency call were sent away. A second call was made at 3:39 a.m., and responders then found Joe Andriano dead in a pool of blood.

The medical evidence described in the opinion was that he had received at least 23 blows to the back of the head and a deep stab wound to the neck, and that traces of sodium azide, a toxic chemical, were in his blood. Investigators found a 500-gram bottle of sodium azide and capsules filled with it in the couple's storage unit. The opinion also records that Wendi Andriano had tried several times to buy insurance on her husband's life, telling insurers he did not have cancer.

At trial in Maricopa County in 2004 she testified that the poisoning had been part of an assisted suicide that her husband wanted, that he later became violent, and that she struck him with a bar stool in self-defense. She also said she had been abused; ABC15 reported that friends testified they had not seen signs of abuse. The jury convicted her of first-degree murder. ABC15 gives the verdict date as November 18, 2004, and the death sentence as December 22, 2004. The jury found one aggravating factor, that the killing was especially cruel.

The Arizona Supreme Court affirmed the conviction and sentence on July 9, 2007. A state post-conviction court later held a hearing on claims that her lawyers had been ineffective at the penalty phase and had a conflict of interest, and rejected them; the Arizona Supreme Court declined review. She filed a federal habeas petition in March 2017, which U.S. District Judge Susan Bolton denied on January 19, 2021.

Wendi Andriano is held at the state women's prison at Perryville. The Death Penalty Information Center's list of women under sentence of death, current to June 24, 2026, still included her. No execution date was found in the sources reviewed.

name: Liam Fee
summary: Two-year-old Liam Fee died at his home near Glenrothes, Fife, Scotland, on March 22, 2014, from heart injuries caused by blunt force trauma. His mother, Rachel Fee, and her civil partner, Nyomi Fee, were convicted of his murder in May 2016 and given life sentences with minimum terms of 23.5 and 24 years. Rachel Fee's appeal was refused in March 2017.
lastSeen: March 22, 2014, at his home near Glenrothes, Fife, Scotland

sources.title: BBC News - Liam Fee: Mother and partner given life sentences
BBC News - Rachel Fee's murder appeal rejected

Scottish Government - Significant Case Review

narrative: Liam Fee was two and a half years old when he died at his home near Glenrothes in Fife, Scotland, on March 22, 2014. According to BBC News, he had suffered a ruptured heart caused by severe blunt force trauma. The court heard that the damage resembled injuries seen in road crash victims, that he had more than 30 external injuries, and that he had an untreated broken leg and fractured arm in the days before he died.

His mother, Rachel Fee, who is also known as Rachel Trelfa, and her civil partner, Nyomi Fee, were charged with his murder. Both women were originally from Ryton in Tyne and Wear, the BBC reported. They denied the charges and claimed that another young boy was responsible for Liam's death.

The trial ran for seven weeks at the High Court in Livingston before the judge, Lord Burns. The jury retired on May 27, 2016, and by May 31 had found both women guilty, by majority, of assault and murder. According to the BBC, they were also convicted of a series of offences of cruelty against two other boys, who cannot be named for legal reasons, and of attempting to defeat the ends of justice by trying to blame one of those boys for the death.

On July 6, 2016, at the High Court in Edinburgh, Lord Burns sentenced both women to life imprisonment. Rachel Fee was ordered to serve a minimum of 23 and a half years and Nyomi Fee a minimum of 24 years. The judge said the post-mortem findings showed Liam had been subjected to a prolonged course of violent behaviour. Counsel for Nyomi Fee said she accepted responsibility for neglecting Liam but maintained she had not murdered him.

Rachel Fee appealed against her conviction, arguing that the jury should have been given the option of a culpable homicide verdict in her case. The Court of Criminal Appeal refused the appeal in a written opinion delivered by Lord Turnbull in March 2017; Scottish Legal News dates the decision to March 10.

The trial heard that Liam's childminder, his nursery and a member of the public had each raised concerns with social services in 2013, and a senior social worker acknowledged in evidence that his case had at one stage dropped out of view. A significant case review commissioned by the Fife Child Protection Committee was published on June 20, 2017, and the Scottish Government said it would consider the national implications. A social worker involved in Liam's case was later removed from the register by the Scottish Social Services Council, which also pointed to systemic failings at the council, the BBC reported.

name: Daniel Pelka
summary: Daniel Pelka, 4, died of a head injury on March 3, 2012, in Coventry, England, after months of starvation and beatings. His mother, Magdalena Luczak, and her partner, Mariusz Krezolek, were convicted of murder at Birmingham Crown Court in 2013 and jailed for life with minimum terms of 30 years. A serious case review found that agencies missed chances to help him.
lastSeen: March 3, 2012, at his home in Coventry, West Midlands, England

sources.title: BBC News - Daniel Pelka murder: Mother and partner given life
