Wikipedia - Murder of Daniel Pelka

narrative: Daniel Pelka was four years old when he died on March 3, 2012, in Coventry, England. According to the BBC, he died from a head injury at his home after being starved and beaten over a period of months. He weighed just over a stone and a half, roughly 10 kilograms, and the trial judge said medical experts regarded his emaciation as unprecedented in Britain.

Daniel lived with his mother, Magdalena Luczak, and her partner, Mariusz Krezolek, both originally from Poland. In her sentencing remarks, published by the BBC, Mrs Justice Cox said their relationship began in early 2010 and that Daniel had appeared healthy before then. She found that the first sign of ill treatment was a broken arm about 14 months before his death, and that systematic cruelty probably began when he started school in September 2011.

The court heard that Daniel was denied food, made to swallow salt, forced to perform punishment exercises, subjected to cold water punishment and shut in a small room. Staff at Little Heath Primary School noticed bruising and saw him taking food from other children's lunch boxes and scavenging for food. The judge said the couple gave the school and doctors a false account that he had an eating disorder, which was designed to prevent anyone from intervening.

Luczak and Krezolek denied murder and blamed each other. A jury at Birmingham Crown Court found both guilty, and Wikipedia gives the verdict date as July 31, 2013. They were sentenced in early August 2013 to life imprisonment with minimum terms of 30 years each. In December 2014 the Court of Appeal rejected Krezolek's attempt to challenge his conviction and dismissed both defendants' claims that their sentences were excessive, the BBC reported.

A serious case review by Coventry's Safeguarding Children Board was published in September 2013. According to the BBC, it recorded 26 incidents that required police involvement at the family home between 2006 and 2010, several involving domestic abuse, and set out a series of missed opportunities involving police, health staff, social care and the school. The review concluded that Daniel had been invisible at times and that no professional had tried hard enough to speak to him directly. A GP later received a formal warning for failing to act adequately on concerns raised about the boy.

Both of the people convicted have since died in custody. Luczak, 29, was found in her cell at HMP Foston Hall in Derbyshire in July 2015, and the BBC later reported that she had been found hanged. Krezolek, 36, was found unresponsive in his cell at HMP Full Sutton on January 27, 2016.

name: Marc Dutroux Victims
summary: Six girls aged 8 to 19 were abducted in Belgium in 1995 and 1996; four died and two were rescued alive from a hidden cellar on August 15, 1996, two days after Marc Dutroux was arrested. In June 2004 a jury in Arlon convicted Dutroux, who was sentenced to life in prison. Three co-defendants also received prison terms. Failures in the investigation led to mass protest and reform.
lastSeen: Abducted between June 1995 and August 1996 in Grâce-Hollogne, Ostend, Tournai (Kain) and Bertrix, Belgium

sources.title: NBC News - Notorious child rapist-murderer convicted
NBC News - Belgian child killer imprisoned for life
VRT NWS - Court reporter looks back on Marc Dutroux case that shook Belgium

narrative: Between June 1995 and August 1996 six girls and young women were abducted in Belgium. According to VRT and Euronews, eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Mélissa Russo disappeared from Grâce-Hollogne, near Liège, on June 24, 1995. An Marchal, 17, and Eefje Lambrecks, 19, vanished in August 1995 while on holiday in Ostend. Sabine Dardenne, 12, was taken in May 1996 while cycling to school near Tournai, and Laetitia Delhez, 14, was taken on August 9, 1996 after leaving a swimming pool in Bertrix.

Marc Dutroux, who had earlier been convicted of sexual offences and released early, was arrested on August 13, 1996 together with his then wife Michelle Martin and Michel Lelièvre. The Brussels Times reports that a witness to the Bertrix abduction had noted part of a vehicle registration, which led investigators to him. Two days later, on August 15, Dardenne and Delhez were found alive in a concealed cellar in his house in Marcinelle, a district of Charleroi. According to Wikipedia's summary of the case, the bodies of Lejeune and Russo were recovered on August 17, 1996 and those of Marchal and Lambrecks on September 3, 1996.

Reporting by NBC News on the trial states that the two eight-year-olds starved in the cellar while Dutroux was in custody for several months on a vehicle theft case, and that Marchal and Lambrecks were drugged and buried alive. Euronews and The Brussels Times describe how police searched the house during that period without finding the hidden cell, that an officer who heard voices attributed them to noise from outside, and that seized videotapes were not reviewed.

Public anger at the handling of the investigation grew after the investigating judge, Jean-Marc Connerotte, was removed from the case. On October 20, 1996 about 300,000 people joined the White March in Brussels, according to VRT, and the affair led to reforms of Belgium's police and justice system. Wikipedia records that Dutroux briefly escaped from custody in April 1998 and was recaptured within hours.

The trial opened in Arlon on March 1, 2004. On June 17, 2004 a twelve-member jury convicted Dutroux of abducting the six girls and of killing Marchal, Lambrecks and an accomplice, Bernard Weinstein, NBC News reported. On June 22 he was sentenced to life imprisonment. Martin received 30 years and Lelièvre 25 years. Michel Nihoul was acquitted of involvement in the kidnappings and received five years for drug and people trafficking offences.

Martin was conditionally released in 2012 and Lelièvre in 2019, according to Euronews. RTBF reported in June 2025 that Dutroux, then 67, remained in prison and that legal experts considered conditional release very unlikely, since the conditions set by law were not met.

narrative: In August 1984, Josef Fritzl lured his 18-year-old daughter Elisabeth into the basement of their family home in Amstetten, Austria, where he drugged her and locked her in a purpose-built cellar. He would keep her imprisoned for 24 years.

During her captivity, Fritzl repeatedly raped Elisabeth, fathering seven children. Three of the children were raised upstairs by Fritzl and his wife, who believed Elisabeth had abandoned them. Three remained in the cellar. One died shortly after birth.

The case was discovered in April 2008 when 19-year-old Kerstin, one of the cellar children, fell critically ill and was taken to hospital. Elisabeth persuaded Fritzl to let her accompany Kerstin, and she told authorities the truth.
Fritzl was convicted of murder (the baby who died), enslavement, rape, incest, and imprisonment in 2009. He was sentenced to life in a psychiatric institution.

narrative: On February 26, 2024, thirteen-year-old Madeline Soto was reported missing from Kissimmee, Florida by her mother's boyfriend Stephan Sterns, who claimed he dropped her off at school. The school had no record of her arrival.

Madeline's body was found in a rural area of St. Cloud, Florida on March 1, 2024. Investigation revealed Sterns had been sexually abusing Madeline for years—thousands of images of child sexual abuse material involving Madeline were found on his devices.
Sterns was charged with first-degree murder and over 60 counts of sexual offenses against Madeline. Evidence showed the abuse had been ongoing since she was approximately 8 years old.

The state initially sought the death penalty, but on July 21, 2025 Sterns pleaded no contest to murder and guilty to the sex-crime charges and was sentenced to life in prison without parole. The case prompted outrage about how the abuse went undetected for so long and raised questions about the mother's awareness.

name: Laken Riley
summary: Laken Riley, a 22-year-old Augusta University nursing student, was killed on February 22, 2024 while running on a trail on the University of Georgia campus in Athens. Jose Antonio Ibarra, a Venezuelan national, was found guilty on all ten counts at a bench trial on November 20, 2024 and sentenced to life without parole. A judge denied his motion for a new trial in March 2026.
lastSeen: February 22, 2024, running toward Oconee Forest Park near Lake Herrick, University of Georgia campus, Athens, Georgia

narrative: Laken Hope Riley was 22 and studying nursing at Augusta University's college of nursing in Athens, Georgia. She had graduated from River Ridge High School in Cherokee County and had previously attended the University of Georgia, according to Atlanta News First. On the morning of February 22, 2024 she went for a run on the University of Georgia campus.

According to the timeline summarized by Wikipedia from trial testimony, Riley texted and called her mother shortly before 9:05 a.m., and a security camera recorded her jogging toward Oconee Forest Park at about that time. Her phone placed a 911 call at 9:11 a.m., and data from her smartwatch indicated that her heart stopped at 9:28 a.m. A roommate reported her missing to university police shortly after noon, and an officer found her body about half an hour later in a wooded area behind Lake Herrick, near the intramural fields. The medical examiner found that she died of blunt force trauma and asphyxiation.

University of Georgia police arrested Jose Antonio Ibarra, then 26, on the evening of February 23, 2024, FOX 5 Atlanta reported. He was charged with malice murder, felony murder, kidnapping and related offences, and a judge denied bond the following morning. Police Chief Jeff Clark described the killing as a crime of opportunity and said investigators had found no prior connection between Riley and Ibarra. He said it was the first homicide on the campus in at least 30 years. Ibarra is a Venezuelan national who, according to the sources consulted, had entered the United States unlawfully in 2022.

A grand jury indicted Ibarra on ten counts in May 2024 and he pleaded not guilty. He waived his right to a jury, and the case was heard as a bench trial before Athens-Clarke County Superior Court Judge H. Patrick Haggard beginning November 15, 2024. Prosecutors presented DNA, fingerprint, video and smartwatch evidence, along with testimony from Riley's roommates, police officers and forensic examiners. The defence argued that the evidence was circumstantial. On November 20, 2024 Judge Haggard found Ibarra guilty on all ten counts and sentenced him to life in prison without the possibility of parole for malice murder, with additional terms on other counts, Atlanta News First reported.

The case drew national attention because of Ibarra's immigration status and featured in the 2024 presidential campaign. Congress passed the Laken Riley Act in January 2025 and President Trump signed it; according to UPI, the law provides for the detention of immigrants arrested for offences such as theft, burglary and shoplifting.

In March 2026 Judge Haggard denied Ibarra's motion for a new trial, writing that the evidence against him was overwhelming, UPI reported. His lawyers had argued that his rights were violated by the denial of two pretrial motions, one seeking a delay so a defence expert could review DNA evidence and one seeking to exclude cellphone evidence. They had 30 days to appeal the ruling.

name: Rachel Morin
summary: Rachel Morin, a 37-year-old mother of five, was raped and murdered on the Ma & Pa Trail in Bel Air, Maryland, on August 5, 2023; her body was found the next day. Victor Martinez-Hernandez, a Salvadoran national arrested in Tulsa, Oklahoma, in June 2024, was convicted on April 14, 2025, and sentenced on August 11, 2025, to life without parole plus a second life term and 40 years.
lastSeen: August 5, 2023, Ma & Pa Trail, Bel Air, Harford County, Maryland

narrative: Rachel Morin, a 37-year-old mother of five from Bel Air, Maryland, went out on the Ma & Pa Trail on the evening of August 5, 2023, and did not come home. According to CBS News Baltimore, she stopped responding to messages at about 7 p.m. She was reported missing, and the following day her body was found in a drainage culvert roughly 150 feet from the trail. The Harford County Sheriff's Office treated the death as a homicide.

DNA recovered at the scene gave investigators an early lead. WMAR-TV reported that within days the profile was matched to an unsolved home invasion in Los Angeles in March 2023, in which a woman and a nine-year-old girl were assaulted. The match linked the two crimes but did not supply a name, and the search for the person responsible lasted about ten months.

On the night of June 14, 2024, officers arrested Victor Antonio Martinez-Hernandez, then 23, at a bar in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and the Harford County Sheriff's Office announced the arrest the next day. News reports, citing the sheriff's office and federal officials, said he was a citizen of El Salvador who had entered the United States unlawfully in February 2023. Officials also said he was wanted in connection with a killing in El Salvador; that allegation has not been tried in the proceedings described here. He was returned to Maryland and charged with first-degree murder and first-degree rape.

The trial was held in Harford County Circuit Court in April 2025 after the judge denied a defence request to move it elsewhere. According to CBS News Baltimore, prosecutors told jurors that the defendant's DNA was present on every piece of evidence they presented, and that a phone seized at his arrest contained searches relating to the Bel Air area. The defence argued that there was no motive and that he had never known Morin. On April 14, 2025, after deliberating for less than an hour, the jury found him guilty of first-degree premeditated murder, first-degree rape, a third-degree sex offence and kidnapping.

On August 11, 2025, he received the maximum sentence on each count: life without the possibility of parole for the murder, a consecutive life term for the rape, and a further 40 years for the remaining counts. Members of Morin's family addressed the court; her sister told reporters the family would always feel her absence but had gained some closure.

State's Attorney Alison Healey said she expected the defence to appeal and was confident the sentence would stand, WMAR-TV reported. No ruling on an appeal was found in searches carried out in September 2026. The case also drew national political attention because of the defendant's immigration status.

summary: Eleven-year-old Audrii Cunningham of Livingston, Texas, disappeared on February 15, 2024, after failing to board her school bus. Her body was recovered from the Trinity River five days later. Don Steven McDougal, a family friend who lived in a camper behind her home, pleaded guilty to capital murder on January 17, 2025, and was sentenced to life in prison without parole.

narrative: Audrii Cunningham was an 11-year-old girl from the Livingston area of Polk County, Texas. On the morning of Thursday, February 15, 2024, she left home for school but did not board the bus at her neighborhood stop, and school officials reported that she never arrived, according to CBS News Texas. An AMBER Alert was issued the same day.

Investigators quickly focused on Don Steven McDougal, then 42, whom news reports described as a friend of the family. According to CBS News Texas and FOX 26 Houston, he lived in a camper behind the home Audrii shared with her father and grandmother, and he sometimes drove her to school or to the bus stop. McDougal was arrested on February 16, 2024, on an unrelated aggravated assault charge, and authorities publicly described him as a person of interest. Witnesses had linked his dark blue 2003 Chevrolet Suburban to the case, CBS News Texas reported.

On February 20, 2024, Polk County Sheriff Byron Lyons announced that Audrii's body had been found in the Trinity River near US Highway 59. Officials said that cellphone analysis, video footage and information provided by McDougal had led searchers to several locations of interest, one of which was where she was found. KWTX later reported that a large rock had been tied to her body with rope that matched rope from McDougal's vehicle. Her remains were sent to the Harris County medical examiner, which determined that she died of homicidal violence with blunt head trauma, according to FOX 26 Houston and KPRC.

At the February 20 news conference, Polk County District Attorney Shelly Sitton said an arrest warrant for capital murder was being prepared. According to KPRC, a grand jury indicted McDougal in April 2024 on two counts of capital murder.

On Friday, January 17, 2025, McDougal pleaded guilty to capital murder at a special hearing at the Polk County Judicial Center and was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. KPRC reported that he pleaded to the second count of the indictment, that the state abandoned the first count, and that four other pending cases against him were dismissed as part of the agreement. Bluebonnet News reported that the agreement also waived his right to appeal. Members of Audrii's family, including her father and grandparents, gave victim impact statements in court.

The district attorney's office said it did not seek the death penalty because a review of McDougal's records showed significant documented intellectual and developmental disabilities, which under Texas law restrict eligibility for capital punishment. The district attorney said the plea spared the family a prolonged trial and appeals process. FOX 26 Houston also reported that McDougal had an earlier conviction for enticing a child but had not been required to register as a sex offender because of the terms of a plea agreement in that case.

narrative: Ruby Garcia, 25, was killed on March 22, 2024, in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Her body was found beside southbound US-131 near Leonard Street NW, according to WWMT. The station reported that she had been shot four times, twice in the head, once in the hand and once in the upper arm.

The man responsible was her boyfriend, Brandon Ortiz-Vite, also 25. According to WWMT's account of the court record, the shooting happened in Garcia's car after the two had been talking about their relationship. He pulled her from the vehicle, shot her again and drove away, later leaving the car in South Haven. On March 24 he called Allegan County Central Dispatch and confessed, and he was arrested. NewsNation reported that he initially faced five charges, including felony murder and carjacking.

Ortiz-Vite was a Mexican national who was in the United States without legal status. ABC News reported that, according to immigration authorities, he had been brought into the country as a child, had previously been deported and had re-entered at an unknown date and place. WWMT reported that he told investigators he was afraid of police involvement because of his immigration status.

The case drew national political attention. At a campaign event in Grand Rapids on April 2, 2024, former President Donald Trump spoke about Garcia's death in remarks on immigration and said he had spoken with some of her family. Her sister, Mavi Garcia, who acted as the family's spokesperson, told reporters that he had not spoken with her or her immediate family. According to NewsNation, she said the family was upset that the death was being treated as a political matter and that attention should be on her sister.

On September 23, 2024, Ortiz-Vite pleaded guilty in Kent County Circuit Court to second-degree murder, felony firearm, carrying a concealed weapon and carjacking, WWMT reported. In exchange, prosecutors dropped a first-degree murder charge, which would have carried life in prison without parole.

Judge Mark A. Trusock sentenced him on November 7, 2024, to 37 to 100 years for the murder and two years for the firearm offense, which means he must serve at least 39 years. The judge told him the killing was intentional and called him a danger to society. Ortiz-Vite addressed the Garcia family in court and acknowledged that his words would mean little to them. Kent County Prosecutor Christopher Becker said Ortiz-Vite would face deportation to Mexico after serving his sentence, WWMT reported.

narrative: Elijah Vue was three years old when he was reported missing on February 20, 2024, from an apartment in Two Rivers, in Manitowoc County, Wisconsin. According to WBAY and Fox 11, the report was made by Jesse Vang, the boyfriend of Elijah's mother, Katrina Baur, in whose care the boy was staying. An Amber Alert was issued the same day.

name: King Von
summary: Chicago rapper King Von (Dayvon Bennett), 26, was fatally shot outside the Monaco Hookah Lounge in Atlanta on November 6, 2020, when an argument between two groups turned into a gunfight. Timothy Leeks was charged with felony murder, but the case was dismissed before indictment, his attorney confirmed in August 2023. No one has been convicted of the killing.

narrative: Dayvon Bennett, who performed as King Von, was a 26-year-old rapper from Chicago. In the early hours of Friday, November 6, 2020, he and a group of men left the Opium nightclub in Atlanta and went to the Monaco Hookah Lounge at 255 Trinity Avenue, according to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation.

The GBI said two men approached the group in the parking lot, an argument began and it quickly turned into an exchange of gunfire between the two sides. Music outlets including XXL reported that the other group included the rapper Quando Rondo and Timothy Leeks. Atlanta police officers intervened, among them officers working off duty as security at the lounge. The GBI stated that two officers, one on duty and one off duty, fired their weapons and that no officer was hurt.

Six people were shot. Bennett and Mark Blakely, 34, also of Chicago, died. The GBI at first announced three deaths and corrected the figure to two on November 9, 2020. Because officers had fired, the GBI investigated the police use of force while the Atlanta Police Department handled the homicide inquiry, and the GBI said its findings would go to the Fulton County District Attorney. The Atlanta Police Department said its investigators believed Bennett was shot during the initial exchange between the two groups, before officers responded, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

Atlanta police charged Timothy Leeks, then 22, with felony murder in Bennett's death. Leeks had himself been wounded in the shooting. The Journal-Constitution reported on November 13, 2020, that two other men had been arrested on separate charges arising from the shootout, one for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon and one for aggravated assault. Neither was charged with killing Bennett.

Leeks was never indicted. On August 20, 2023, his attorney, Noah Pines, confirmed that the case against him had been dismissed before any indictment was returned, Revolt and XXL reported. Wikipedia and music-press reports attribute the dismissal to Georgia's stand-your-ground self-defence law. Members of Bennett's family publicly objected and said prosecutors had not informed them beforehand, according to XXL.

No one has been convicted of killing Bennett, and Leeks is legally presumed innocent of the dismissed charge. Bennett was buried near Chicago in November 2020. Wikipedia notes that in October 2024 federal prosecutors charged the rapper Lil Durk with a murder-for-hire conspiracy that they allege was aimed at Quando Rondo in retaliation for Bennett's death. Those are allegations in a separate case and not findings about the 2020 shooting.

narrative: Jahseh Onfroy, who performed as XXXTentacion, was a 20-year-old rapper from South Florida whose music had reached the Billboard charts. On the afternoon of June 18, 2018, he visited RIVA Motorsports, a motorcycle dealership in Deerfield Beach, north of Fort Lauderdale. According to CBS Miami, he was carrying a Louis Vuitton bag holding 50,000 dollars in cash that he had withdrawn from a bank.

As he drove out of the dealership in his BMW, a Dodge Journey SUV cut in front of his car and blocked it, WPLG Local 10 reported. Two masked men got out, confronted him at the driver's window, took the bag and shot him several times before the SUV drove away. Wikipedia's account, based on Broward Sheriff's Office statements, puts the shooting shortly before 4 p.m. and says he was pronounced dead at a hospital less than an hour later.

The Broward Sheriff's Office made four arrests over the following weeks. NBC News reported that Dedrick Williams, 22, was arrested within days of the shooting and that Michael Boatwright, 22, already in jail on an unrelated drug charge, was served with a murder warrant on July 11, 2018. Robert Allen and Trayvon Newsome were arrested later that summer, according to Wikipedia. A grand jury indicted the four men in July 2018.

The case took nearly five years to reach trial, delayed in part by the COVID-19 pandemic and pretrial disputes, CBS Miami reported. In 2022 Allen pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and agreed to testify for the prosecution. Jury selection for the other three began in Fort Lauderdale in January 2023. Prosecutors relied on surveillance video from the dealership, cellphone data, a fingerprint on the victim's car door attributed to Boatwright, and photographs of the defendants with large amounts of cash, according to CBS Miami. Investigators said Boatwright and Newsome were the masked men, that Williams drove the SUV and that Allen was a passenger, Local 10 reported.

After more than a week of deliberations, the jury found Boatwright, Williams and Newsome guilty of first-degree murder and armed robbery on March 20, 2023. On April 6, 2023, all three were sentenced to life in prison; the death penalty had not been sought. Relatives and the rapper's manager addressed the court at sentencing.

According to Wikipedia, Allen was sentenced in May 2023 to seven years in prison followed by 20 years of probation and, with credit for time served, was released in October 2023. Local 10 reported at sentencing that the three convicted men were expected to appeal; no ruling overturning the convictions was found in the sources reviewed.

narrative: Bashar Barakah Jackson, the Brooklyn rapper who performed as Pop Smoke, was 20 when he was shot during a break-in at a short-term rental house in the Hollywood Hills area of Los Angeles on February 19, 2020. According to CBS News, several people entered the house in the early morning, at least one of them carrying a handgun, and the emergency call was placed by someone on the East Coast who had been contacted from inside the house. Courthouse News Service reported that the group is alleged to have found the house through social media posts that revealed where Jackson was staying. By the time the case concluded, local outlets described Walker, who was 19 at the time of the killing, as the only defendant prosecuted as an adult, with three co-defendants dealt with in juvenile court. narrative: Adolph Thornton Jr., who performed as Young Dolph, was a Memphis rapper and independent label owner known locally for his charity work, according to CBS News. On November 17, 2021, he was at Makeda's Homemade Butter Cookies in South Memphis when two men got out of a white Mercedes-Benz and opened fire. CBS News reported that he was hit about 20 times and died at the age of 36, and that he was in the city to hand out Thanksgiving turkeys. His brother was present during the shooting, according to the Shelby County District Attorney's office.

The Mercedes had been taken in a carjacking a week earlier and was found on November 20, WLBT reported. Cornelius Smith was arrested in Southaven, Mississippi, on December 9, 2021, on an auto-theft warrant tied to that car, and a grand jury indicted him for first-degree murder on January 11, 2022. The same day, U.S. Marshals task forces arrested Justin Johnson, then 23, in Indiana after a search that included a reward offer.

Johnson went on trial in Memphis in September 2024. Smith testified for the prosecution and admitted his own role as one of the two gunmen. On September 26, 2024, the jury found Johnson guilty of first-degree murder, conspiracy and a firearms offence, and he was sentenced to life in prison. On November 1, 2024, Judge Jennifer Mitchell added 35 years for the conspiracy count, with a concurrent 15 years for the firearm count, Action News 5 reported. The District Attorney's office has said his appeal was denied.

Prosecutors alleged that a third man, Hernandez Govan, had directed the two shooters. A Memphis jury found him not guilty of first-degree murder and conspiracy on August 21, 2025, after about three hours of deliberation, according to CBS News. Prosecution testimony in the trials described the killing as arising from a feud between rival record labels; no one else has been convicted of ordering it.

On May 15, 2026, Smith pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 20 years without eligibility for parole or early release. The remaining counts against him were dropped as part of the agreement. District Attorney Steve Mulroy said the outcome reflected both the seriousness of the crime and Smith's cooperation. Smith was the last defendant with pending charges, which brought the prosecution to a close.

name: Paul Bernardo & Karla Homolka Victims
summary: Paul Bernardo and Karla Homolka, the 'Ken and Barbie Killers,' raped and murdered teenagers Leslie Mahaffy and Kristen French in Ontario. Homolka received a controversial plea deal.
lastSeen: Various dates, St. Catharines/Burlington, Ontario, Canada

sources.title: Paul Bernardo - Wikipedia
Bernardo case - Toronto Star (archived copy)

narrative: Paul Bernardo and his wife Karla Homolka kidnapped, raped, and murdered at least two teenage girls in southern Ontario between 1991 and 1992. Their victims were Leslie Mahaffy (14) and Kristen French (15).
The couple also drugged and sexually assaulted Karla's younger sister Tammy Homolka in December 1990; Tammy died from the effects of the drugs administered to sedate her.
Bernardo had also been the 'Scarborough Rapist,' committing at least 13 sexual assaults before the murders. He videotaped the torture and murder of the victims.

Homolka received a controversial plea deal—12 years for manslaughter in exchange for testimony against Bernardo—before the videotapes revealing her active participation were discovered. Bernardo was sentenced to life with no parole for 25 years. Homolka was released in 2005.

name: Clifford Olson Victims
summary: Clifford Olson murdered 11 children and young people, aged 9 to 18, in the Greater Vancouver area of British Columbia between November 1980 and July 1981. Arrested on August 12, 1981, he pleaded guilty in January 1982 and was sentenced to life in prison. Police paid $100,000 into a trust for his family in return for his leading them to victims' remains. He died in custody in 2011.
lastSeen: November 17, 1980 to July 30, 1981, Greater Vancouver and the Lower Mainland, British Columbia, Canada

sources.title: Global News / The Canadian Press - Small sketches of Olson's 11 victims
CBC News In Depth (archived) - Clifford Olson: The Beast of British Columbia
CTV News (archived) - Notorious serial killer Clifford Olson dies
The Globe and Mail - One family's story: How Olson's murders prompted changes to victim rights
CBC News - Clifford Olson 'will kill again' if freed, parole board says in ruling
Wikipedia - Clifford Olson

narrative: Between November 1980 and July 1981, eleven children and young people were abducted and killed in the Greater Vancouver area and the Lower Mainland of British Columbia. According to the Globe and Mail, the victims were Christine Weller, 12; Colleen Daignault, 13; Daryn Johnsrude, 16; Sandra Wolfsteiner, 16; Ada Court, 13; Simon Partington, 9; Judy Kozma, 14; Raymond King, 15; Sigrun Arnd, 18, a visitor from Germany; Terri Lyn Carson, 15; and Louise Chartrand, 17.

A Canadian Press summary published by Global News records that Christine Weller disappeared on November 17, 1980, while riding her bicycle home in Surrey, and that her body was found in Richmond on Christmas Day. No further victims are recorded until April 1981, when Colleen Daignault and Daryn Johnsrude disappeared within days of each other. Six of the eleven were taken in July 1981, the last of them, Louise Chartrand, on July 30. CBC News reported that several victims were lured with the offer of a job.

Families later said that early reports were not taken seriously. The Globe and Mail reported that Daryn Johnsrude's parents were told he was probably a runaway, and the Canadian Press noted that police had classed earlier disappearances as runaways before acknowledging foul play in the case of nine-year-old Simon Partington.

Clifford Olson, a Coquitlam resident who had spent most of his adult life in prison, was already under suspicion. According to CTV News, he was arrested on August 12, 1981, on Vancouver Island after a surveillance team saw him pick up two young hitchhikers. He was charged with the murder of Judy Kozma. He then reached an agreement with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police under which $100,000 was paid into a trust for his wife and son in return for his leading investigators to the remains of victims, CBC News reported. The Globe and Mail reported that families learned of the arrangement only after the court case, when the prosecutor disclosed it.

In January 1982 Olson pleaded guilty to eleven counts of murder and was sentenced to life imprisonment. Because the trial ended with the plea, much of the evidence was never made public, according to CTV News. A jury rejected his application for early parole eligibility in 1997, and the National Parole Board refused him parole in July 2006, stating that he presented a high risk. He was refused again in 2010.

The case had lasting effects on Canadian law and practice. Relatives of Daryn Johnsrude founded the group Victims of Violence, and the case contributed to restrictions on, and later repeal of, the so-called faint hope clause. Olson died of cancer on September 30, 2011, aged 71, in a Quebec hospital while still in custody.

name: Annecy Knife Attack
summary: A man stabbed six people, including four toddlers, at a lakeside playground in Annecy, France, in June 2023. All survived. The suspect, Abdalmasih Hanoun, a Syrian refugee who had been living in Sweden, was charged with attempted murder and in June 2026 was ordered to stand trial before an assize court; he has not yet been tried.

narrative: On June 8, 2023, a man attacked people with a knife at the Paquier gardens playground in Annecy, a lakeside town in the French Alps. He stabbed four toddlers in strollers and two adults.
The children, aged between 22 and 36 months, suffered serious injuries including one who was stabbed in the chest. Bystanders, including a Catholic pilgrim named Henri, tackled the attacker.

The suspect was identified as Abdalmasih H., a 31-year-old Syrian refugee who had been granted asylum in Sweden. French psychiatric experts later found his judgment was impaired but that he remains criminally responsible.
All six victims survived. The attack shocked France and was described by President Macron as 'absolute cowardice.' The attacker was charged with attempted murder.

name: Pedro López (Monster of the Andes)
summary: Colombian-born Pedro Alonso López was arrested in Ambato, Ecuador in 1980 and confessed to killing several hundred girls in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. He was convicted in Ecuador and given the 16-year maximum sentence, was released in 1994 and sent to Colombia, where he was held in psychiatric custody until 1998. He was last confirmed seen in Bogotá in September 1999.
lastSeen: September 22, 1999, Bogotá, Colombia (last confirmed sighting of López)

sources.title: El Tiempo - Quedaría libre el Monstruo de los Andes (March 12, 1994)
El Tiempo - Pedro Alonso López fue trasladado ayer al Espinal (September 6, 1994)
El Tiempo - Pedro Alonso López: el misterio por paradero del peor asesino en serie
El Telégrafo - El paso del Monstruo de los Andes aún lastima
Deseret News - 'Monster of the Andes' to soon go free (March 22, 1992)
Infobae - El Monstruo de los Andes (August 29, 2021)
Infobae - La misteriosa desaparición del mayor asesino serial de niñas de Colombia (November 14, 2018)
Wikipedia - Pedro López (serial killer)

narrative: Pedro Alonso López was born in 1948 in the Tolima department of Colombia. According to El Tiempo, he was first imprisoned in Bogotá in 1969 for car theft and was released in 1978. In the years that followed he moved between Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, and news accounts say he targeted young girls, many from poor and indigenous families, whom he approached in markets and lured away with small gifts or coins.

He was arrested in 1980 in Ambato, Ecuador. Accounts of the arrest differ in detail, but El Telégrafo, Infobae and the Deseret News all describe him being seized at or near a market after trying to take a girl, with the child's mother and bystanders intervening. Infobae reports that flooding in Ambato had recently exposed the buried bodies of girls who had been reported missing.

In custody López confessed to Ecuadorian police. El Telégrafo reports that he admitted raping and killing more than 300 girls aged roughly 8 to 13 across the three countries; a 1994 El Tiempo report put the figure at more than 100 girls in Ecuador plus dozens in Colombia. News reports say he led investigators to graves in the Ambato area, with the number of bodies recovered given as 53 by the Deseret News and more than 60 by El Tiempo. The totals he claimed were never established in court, and El Tiempo reported in 1994 that in prison he had begun describing himself as only an accomplice.

An Ecuadorian court gave him 16 years, which was the maximum sentence available in the country at the time. Sources disagree on the number of killings covered by the conviction: Wikipedia states he was found guilty of three murders in January 1981 after being charged with 57, while other outlets cite 57 or 110. With reductions for good behavior he was released in 1994 and handed over to Colombia.

El Tiempo reported on September 6, 1994 that López had been taken to El Espinal, Tolima, to answer accusations concerning the rape and murder of children there some 14 years earlier, and that a courthouse fire had destroyed much of the original file. He was then held in a psychiatric facility. According to El Tiempo and Infobae, he was declared mentally sound in 1998 and released on a small bail payment with a requirement to report to the authorities.

He did not remain in contact. El Tiempo reports that the last confirmed sighting was on September 22, 1999, when he renewed his identity card in Bogotá, and that an Interpol alert was issued in 2002 in connection with another child's death. His identity document was cancelled in 2005, but records conflict as to whether he died. As of the most recent reports located, his whereabouts are unknown.

He is declared mentally sound and released on bail.
Last confirmed sighting, when he renews his identity card in Bogotá.
An Interpol alert is issued for López in connection with another child's death.

name: Tsutomu Miyazaki Victims
summary: Tsutomu Miyazaki, the 'Otaku Killer,' murdered four young girls in the Tokyo/Saitama area. He kept body parts as trophies and sent taunting letters to families. He was executed in 2008.
lastSeen: 1988-1989, Saitama Prefecture, Japan

sources.title: Tsutomu Miyazaki - Wikipedia

narrative: Between August 1988 and June 1989, Tsutomu Miyazaki kidnapped and murdered four girls aged 4 to 7 in the Saitama Prefecture and Tokyo areas of Japan.

Miyazaki committed acts of necrophilia, mutilated the bodies, and kept body parts as trophies. He sent taunting postcards to the families of victims, including bone fragments of one girl sent to her family.

He was caught on July 23, 1989 while attempting to photograph a young girl. Police found over 5,000 videotapes in his home, many containing anime and horror films, leading to the derogatory label 'Otaku Killer.'
Miyazaki was convicted of four murders and sentenced to death. He was executed by hanging on June 17, 2008. The case created lasting stigma against otaku culture in Japan.

name: Casey White (murder conviction)
summary: Connie Ridgeway, 59, was found stabbed to death in her Lauderdale County, Alabama apartment in October 2015. Inmate Casey White confessed in 2020 and was charged with capital murder, but he later recanted and pleaded not guilty, and in 2023 prosecutors shelved the case shortly before trial without a conviction. White, who escaped from jail in 2022 with corrections officer Vicky White, is serving a 75-year sentence and a life sentence for unrelated crimes and the escape; Ridgeway's murder remains unsolved.
lastSeen: 2015, Lauderdale County, Alabama

sources.title: Fox News - Original murder case dropped against inmate whose escape left jail guard accomplice dead
Wikipedia - Casey White prison escape

narrative: Connie Ridgeway, 58, was found stabbed to death in her Lauderdale County, Alabama apartment on October 23, 2015. The case went cold for several years.
In 2020, while Casey White was serving a 75-year sentence for other crimes, he confessed to an inmate that he had killed Ridgeway as a murder-for-hire. He was charged with capital murder.

While awaiting trial for Ridgeway's murder, White engineered an escape from jail with the help of corrections officer Vicky White in April 2022. They were fugitives for 11 days before being caught in Indiana.

White later recanted the confession and pleaded not guilty. In 2023, shortly before the capital murder trial was due to start, prosecutors shelved the case, noting he is expected to die in prison on his other sentences; he has not been convicted of Ridgeway's murder, and her son has said he doubts the confession.

name: Alex Batty (found)
summary: Alex Batty of Oldham, England, was 11 when he failed to return from a holiday in Spain with his mother and grandfather in October 2017. He was found alive on December 13, 2023, walking on a road in south-western France, and returned to the UK three days later. Greater Manchester Police opened an investigation into alleged child abduction but closed it in 2025 without charges.
lastSeen: October 8, 2017, Port of Malaga, Spain

sources.title: BBC News - Who is Alex Batty and how was he found?
BBC News - Alex Batty: Police launch abduction investigation into disappearance of British teen
BBC News - Alex Batty case: Mum and grandfather wanted over 'abduction'
The Guardian - Alex Batty back in UK six years after vanishing on holiday in Spain
Wikipedia - Disappearance of Alex Batty

narrative: Alex Batty grew up in Oldham, Greater Manchester, where his maternal grandmother, Susan Caruana, was his legal guardian. According to the BBC, his mother, Melanie Batty, and his grandfather, David Batty, took him on a pre-arranged holiday to Marbella, Spain, leaving on September 30, 2017. Neither of them had legal guardianship of the boy, who was 11 at the time.

The three were expected back in the United Kingdom on October 8, 2017. They did not return, and Alex was last seen that day at the Port of Malaga. Greater Manchester Police treated the case as an alleged abduction and, in February 2018, said the two adults were wanted in connection with it. Caruana told the BBC she had received a video message in which her daughter explained her reasons, and said the family disagreed about schooling and lifestyle. Police said one line of inquiry was that the group had crossed to Morocco, where Caruana said they had stayed in a commune in 2014.

An international appeal produced no trace of the boy for six years. Alex later described an itinerant existence in communes, caravans and remote houses in Spain and then in the foothills of the French Pyrenees, without formal schooling, the BBC reported. He told The Sun that the early years felt like a holiday but that from about the age of 14 he was doing construction and renovation work, and that he decided he wanted to go back to England.

In the early hours of December 13, 2023, delivery driver Fabien Accidini saw a teenager walking along an unlit road in the rain and offered him a lift. According to Wikipedia, this was between Camon and Chalabre, and Accidini took him to the gendarmerie at Revel, near Toulouse. Alex, then 17, identified himself and sent a message to his grandmother. He initially said he had walked for four days; he later told The Sun the journey took two days and that he had altered details to protect his mother and grandfather.

Alex flew from Toulouse to the UK on December 16, 2023, and went to live with his grandmother, The Guardian and the BBC reported. On December 22, Greater Manchester Police confirmed that they had interviewed him and begun a criminal investigation into alleged child abduction.

In 2025 the force closed that investigation. According to the BBC, police said the family did not support it and that there was no realistic prospect of a prosecution, and Alex had said throughout that he did not want charges brought. Neither Melanie Batty nor David Batty was charged. In May 2026 the BBC broadcast a documentary in which Alex, by then 20, retraced his route.

Police close the investigation without charges.
The BBC broadcasts the documentary Kidnapped by My Mum.

name: Nicola Bulley
summary: Nicola Bulley vanished while walking her dog by the River Wyre in Lancashire, England. Her body was found in the river three weeks later. The case drew massive attention and amateur sleuthing.
lastSeen: January 27, 2023, River Wyre, St Michael's on Wyre, Lancashire, England

sources.title: Disappearance of Nicola Bulley - Wikipedia

narrative: On January 27, 2023, Nicola Bulley, 45, a mortgage adviser and mother of two, vanished while walking her dog along the River Wyre in St Michael's on Wyre, Lancashire. Her phone was found on a bench, still connected to a work call.
The case generated enormous media coverage and attracted 'armchair detectives' who traveled to the area, filmed residents, and promoted conspiracy theories about her disappearance.

Lancashire Police controversially disclosed that Bulley had struggled with alcohol and the menopause, drawing criticism. The Information Commissioner took no enforcement action and the IOPC found no misconduct, but a November 2023 College of Policing review criticised the disclosure and the force's media handling.

Nicola's body was found in the River Wyre on February 19, about a mile from where she disappeared. The coroner ruled her death was accidental—she had fallen into the river. The case prompted debate about social media speculation and police transparency.

name: Holly Wells & Jessica Chapman
summary: Ten-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman were murdered by school caretaker Ian Huntley in Soham, Cambridgeshire, in August 2002. Huntley was convicted in December 2003 and given a 40-year minimum term; he died in March 2026 after an attack in prison. The case led to major reforms in criminal record checks for people working with children.
lastSeen: August 4, 2002, Soham, Cambridgeshire, England

sources.title: Soham murders - Wikipedia
Wikipedia - Ian Huntley

narrative: On August 4, 2002, ten-year-old best friends Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman disappeared from a family barbecue in Soham, Cambridgeshire. They were last seen walking past the home of Ian Huntley, the caretaker at their school.
Huntley, 28, publicly appealed for information and gave media interviews while secretly knowing the girls were dead. His girlfriend Maxine Carr provided him with a false alibi.
Huntley had lured the girls into his house and murdered them. Their bodies were found two weeks later in a ditch near RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk.

Huntley was convicted of two counts of murder and sentenced to a minimum of 40 years. The Bichard Inquiry that followed revealed that Huntley had previous allegations of sexual offenses that were never properly recorded, leading to the creation of the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check system.

name: Moors Murders Victims
summary: Ian Brady and Myra Hindley killed five children and teenagers in the Manchester area between July 1963 and October 1965, burying four of them on Saddleworth Moor. Both were jailed for life at Chester Assizes on May 6, 1966, and both died in custody. The body of 12-year-old Keith Bennett has never been found, and Greater Manchester Police say the search for him remains open.
lastSeen: July 1963 - October 1965, Manchester area, England

sources.title: BBC On This Day - 1966: Moors murderers jailed for life
The Guardian - Search ends for Moors murder victim Keith Bennett after no remains found
LBC - Search for Moors Murder victim Keith Bennett continuing 'outside of public view'
CBS News - Police investigating after human remains reportedly found in Moors murders case
BBC News - Ian Brady: How the Moors Murderer came to symbolise pure evil
Wikipedia - Moors murders

narrative: The Moors murders were a series of killings of children and teenagers carried out by Ian Brady and Myra Hindley in and around Manchester, England, between July 1963 and October 1965. The five known victims were Pauline Reade, 16, who disappeared on July 12, 1963; John Kilbride, 12, taken from a market in Ashton-under-Lyne on November 23, 1963; Keith Bennett, 12, who vanished on June 16, 1964, while walking to his grandmother's home in Chorlton-on-Medlock; Lesley Ann Downey, 10, abducted on December 26, 1964; and Edward Evans, 17, killed in October 1965.

According to the BBC's account of the case, the crimes came to light after Hindley's 17-year-old brother-in-law, David Smith, witnessed the killing of Edward Evans at the couple's house in Hattersley and went to the police. He also told officers that Brady had spoken of burying other victims on the moors. A left-luggage ticket found in Hindley's prayer book led detectives to a suitcase containing photographs and tape recordings, and a photograph of Hindley on the moor helped locate John Kilbride's grave. The bodies of Kilbride and Downey were recovered from Saddleworth Moor in October 1965.

The trial opened at Chester Assizes on April 19, 1966, before Mr Justice Fenton Atkinson; both defendants pleaded not guilty. On May 6, 1966, Brady was convicted of the murders of Evans, Downey and Kilbride and given three concurrent life sentences. Hindley was convicted of murdering Evans and Downey and received two concurrent life sentences; the BBC reported that she was found not guilty of murdering Kilbride. At that time Pauline Reade and Keith Bennett were still listed as missing.

Greater Manchester Police reopened the inquiry in the mid-1980s. According to LBC and the BBC, both Brady and Hindley admitted in 1987 to killing Reade and Bennett, and each was taken back to the moor separately to help with the search. Pauline Reade's remains were found in 1987. Neither offender was tried for those two murders. Hindley sought release several times, without success, and died in November 2002 aged 60. Brady spent his later decades at Ashworth high-security hospital and died in May 2017 aged 79.

Keith Bennett remains the only victim who has not been found. His mother, Winnie Johnson, campaigned for decades for information and died in 2012. In September 2022 police searched a site on Saddleworth Moor after an author reported finding what he believed were remains; The Guardian reported that the week-long search ended on October 7, 2022, with no evidence of human remains. After a 2025 BBC documentary, Greater Manchester Police said that visible searches had paused but that a team was still working on the case, according to LBC.

Ian Brady dies at Ashworth Hospital aged 79.
Greater Manchester Police end a week-long search of Saddleworth Moor, having found no evidence of human remains.

name: Fred & Rose West Victims
summary: In February and March 1994, police found the remains of nine young women and girls at 25 Cromwell Street, Gloucester, the home of Fred and Rose West; three more victims were found elsewhere. Fred West, charged with 12 murders, died in custody on January 1, 1995, before trial. Rose West was convicted of 10 murders at Winchester Crown Court in November 1995 and is serving a whole-life sentence.
lastSeen: 1967-1987, Gloucester area, England

sources.title: UPI Archives - British jury convicts West of 10 murders
Crime+Investigation UK - Rosemary West: The Trial
LBC - Fred West: No remains found in cellar search for Mary Bastholm
Wikipedia - Fred West
Wikipedia - Rose West

narrative: Between 1967 and 1987, twelve girls and young women whose deaths were later attributed to Fred West, in most cases together with his wife Rose West, disappeared in and around Gloucester, England. The victims included lodgers at the couple's home, young women and teenagers who vanished while travelling or waiting for buses, and members of the Wests' own family.

According to Wikipedia's account, police obtained a warrant in February 1994 to search the garden of 25 Cromwell Street for the couple's daughter Heather, who had not been seen since June 1987, when she was 16. Fred West was arrested on February 24, 1994, and Heather's remains were found on February 26. Over the following days the remains of Shirley Robinson, 18, and Alison Chambers, 16, were also found in the garden, and in early March the remains of Lynda Gough, Carol Ann Cooper, Lucy Partington, Therese Siegenthaler, Shirley Hubbard and Juanita Mott were recovered from the cellar. Those six had disappeared between 1973 and 1975.

Three further victims were found away from Cromwell Street, according to the same account: Charmaine West, Fred West's eight-year-old stepdaughter, at the couple's former home at 25 Midland Road, Gloucester; and his first wife, Catherine 'Rena' West, and Anne McFall, 18, in fields near Much Marcle in Herefordshire.

Fred West was charged with 12 murders. He was found dead in his cell at a Birmingham prison on January 1, 1995, while on remand; UPI reported at the time that he had apparently hanged himself. He was never tried.

Rose West's trial began on October 3, 1995, at Winchester Crown Court. She denied the charges. UPI reported that the jury convicted her on November 21 of murdering Charmaine West, Heather West and Shirley Robinson, and on November 22 of the seven remaining counts. The judge, Mr Justice Mantell, imposed a life sentence on each count and said that in his view she should never be released. According to Crime+Investigation UK, her appeal was rejected in 1996 and she later abandoned further attempts. Wikipedia states that a whole-life tariff was subsequently set and that she continues to maintain her innocence. The house at 25 Cromwell Street was demolished in 1996 and replaced by a walkway.

Police have long considered whether Fred West was responsible for other disappearances, including that of Mary Bastholm, a 15-year-old who vanished in Gloucester in 1968. In May 2021, after a documentary production company reported possible evidence, Gloucestershire Police excavated the cellar of a Gloucester cafe. LBC reported that the force found no human remains or items of significance. Mary Bastholm remains missing, and no one was ever charged over her disappearance.

He was convicted in three separate trials between 2007 and 2009 and died in custody in Edinburgh on October 8, 2022, aged 76.

narrative: Peter Tobin was a Scottish sex offender who was convicted of three murders in three separate trials between 2007 and 2009. According to STV News, his victims were Angelika Kluk, a 23-year-old Polish student, Vicky Hamilton, a 15-year-old schoolgirl, and Dinah McNicol, an 18-year-old from Essex. Hamilton and McNicol both disappeared in 1991, and their fates were unknown for 16 years.

Kluk was living at St Patrick's Church in the Anderston area of Glasgow, where she also worked as a cleaner, in September 2006. Tobin was working there as a handyman. According to STV News, he raped and stabbed her and hid her body beneath the floor of the church, where police found it on September 29, 2006. Wikipedia's account, drawing on court reporting, says she was last seen alive on September 24. Tobin was tried at the High Court in Edinburgh and convicted in May 2007 of her rape and murder. He was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 21 years. STV reports that he had been released from prison in 2004 after serving part of a 14-year sentence for attacking two 14-year-old girls in Hampshire in 1993.

After that conviction, police examined where Tobin had lived in earlier decades. According to ABC News, which carried agency reporting from the trial, he had been living in Bathgate, West Lothian, when Vicky Hamilton vanished there in 1991. In November 2007 her remains were found at a house in Margate, Kent, that Tobin had occupied in the 1990s. The remains of Dinah McNicol, who disappeared in 1991 after hitchhiking in Hampshire, were found at the same property.

A jury at the High Court in Dundee convicted Tobin of Hamilton's murder in early December 2008 after a trial lasting about a month and less than three hours of deliberation, ABC News reported. The judge, Lord Emslie, set a minimum term of 30 years. In December 2009 a jury at Chelmsford Crown Court convicted him of McNicol's murder; according to Crime+Investigation UK, the trial lasted three days, the defence offered no evidence and the jury took 13 minutes. STV News describes him as serving a whole-life term at HMP Edinburgh.

Police set up a national inquiry, Operation Anagram, to establish whether Tobin was responsible for other crimes. David Swindle, the former detective superintendent who led it, told STV News that the team never established how many victims there were. According to Wikipedia, the operation was wound down in 2011 without further charges. Tobin was never convicted of any other killing.

Tobin died at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh on October 8, 2022, aged 76. According to the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service, he had fallen in his cell at HMP Edinburgh on September 8, 2022. Because he died in legal custody a Fatal Accident Inquiry was mandatory, and its determination was published in October 2024.

name: Josef Mengele (fugitive)
summary: Josef Mengele, an SS physician at Auschwitz from 1943 to 1945, fled Germany in 1949 and lived in Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil without ever being arrested. He died on February 7, 1979, after suffering a stroke while swimming at Bertioga, Brazil, and was buried under a false name. His remains were exhumed in June 1985 and identified by forensic experts; DNA testing confirmed the result in 1992.
lastSeen: February 7, 1979, Bertioga, São Paulo state, Brazil

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum - Josef Mengele
Jewish Virtual Library - Josef Mengele
History.com - Josef Mengele, known as the "Angel of Death," dies
Wikipedia - Josef Mengele

narrative: Josef Mengele was a German SS officer and physician who served at the Auschwitz camp complex in occupied Poland. According to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, he was assigned to Auschwitz on May 30, 1943, and in November 1943 became chief camp physician of Auschwitz II (Birkenau). Historical accounts describe him taking part in the selection of arriving prisoners and carrying out medical experiments on inmates, including studies of twins. He left the camp in January 1945 as Soviet forces approached.

After the war Mengele avoided prosecution. The museum's account states that he worked under a false name as a farmhand near Rosenheim in Bavaria until 1949, and that in July 1949 he emigrated to Argentina under an assumed identity with financial help from his family. He later obtained Argentine citizenship under the name José Mengele. A court in Freiburg, West Germany, issued a warrant for his arrest in 1959, and he moved to Paraguay that year after learning that prosecutors were looking for him. Around 1960 he relocated to Brazil and settled in the São Paulo area, where he lived under other names.

According to the Jewish Virtual Library's account, Mengele's health declined during the 1970s and he suffered a stroke in 1976. On February 7, 1979, while visiting friends at the coastal resort of Bertioga, he had another stroke while swimming and drowned. He was 67. He was buried in Embu das Artes under the name Wolfgang Gerhard, an identity he had been using for several years. His death was not made public, and reported sightings of him continued in various countries for years afterward.

In 1985 the governments of West Germany, Israel and the United States began a coordinated effort to find him. According to the Jewish Virtual Library, West German police searched the home of Hans Sedlmeier, a family friend and employee of the Mengele family firm in Günzburg, on May 31, 1985, and found correspondence that included a letter reporting Mengele's death. Brazilian police then questioned the couple who had hosted him in Bertioga, who disclosed the location of the grave. The remains were exhumed on June 6, 1985.

An international group of forensic specialists examined the skeleton and concluded with a high degree of probability that it was Mengele's. His son, Rolf Mengele, issued a statement days after the exhumation saying the body was his father's and that the family had kept the death secret. Some doubts were voiced publicly until DNA analysis in 1992 confirmed the identification.

Mengele was never arrested or tried. The museum notes that he evaded capture for 34 years. The case is recorded here as resolved because the fugitive's fate and identity were established after his death, not because any court ruled on his conduct.

DNA analysis confirms the identification.

name: Andrei Chikatilo Victims
summary: Andrei Chikatilo, a former schoolteacher, was found guilty by a court in Rostov-on-Don in October 1992 of murdering 52 women and children between 1978 and 1990 and was sentenced to death. His victims were killed across southern Russia, Ukraine and Uzbekistan. After President Boris Yeltsin rejected a clemency appeal, he was executed on February 14, 1994.
lastSeen: Various dates 1978-1990, mainly Rostov Oblast, Russia

sources.title: The Independent - Russian 'mad beast' who butchered 52 faces the firing squad
Los Angeles Times - 'I Was Like a Crazed Wolf' (trial report, April 28, 1992)
UPI Archives - Russian mass murderer executed
Wikipedia - Andrei Chikatilo

narrative: Between December 1978 and November 1990, dozens of women, teenagers and children were murdered in and around the Rostov region of southern Russia, with further killings in Ukraine and Uzbekistan. The man eventually held responsible was Andrei Chikatilo, a former schoolteacher and Communist Party member. According to the verdict reported by The Independent, the court found that he had killed 17 women, 21 boys and 14 girls. Many of the victims were approached at railway and bus stations and led into nearby woodland.

The Los Angeles Times reported during the trial that the crimes became known as the "Forest Strip" killings and prompted a very large manhunt, including blood tests of nearly 200,000 drivers and the questioning of tens of thousands of people. The same report said Chikatilo had been detained twice before his final arrest: once in 1978 after the first killing, and again in 1984, when a detective saw him approaching young women at a bus station and found rope, wire and a knife in his briefcase. He was released after authorities said his blood test did not match the killer's.

The investigation also produced a serious miscarriage of justice. According to the Los Angeles Times and The Independent, another man was convicted and executed for the murder of a nine-year-old girl whom Chikatilo later acknowledged as his first victim. Wikipedia identifies that victim as Yelena Zakotnova, killed in Shakhty in December 1978, and the executed man as Aleksandr Kravchenko.

Chikatilo was arrested on November 20, 1990, and confessed later that month, according to Wikipedia's account of the case. He went on trial in Rostov-on-Don in April 1992, charged with 53 murders, and was held in a metal cage in the courtroom throughout the proceedings. In mid-October 1992 the court, presided over by Judge Leonid Akubzhanov, found him guilty of 52 murders, and he was sentenced to death.

UPI reported that President Boris Yeltsin rejected Chikatilo's appeal for clemency and that he was executed on February 14, 1994, by a gunshot to the back of the neck in a prison near Rostov-on-Don. Wikipedia gives the place of execution as Novocherkassk.

This record is dated by the 1992 verdict rather than by the crimes themselves, which were committed over twelve years. The case is often cited for the failures of the original investigation, including the wrongful execution and the 1984 release of Chikatilo on the basis of a blood-type comparison.

name: Diane Downs Children
summary: Seven-year-old Cheryl Downs was shot dead and her siblings Christie, 8, and Danny, 3, were badly wounded on a rural road near Springfield, Oregon, on May 19, 1983. Their mother, Diane Downs, blamed a stranger who tried to take her car. A jury convicted her of murder, attempted murder and assault in June 1984. She has been denied parole repeatedly, most recently in December 2025.
lastSeen: May 19, 1983, Old Mohawk Road, near Springfield, Oregon

sources.title: UPI Archives - Jurors relieved at end of mother's trial

narrative: On the night of May 19, 1983, Diane Downs, a 27-year-old postal worker, arrived at a hospital in Springfield, Oregon, with her three children, all of whom had been shot. According to ABC News, seven-year-old Cheryl died, while eight-year-old Christie and three-year-old Danny survived with serious wounds. Downs had a gunshot wound to her left arm. Later reporting describes lasting injuries to both survivors: UPI reported at the time of the verdict that Christie was left with a speech impediment and limited use of one arm, and that Danny was paralysed.

Downs told police that a stranger with bushy hair had flagged her down on a rural road, demanded her car at gunpoint and opened fire on the children. Wikipedia's account, which draws on contemporary Oregon newspapers and Ann Rule's book, places the scene on Old Mohawk Road shortly before 10:30 pm. Investigators doubted the story. Inside Edition reported that authorities found her manner detached, that her account shifted, and that no blood spatter was found on the driver's side of the car.

Downs was arrested on February 28, 1984, nine months after the shooting, according to ABC News. Prosecutors argued that she wanted to be free of her children in order to pursue a relationship with a married man in Arizona who did not want children. A central part of the state's case was the testimony of Christie, who, Inside Edition reported, told the court that her mother stopped the car, took something from the trunk and shot the children.

UPI reported that the jury of nine women and three men returned guilty verdicts on June 17, 1984, after a 31-day trial and about 36 hours of deliberation. Downs was heavily pregnant at the time; the daughter she gave birth to shortly afterwards was placed for adoption, ABC News reported. ABC News gives her sentence as life plus 50 years. The two surviving children were adopted by the prosecutor who tried the case, according to the same report.

Downs escaped from the women's prison in Salem, Oregon, on July 11, 1987, and was recaptured on July 21, ABC News reported. The case became widely known through Ann Rule's 1987 book Small Sacrifices and a later television film.

Downs has always maintained that she is innocent. According to Wikipedia, her first parole hearing was held in December 2008 and later hearings followed, all ending in denial. KPTV reported that after a virtual hearing in October 2025 the Oregon parole board again refused release on December 16, 2025, finding that she has a mental or emotional disturbance that makes her a danger to others, and that she cannot petition again until 2031.

name: David Carrick Victims
summary: Former Metropolitan Police officer David Carrick admitted 49 offences, including 24 counts of rape, against 12 women between 2003 and 2020. On February 7, 2023, he received 36 life sentences with a minimum term of 30 years and 239 days. In November 2025 an Old Bailey jury convicted him of nine further offences against two more victims, and he was given another life sentence.
lastSeen: Offences between 2003 and 2020, mostly in Hertfordshire, England

narrative: David Carrick joined the Metropolitan Police in 2001 and, according to the sentencing remarks of Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb, moved in 2009 to the unit responsible for diplomatic protection, where he routinely carried a firearm. The BBC reported that he served with the Parliamentary and Diplomatic Protection Command and lived in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, where most of his offences took place.

According to the sentencing remarks, a woman reported on October 1, 2021, that Carrick had raped her, and he was arrested and charged on October 3, 2021. No evidence was ultimately offered on that particular count and a not guilty verdict was entered, but the judge noted that publicity about his arrest led other women to come forward. The BBC reported that he was suspended from duty after his arrest and that the investigation was led by the Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Major Crime Unit.

Carrick initially pleaded not guilty. The BBC reported that he admitted 43 charges in December 2022 and the remaining six at Southwark Crown Court on January 16, 2023, making 49 offences against 12 women, including 24 counts of rape, as well as false imprisonment, sexual assault and controlling and coercive behaviour. The offences were committed between 2003 and 2020. The judge said the charges represented at least 71 instances of sexual violence, and that he had referred to his job as a police officer when offending. The BBC reported that he met some of the women through dating sites.
On February 7, 2023, Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb imposed 36 life sentences and set a minimum term of 30 years and 239 days, after allowing a 20 percent reduction for the guilty pleas.

The Metropolitan Police apologised. The BBC reported that Carrick had come to the attention of police over nine incidents between 2000 and 2021, and quoted Assistant Commissioner Barbara Gray as saying the force had missed opportunities to remove him. In July 2023 the Independent Office for Police Conduct announced investigations into how reports made about Carrick in 2002, 2016, 2019 and 2021 had been handled, along with a separate investigation following a referral from Wiltshire Police.

After the 2023 sentencing two more people came forward. According to the Crown Prosecution Service, an Old Bailey jury in November 2025 found Carrick guilty of five counts of indecent assault against a girl who was 12 at the time, in 1989 and 1990, and of two counts of rape, one of sexual assault and one of controlling and coercive behaviour against a woman. Press reports state that the offences against the woman took place between 2014 and 2019 and that on November 20, 2025, Mrs Justice McGowan imposed a further life sentence with a minimum term of 30 years, to run concurrently. Carrick had denied those charges. The victims in both cases are protected by law from being identified.

name: John O'Keefe (Karen Read)
summary: Boston police officer John O'Keefe, 46, was found dead in the snow outside a home in Canton, Massachusetts, on January 29, 2022. His girlfriend Karen Read was charged with second-degree murder; her first trial ended in a mistrial in July 2024, and on June 18, 2025, a second jury acquitted her of murder, manslaughter and leaving the scene, convicting her only of operating under the influence, for which she received a year of probation. No one else has been charged in his death.
lastSeen: January 29, 2022, Canton, Norfolk County, Massachusetts

narrative: On January 29, 2022, Boston police officer John O'Keefe, 46, was found dead in the snow outside a house in Canton, Massachusetts. He had injuries to his head and arm.
His girlfriend Karen Read was charged with second-degree murder. Prosecutors alleged she struck O'Keefe with her SUV and left him to die in a snowstorm after a night of drinking.
Read's defense argued she was being framed by law enforcement and that O'Keefe was killed inside the house during an altercation, then moved outside. The theory gained massive public support.

Her first trial in 2024 ended in a mistrial after the jury deadlocked. At a second trial she was acquitted on June 18, 2025, of murder, manslaughter and leaving the scene, and convicted only of operating under the influence. The lead investigator, Michael Proctor, was fired in March 2025 over his conduct in the case.

name: Riley Strain
summary: University of Missouri senior Riley Strain disappeared on Nashville's Broadway after being kicked out of a bar. His body was found in the Cumberland River two weeks later. His death was ruled accidental drowning.

narrative: On March 8, 2024, Riley Strain, a 22-year-old University of Missouri senior, disappeared during a night out on Broadway in Nashville, Tennessee. He was asked to leave Luke Bryan's bar after appearing intoxicated.
CCTV footage tracked Strain walking toward the Cumberland River. His bank card and phone were found near the riverbank.
After a two-week search that drew national attention, Strain's body was found in the Cumberland River on March 22, about eight miles downstream from where he was last seen.
The medical examiner ruled his death an accidental drowning with acute alcohol intoxication as a contributing factor. The case highlighted the dangers of Nashville's riverside bar district.

name: Baby Victoria (daughter of Constance Marten & Mark Gordon)
summary: Newborn Victoria died in early 2023 while her parents, Constance Marten and Mark Gordon, were living in a tent on the South Downs to avoid social services. Her body was found in a shopping bag in a disused shed in Brighton two days after their arrest on February 27, 2023. Both parents were convicted of gross negligence manslaughter in July 2025 and sentenced to 14 years.
lastSeen: Seen alive on CCTV in January 2023; body found in a disused shed in Brighton, East Sussex, on March 1, 2023

narrative: Victoria was the fifth child of Constance Marten and Mark Gordon, who had been a couple since 2016. According to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), their four older children had been taken into care, and the couple went on the run in late December 2022, when Marten was heavily pregnant, in order to keep the new baby. Marten gave birth in secret. The CPS states that the exact dates of Victoria's birth and death are not known.

Police first learned that a baby existed on January 5, 2023, when a placenta wrapped in a towel was found in a car that had caught fire on the M61 motorway near Bolton, Greater Manchester. The couple left the scene, and a national appeal was launched. According to the CPS, they travelled long distances by taxi, avoided using bank cards and phones, and spent time near ports. From about January 8, 2023, they were living in a tent in the South Downs National Park in East Sussex in near-freezing conditions. Witnesses and CCTV showed the baby dressed only in a babygrow, the CPS said.

Marten and Gordon were arrested in Brighton on February 27, 2023, after about seven weeks of searching. According to the CPS, they did not answer questions about the baby. Two days later, Victoria's body was found in a shopping bag inside a disused shed in Brighton. Wikipedia's account, citing news coverage, dates the discovery to March 1, 2023, places it on an allotment in the Hollingdean area, and says the couple were charged on March 3, 2023.

At a first trial at the Old Bailey in 2024, the jury could not reach a verdict on manslaughter. The CPS states that both defendants were convicted at that trial of concealing the birth of a child, cruelty to a child and perverting the course of justice. The CPS sought a retrial and presented additional expert evidence on weather conditions and the risk of hypothermia from damp clothing and condensation in the tent. On July 14, 2025, the retrial jury found both guilty of gross negligence manslaughter, as reported by CBS News.

On September 15, 2025, Judge Mark Lucraft sentenced Marten to 14 years in prison and Gordon to 14 years with a four-year extended licence period, with shorter concurrent terms for the other offences, according to the CPS. CBS News and later press reports state that the judge concluded the baby died of hypothermia and rejected the parents' account that she died accidentally while Marten slept with her in the tent. Wikipedia notes that the cause of death could not be medically ascertained.

In August 2026, ITV News and the Telegraph reported that Marten had been granted permission to appeal against her sentence and had renewed an application for permission to appeal against her manslaughter conviction. No hearing date had been set at the time of those reports.

name: Lucy Letby Victims
summary: Neonatal nurse Lucy Letby was convicted of murdering seven babies and attempting to murder six others at the Countess of Chester Hospital. She received a whole-life order.
lastSeen: 2015-2016, Countess of Chester Hospital, Chester, England

sources.title: Lucy Letby - Wikipedia

narrative: Lucy Letby, a neonatal nurse at the Countess of Chester Hospital, was convicted in August 2023 of murdering seven babies and attempting to murder six others between June 2015 and June 2016.

Letby killed babies through methods including injecting air into their bloodstreams, poisoning them with insulin, overfeeding them with milk, and causing trauma. She targeted the most vulnerable premature infants.

Senior doctors had raised concerns about Letby in 2016 when they noticed a correlation between her shifts and unexplained baby deaths. Hospital management initially failed to act and ordered the doctors to apologize to Letby.

Letby was sentenced to a whole-life order—meaning she will never be released. The case led to a public inquiry (the Thirlwall Inquiry) into the hospital's failures. She was convicted of a further attempted murder at a retrial in 2024.

summary: Lukasz Slaboszewski, 31, John Chapman, 56, and Kevin Lee, 48, were stabbed to death in Peterborough, England, in March 2013 and their bodies left in ditches. Joanna Dennehy pleaded guilty to the three murders and to the attempted murder of two men in Hereford. On February 28, 2014, she received a whole-life order; three men were convicted of related offences.
lastSeen: March 2013, Peterborough, Cambridgeshire, England
