narrative: Three men were killed in Peterborough, Cambridgeshire, in March 2013: Lukasz Slaboszewski, 31, a Polish national; John Chapman, 56; and Kevin Lee, 48, a property developer and landlord. All three died of stab wounds, and their bodies were left in ditches in the countryside outside the city. The case became known as the Peterborough ditch murders.

According to Wikipedia's account, Slaboszewski was killed between March 19 and March 29, and Chapman and Lee were both killed on March 29. Lee's body was found on March 30 near Newborough. The bodies of Slaboszewski and Chapman were found on April 3 near Thorney. Heart radio's summary of the case describes Chapman as a Falklands veteran who shared a house with Joanna Dennehy, and says Slaboszewski had met her only days before he died.

After the killings, Dennehy travelled to Hereford, about 140 miles away, with Gary Stretch, also known as Gary Richards. There she stabbed two men who were out walking their dogs, Robin Bereza and John Rogers. Both survived. Wikinews reported that the second attack came within minutes of the first. Dennehy and Stretch were arrested shortly afterwards.

On November 18, 2013, Dennehy pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey in London to three counts of murder and two of attempted murder. NBC News reported that the plea surprised her own lawyers and that she refused their request for time to discuss it. Stretch, Leslie Layton and Robert Moore faced related charges. According to Wikipedia, a jury convicted Stretch of attempted murder and Layton of perverting the course of justice in February 2014, and Moore admitted assisting an offender.

All four were sentenced on February 28, 2014. Mr Justice Spencer gave Dennehy a life sentence with a whole-life order, meaning she is never to be released. Reports at the time said she was the third woman in the United Kingdom to be given such a term, after Myra Hindley and Rosemary West. Stretch received life with a minimum of 19 years, Layton 14 years and Moore three years, Wikinews reported. The judge said the murders were premeditated and referred to psychiatric evidence of a psychopathic personality disorder.

Wikipedia reports that a later review found Dennehy had been under probation supervision at the time of the killings. It also reports that she was held in segregation after an escape plan was discovered at HMP Bronzefield, and that the High Court rejected her legal challenge to that segregation.

narrative: On February 11, 2023, Brianna Ghey, a 16-year-old transgender girl, was stabbed 28 times in Culcheth Linear Park in Warrington, Cheshire. She died at the scene.
Her killers, Scarlett Jenkinson and Eddie Ratcliffe, both 15, had planned the attack for weeks. Messages between them showed they had discussed methods of killing and had targeted Brianna.
Jenkinson, who had an obsession with torture and serial killers, lured Brianna to the park where Ratcliffe stabbed her. They tried to cover their tracks by wiping their phones.

Both were convicted of murder on December 20, 2023, and sentenced on February 2, 2024. Jenkinson received a minimum term of 22 years and Ratcliffe 20 years. Brianna's mother Esther campaigned for stricter controls on children's social media access.

name: Richard Glossip (case)
summary: Motel owner Barry Van Treese was beaten to death at the Best Budget Inn in Oklahoma City in January 1997 by Justin Sneed, who testified that Richard Glossip put him up to it. Glossip was twice convicted and sentenced to death. The U.S. Supreme Court vacated his conviction on February 25, 2025. He was released on $500,000 bond in May 2026; a third trial is set for December 2026. He maintains his innocence.
lastSeen: January 1997, Best Budget Inn, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma (where Barry Van Treese was killed)

narrative: Barry Van Treese, the owner of the Best Budget Inn on the outskirts of Oklahoma City, was killed at the motel in January 1997. Justin Sneed, a 19-year-old maintenance worker there, admitted beating him to death with a baseball bat, according to The Intercept. Sneed said that Richard Glossip, who managed the motel, had pushed him to do it. Sneed's account became the basis of the state's case, and under a plea agreement he avoided the death penalty and is serving a life sentence. Prosecutors have never claimed that Glossip struck Van Treese himself, SCOTUSblog noted. Glossip has always denied any part in the killing.

Glossip was convicted and sentenced to death in 1998. The Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals overturned that conviction in 2001, finding that his lawyers had been ineffective, The Intercept reported. A second jury convicted him in 2004 and he was again sentenced to death. According to his attorney's statement quoted by The Intercept, he faced nine execution dates over the following years.

According to SCOTUSblog, Glossip returned to state court in 2023 after the state disclosed files indicating that prosecutors had known Sneed was prescribed lithium for bipolar disorder after his arrest and had allowed him to testify falsely about it. Two independent reports had questioned the conviction, and Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond supported Glossip's request to set it aside. The Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals refused, and the state parole board denied clemency.

On February 25, 2025, the U.S. Supreme Court reversed the state court and ordered a new trial. In an opinion by Justice Sonia Sotomayor, the court held that prosecutors had violated their duty under Napue v. Illinois to correct testimony they knew to be false, and that because Sneed's testimony was the only direct evidence of Glossip's guilt, the error could have affected the verdict, SCOTUSblog reported. The ruling did not decide whether Glossip is guilty or innocent.

In June 2025 Drummond announced that the state would try Glossip again for first-degree murder, The Intercept reported; News 9 reported that the state is not seeking the death penalty. District Judge Heather Coyle denied bond in July 2025 and later left the case. Glossip's lawyers argued that a 2023 email exchange with the attorney general amounted to a binding plea agreement, under which he would have pleaded guilty to accessory after the fact and been released; the state denied that any deal was reached, and on April 10, 2026, District Judge Natalie Mai declined to enforce it, according to News 9.

On May 14, 2026, Judge Mai set bond at $500,000, with electronic monitoring, a nightly curfew and a ban on leaving the state, and Glossip, then 63, left the Oklahoma County jail that afternoon, The Intercept reported. His trial was first set for September 2026. News 9 reported on July 28, 2026, that it had been moved, with jury selection scheduled for December 9, 2026, and the trial expected to last about three weeks.

name: Natalia Grace Barnett
summary: Michael and Kristine Barnett were charged in 2019 with neglecting their adopted daughter Natalia Grace, a Ukrainian-born girl with a rare form of dwarfism, after allegedly leaving her alone in a Lafayette, Indiana, apartment in 2013. A court had changed her legal birth year from 2003 to 1989 in 2012. A jury acquitted Michael Barnett in October 2022, and the case against Kristine Barnett was dismissed in March 2023.
lastSeen: Not a missing-person case; the alleged neglect occurred in 2013 at an apartment in Lafayette, Indiana

sources.title: WRTV - Michael Barnett acquitted on all charges following neglect trial
WRTV - Case against Kristine Barnett dismissed in Tippecanoe County

narrative: Natalia Grace was born in Ukraine and has diastrophic dysplasia, a rare form of dwarfism that affects bone growth, according to Today and ABC News (Australia). Her adoption paperwork listed her birth year as 2003. She was first adopted by a couple in New Hampshire in 2008 and was adopted again in 2010 by Kristine and Michael Barnett of Indiana.

The Barnetts came to assert that Natalia was an adult rather than a child. According to Today, a hospital examination in 2010 put her age at about eight and a skeletal survey in 2012 estimated it at about eleven. In 2012 the Barnetts nevertheless obtained an order from the Marion County probate court changing her birth year from 2003 to 1989, which made her legally 22, WRTV reported. ABC News reported that the change was granted without an evidentiary hearing and without anyone representing Natalia.

In 2013, according to Today, Natalia was placed in an apartment in Hamilton County and then in one in Tippecanoe County. Prosecutors alleged that the Barnetts rented the Lafayette apartment for her and left her there alone while they moved out of the country with their other children; several outlets report that the family went to Canada. Natalia later lived with Antwon and Cynthia Mans, who filed a guardianship petition in March 2016.

In September 2019 Tippecanoe County prosecutors charged Michael and Kristine Barnett, who had since divorced, with multiple counts of neglect of a dependent and conspiracy to commit neglect. Both denied wrongdoing and maintained that Natalia was an adult. WRTV reported that four of the counts against Michael Barnett were dismissed in February 2022. His trial began on October 24, 2022, and on October 27, 2022, a Tippecanoe County jury found him not guilty on all four remaining counts. News reports of the trial said jurors were not permitted to hear evidence about Natalia's age.

Kristine Barnett never stood trial. On March 24, 2023, a Tippecanoe County judge dismissed the case against her; WRTV reported that court documents cited insufficient evidence to prove the charges beyond a reasonable doubt. Her lawyer told the station that the charges should never have been filed. No one has been convicted of any offence in connection with Natalia's care.

The case drew wide attention through the Investigation Discovery documentary series The Curious Case of Natalia Grace and the 2025 drama Good American Family. According to Today and Time, a DNA-based test carried out in 2023 estimated Natalia's age at about 22, consistent with a 2003 birth year, and Time and ABC News report that her legal birth year was changed back to 2003. The Mans family adopted her in 2023, and by January 2025 she was living with Nicole and Vincent DePaul in New York, according to Today.

name: Halyna Hutchins (Rust trial)
summary: Cinematographer Halyna Hutchins, 42, was fatally shot on the set of the film Rust near Santa Fe on October 21, 2021, when a revolver held by actor Alec Baldwin fired a live round. Armorer Hannah Gutierrez-Reed was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in March 2024 and sentenced to 18 months. The charge against Baldwin was dismissed with prejudice on July 12, 2024, and the state dropped its appeal in December 2024.

narrative: Halyna Hutchins, a 42-year-old cinematographer, was fatally shot on October 21, 2021, on the set of the Western film Rust at Bonanza Creek Ranch near Santa Fe, New Mexico. Actor and producer Alec Baldwin was holding a replica Colt .45 revolver during a rehearsal when it fired a live round. The shot struck Hutchins and wounded the film's director, Joel Souza. According to Wikipedia's summary of the case, Hutchins was flown to University of New Mexico Hospital in Albuquerque, where she was pronounced dead, and Souza was treated and released.

Investigators focused on how live ammunition had reached a film set. Prosecutors alleged that the film's armorer, Hannah Gutierrez-Reed, was responsible for live rounds being present, Deadline reported. Baldwin and Gutierrez-Reed were each charged with involuntary manslaughter in January 2023. According to Wikipedia, assistant director David Halls pleaded no contest in March 2023 to negligent use of a deadly weapon and received six months of unsupervised probation. The charge against Baldwin was dropped in April 2023, and a grand jury indicted him again in January 2024.

Gutierrez-Reed was tried in Santa Fe in early 2024. NBC News reported that a jury found her guilty of involuntary manslaughter in March 2024 and not guilty of tampering with evidence. On April 15, 2024, she was sentenced to 18 months in prison, the maximum term for the offense.

Baldwin's trial began in July 2024. On July 12, the third day of trial, Judge Mary Marlowe Sommer dismissed the case with prejudice, which means the charge cannot be brought again. The judge found that the state had failed to give the defense a set of bullets that had been handed to the sheriff's office months earlier by a man who said they were connected to the case. TheWrap reported that she called the withholding intentional and deliberate and said it had affected the fundamental fairness of the proceedings. Baldwin had pleaded not guilty, and his lawyers argued that, as an actor, he was not responsible for firearm safety on the set.

Special prosecutor Kari Morrissey filed a notice of appeal but withdrew it in December 2024. According to Variety, the New Mexico attorney general's office had indicated that it would not fully pursue the appeal, citing the procedural problems the judge had identified. That ended the criminal case against Baldwin without a conviction.

Gutierrez-Reed was released on parole on May 23, 2025, after serving her sentence less credit for good behavior, Deadline reported, citing the New Mexico Corrections Department. Her parole conditions barred contact with the Hutchins family. Wikipedia reports that a wrongful-death claim by the Hutchins family against the production was settled in October 2022, and that Baldwin sued New Mexico officials in January 2025 over his prosecution. Rust was completed and released in May 2025.

narrative: On June 29, 2022, R&B singer R. Kelly (Robert Sylvester Kelly) was sentenced to 30 years in federal prison after his conviction on sex trafficking and racketeering charges.
Kelly had operated a criminal enterprise to recruit and sexually abuse women and underage girls for decades. His inner circle helped identify and groom victims.

In September 2022, Kelly was convicted in a separate Chicago federal trial of child pornography and enticement charges. In February 2023 he was sentenced to 20 years, of which all but one year runs concurrently with the New York sentence, for a combined term of 31 years.
The case was propelled by the 2019 documentary series 'Surviving R. Kelly.' Despite decades of allegations, Kelly had avoided accountability until the #MeToo movement shifted public sentiment.

name: Tyre Nichols
summary: Tyre Nichols, 29, died on January 10, 2023, three days after being beaten by Memphis police officers following a traffic stop. Former officers Desmond Mills Jr. and Emmitt Martin III pleaded guilty to federal and state charges. Tadarrius Bean, Demetrius Haley and Justin Smith were convicted on federal counts in October 2024, but a judge ordered a new federal trial for them in August 2025, and a state jury acquitted all three of all charges, including murder, in May 2025.
lastSeen: January 7, 2023, Memphis, Shelby County, Tennessee

narrative: On January 7, 2023, Tyre Nichols, a 29-year-old Black man, was stopped by Memphis police during a traffic stop. Officers pulled him from his car and attempted to detain him. Nichols ran.
Body camera footage showed five officers—all Black members of the SCORPION unit—punching, kicking, and beating Nichols with a baton after catching him near his home. He called out for his mother.
Nichols died three days later from his injuries. The footage, released on January 27, triggered nationwide protests. The SCORPION unit was permanently disbanded.

Five officers were fired and charged in both state and federal court. Desmond Mills Jr. and Emmitt Martin III pleaded guilty. In October 2024 a federal jury convicted Demetrius Haley of civil rights, conspiracy and obstruction counts, and convicted Tadarrius Bean and Justin Smith only of obstruction through witness tampering, acquitting them of the civil rights charges. In May 2025 a state jury acquitted Bean, Haley and Smith of all charges, and in August 2025 a federal judge ordered a new trial for the three.
